388.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
388.b: Descendant of Saul, had six sons
388.s: Azel, a descendant of Saul, had six sons: Azrikam, Bokeru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan (<ref="1Ch.8.37, 38; 9:43, 44">1Ch.8.37, 38; 9:43, 44</ref>).

389.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
389.b: Ancestor of exiles who returned to Jerusalem
389.s: Azgad was the ancestor of 1,222 (or 2,322) exiles who returned to Jerusalem (<ref="Ezr.2.12; 8:12; Neh.7.17">Ezr.2.12; 8:12; Neh.7.17</ref>).

390.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
390.b: Leader who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time
390.s: Azgad was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during the time of Nehemiah (<ref="Neh.10.15">Neh.10.15</ref>).

391.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
391.b: Descendant of Zattu, had married a foreign woman
391.s: Aziza, a descendant of Zattu, was one of the men who had married foreign women during the time of Ezra (<ref="Ezr.10.27">Ezr.10.27</ref>).

392.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
392.b: Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag
392.s: Azmaveth, a Benjamite warrior, was one of the men who joined David at Ziklag when he was fleeing from Saul (<ref="1Ch.12.3">1Ch.12.3</ref>).

393.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
393.b: Overseer of royal treasuries under King David
393.s: Azmaveth son of Adiel was in charge of King David's treasuries (<ref="1Ch.27.25">1Ch.27.25</ref>).

394.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
394.b: Descendant of Saul, son of Jehoaddah
394.s: Azmaveth, a descendant of Saul, son of Jehoaddah..

395.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
395.b: One of David's mighty men, a Barhumite
395.s: Azmaveth the Barhumite was one of David's mighty men, known for his valor (<ref="2Sa.23.31; 1Ch.11.33">2Sa.23.31; 1Ch.11.33</ref>).

396.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
396.b: Ancestor of Jesus Christ in the genealogy of Matthew
396.s: Azor was an ancestor of Jesus Christ, mentioned in the genealogy of Matthew (<ref="Matt 1:13, 14">Matt 1:13, 14</ref>).

397.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
397.b: Ruler of the tribe of Naphtali under David
397.s: Azriel son of Jeremoth was the ruler of the tribe of Naphtali during the reign of King David (<ref="1Ch.27.19">1Ch.27.19</ref>).

398.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
398.b: Head of a half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead
398.s: Azriel was a head of a father's house in the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead (<ref="1Ch.5.24">1Ch.5.24</ref>).

399.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
399.b: Official sent to arrest the prophet Jeremiah
399.s: Azriel was one of the officials sent by King Jehoiakim to arrest the prophet Jeremiah (<ref="Jer.36.26">Jer.36.26</ref>).

400.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
400.b: A descendant of David through Jehoiachin.
400.s: Azrikam was a descendant of David through Jehoiachin.

401.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
401.b: A descendant of Saul and Jonathan.
401.s: Azrikam was a descendant of Saul and Jonathan.

402.d: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
402.s: Azrikam was a Levite who lived in Jerusalem.

403.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
403.b: An official in King Ahaz's household.
403.s: Azrikam was an official in charge of King Ahaz's palace.

404.d: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
404.b: Wife of Caleb and mother of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.
404.s: Azubah was Caleb's wife and the mother of his sons Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.

405.d: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
405.b: The mother of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.
405.s: Azubah was the mother of King Jehoshaphat of Judah.

406.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
406.b: Father of Paltiel, a leader from the tribe of Issachar.
406.s: Azzan was the father of Paltiel, a leader from Issachar chosen to help divide Canaan.

407.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
407.b: Father of the wicked prince Jaazaniah.
407.s: Azzur was the father of Jaazaniah, one of the wicked princes Ezekiel saw in a vision.

408.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
408.b: Father of the false prophet Hananiah.
408.s: Azzur was the father of Hananiah, a false prophet who opposed Jeremiah.

409.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
409.b: A leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
409.s: Azzur was one of the leaders who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.

410.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
410.s: Baal was a descendant of Reuben, the firstborn son of Jacob.

411.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
411.b: A son of Abiel and descendant of Benjamin.
411.s: Baal was a son of Abiel and a descendant of Benjamin.

412.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
412.b: An overseer of olive and sycamore trees under David.
412.s: Baal-hanan the Gederite was in charge of the olive and sycamore trees in the lowlands under David's reign.

413.d: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
413.s: Baal-hanan was a king of Edom who reigned before Israel had kings.

414.d: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
414.b: King of the Ammonites during the Babylonian exile.
414.s: Baalis, the king of the Ammonites, sent Ishmael to assassinate Gedaliah the governor.

415.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
415.b: A Philistine god worshiped at Ekron.
415.s: Baal-zebub was the god of Ekron whom Ahaziah consulted about his illness.

416.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
416.b: One of Solomon's twelve district governors.
416.s: Baana son of Ahilud was one of Solomon's twelve district governors.

417.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
417.b: One of Solomon's twelve district governors.
417.s: Baana son of Hushai governed the territory of Asher and Aloth under Solomon.

418.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
418.b: A man who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
418.s: Baana son of Zadok made repairs to a section of Jerusalem's wall.

419.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
419.b: One of David's mighty warriors from Netophah.
419.s: Baanah the Netophathite was one of David's mighty warriors.

420.d: David's compatriots living at the time of United Monarchy
420.b: A captain who murdered Ish-bosheth, Saul's son.
420.s: Baanah and his brother Rechab assassinated Ish-bosheth, hoping to gain favor with David.

421.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
421.b: A leader who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.
421.s: Baanah was one of the leaders who returned with Zerubbabel from Babylon to Jerusalem.

422.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
422.b: A leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
422.s: Baanah was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

423.d: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
423.b: A wife of Shaharaim, a Benjamite.
423.s: Baara was one of the wives of Shaharaim, a descendant of Benjamin.

424.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
424.b: A Levite in the lineage of Gershom.
424.s: Baaseiah was a Levite descended from Gershom, the son of Levi.

425.d: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
425.b: Third king of Israel who ruled for 24 years.
425.s: Baasha, son of Ahijah, became king of Israel and reigned for 24 years.

426.d: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
426.b: A Levite who lived in Jerusalem.
426.s: Bakbakkar was a Levite who resided in Jerusalem.

427.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
427.b: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
427.s: Bakbuk was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from exile.

428.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
428.b: A Levite who served in Jerusalem after the exile.
428.s: Bakbukiah was a Levite who held leadership roles in Jerusalem after the exile.

429.d: Prophet living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
429.b: A prophet hired to curse Israel but blessed them instead.
429.s: Balaam was a pagan prophet hired by Balak to curse Israel, but he blessed them instead.

430.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
430.s: Baladan was the father of Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon.

431.d: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
431.b: King of Moab who hired Balaam to curse Israel.
431.s: Balak, son of Zippor, was the king of Moab who tried to curse Israel through Balaam.

432.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
432.b: A Levite musician in the time of David.
432.s: Bani was a Levite who served as a musician during David's reign.

433.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
433.b: A descendant of Perez from the tribe of Judah.
433.s: Bani, a descendant of Perez, was among those who settled in Jerusalem.

434.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
434.b: One of David's mighty warriors from the tribe of Gad.
434.s: Bani the Gadite was one of David's mighty warriors.

435.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
435.b: An Israelite who agreed to put away his foreign wife.
435.s: Bani was one of the men who had married foreign women and agreed to put them away.

436.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
436.b: A family group that had married foreign women.
436.s: The sons of Bani were among those who had married foreign women during Ezra's time.

437.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
437.b: Ancestor of a family who returned from Babylonian exile.
437.s: Bani was the ancestor of a family that returned to Judah from Babylonian captivity.

438.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
438.b: A leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
438.s: Bani was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

439.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
439.b: A Levite overseer in Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.
439.s: Bani was a Levite who served as an overseer in Jerusalem.

440.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
440.b: A Levite who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
440.s: Bani, a Levite, made repairs to a section of Jerusalem's wall.

441.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
441.b: A Levite who taught the Law and led prayers.
441.s: Bani (Binnui) was a Levite involved in teaching the Law and leading prayers during Nehemiah's time.

442.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
442.b: A Levite who led prayers and sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
442.s: Bani was a Levite who led prayers of confession and sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

443.d: Man living at the time of the New Testament
443.b: A notorious prisoner released instead of Jesus.
443.s: Barabbas, a notorious prisoner, was released by Pilate instead of Jesus at the crowd's demand.

444.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
444.b: The father of Elihu, one of Job's friends.
444.s: Barachel the Buzite was the father of Elihu, one of the men who spoke to Job.

445.b: An Israelite commander who defeated Canaanite forces with Deborah.
445.s: Barak, son of Abinoam, led the Israelites to victory against Canaanite forces under Deborah's leadership.

446.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
446.b: A descendant of David through the line of Solomon.
446.s: Bariah was a descendant of King David through Solomon's line.

447.d: Man living at the time of the New Testament
447.b: A Jewish sorcerer who opposed Paul and Barnabas.
447.s: Bar-Jesus, also known as Elymas, was a Jewish sorcerer who tried to hinder Paul and Barnabas' ministry.

448.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
448.b: Ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from exile.
448.s: Barkos was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from Babylonian captivity.

449.d: Levite living at the time of the New Testament
449.b: A Levite from Cyprus who accompanied Paul on missionary journeys.
449.s: Barnabas, also known as Joseph or Joses, was a Levite from Cyprus who played a significant role in the early church and accompanied Paul on missionary journeys.

450.d: Apostle living at the time of the New Testament
450.b: One of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ.
450.s: Bartholomew was one of the twelve apostles chosen by Jesus.

451.d: Man living at the time of the New Testament
451.b: A blind beggar healed by Jesus near Jericho.
451.s: Bartimaeus, a blind beggar, was healed by Jesus as He was leaving Jericho.

452.d: Jeremiah's servant living at the time of Divided Monarchy
452.b: Jeremiah's scribe who recorded and delivered his prophecies.
452.s: Baruch, son of Neriah, served as Jeremiah's scribe and faithfully recorded and delivered his prophecies.

453.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
453.b: A priest who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
453.s: Baruch was a priest who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

454.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
454.b: A descendant of Judah who settled in Jerusalem.
454.s: Baruch, a descendant of Perez from the tribe of Judah, settled in Jerusalem after the exile.

455.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
455.b: A man who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.
455.s: Baruch, son of Zabbai, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's time.

456.d: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
456.b: A Gileadite who provided for David during Absalom's rebellion.
456.s: Barzillai the Gileadite supplied provisions to David during his flight from Absalom and was later honored by the king.

457.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
457.s: Barzillai the Meholathite was the grandfather of the five sons Michal adopted.

458.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
458.b: Ancestor of a priestly family who returned from exile.
458.s: The descendants of Barzillai were a priestly family who returned from Babylonian exile but could not prove their lineage.

459.d: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
459.b: Wife of Ahimaaz, one of Solomon's district governors.
459.s: Basemath, daughter of Solomon, was married to Ahimaaz, one of Solomon's twelve district governors.

460.d: David's wife living at the time of United Monarchy
460.b: Wife of Uriah, later married David and bore Solomon.
460.s: Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, later became David's wife and the mother of Solomon.

461.d: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
461.b: Judah's Canaanite wife; mother of Er, Onan, and Shelah.
461.s: Bath-shua, a Canaanite woman, was Judah's wife and the mother of his first three sons.

462.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
462.b: A leader who helped repair Jerusalem's wall
462.s: Bavvai, son of Henadad and ruler of half the district of Keilah, repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall.

463.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
463.b: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from exile.
463.s: Bazluth (Bazlith) was the ancestor of a family of temple servants who returned from Babylonian captivity.

464.d: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
464.b: A Benjamite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
464.s: Bealiah, a Benjamite warrior, was one of the men who joined David at Ziklag.

465.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
465.b: Head of a family that returned from Babylonian exile.
465.s: Bebai was the head of a family that returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

466.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
466.b: Ancestor of exiles who returned with Ezra to Jerusalem.
466.s: Zechariah, a descendant of Bebai, led 28 men of his family to return with Ezra to Jerusalem.

467.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
467.b: A leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
467.s: Bebai was one of the leaders who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.

468.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
468.b: Son of Benjamin, listed among those who entered Egypt.
468.s: Becher was a son of Benjamin and is listed among the family members who entered Egypt with Jacob.

469.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
469.b: An Ephraimite clan head in the wilderness census.
469.s: The Becherites, descendants of Becher, were a clan of the tribe of Ephraim during the wilderness census.

470.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
470.b: An ancestor of King Saul from the tribe of Benjamin.
470.s: Becorath was an ancestor of King Saul and a member of the tribe of Benjamin.

471.d: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
471.b: Father of Hadad, an Edomite king.
471.s: Bedad was the father of Hadad, one of the kings of Edom before Israel had a king.

472.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
472.b: A descendant of Manasseh through Machir and Gilead.
472.s: Bedan was a descendant of Manasseh, listed in the genealogy of Machir and Gilead.

473.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
473.b: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the exile.
473.s: Bedeiah was one of the Israelites who had married foreign women during the exile and agreed to send them away.

474.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
474.b: A descendant of Asher through Zophah.
474.s: Beera was a descendant of Asher, listed in the genealogy of Zophah.

475.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
475.b: A Reubenite leader exiled by the Assyrian king Tiglath-Pileser.
475.s: Beerah, a leader from the tribe of Reuben, was taken into exile by Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria.

476.d: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
476.b: A Hittite, father of Esau's wife Judith.
476.s: Beeri the Hittite was the father of Judith, one of Esau's wives.

477.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
477.s: Beeri was the father of Hosea, the prophet who authored the biblical book bearing his name.

478.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
478.s: Bela, a descendant of Reuben, was the son of Azaz

479.d: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
479.b: Son of Beor, the first king of Edom.
479.s: Bela, son of Beor, was the first king to reign in Edom before Israel had a king.

480.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
480.b: Son of Benjamin, head of the Belaite clan
480.s: Bela was a son of Benjamin and the head of the Belaite clan within the tribe of Benjamin.

481.d: Emperor living at the time of Exile and Return
481.b: The last Emperor of Babylon, son of Nabonidus.
481.s: Belshazzar, the last Emperor of Babylon, is mentioned in the book of Daniel as the son of Nebuchadnezzar (though historically known as the son of Nabonidus).

482.d: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
482.b: A Levite appointed as a gatekeeper for the ark.
482.s: Ben, a Levite, was appointed as one of the gatekeepers for the ark during its transfer to Jerusalem.

483.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
483.b: Solomon's son-in-law, an official in his administration.
483.s: Ben-abinadab, Solomon's son-in-law, was one of the twelve officials appointed over Israel to provide food for the king and his household.

484.d: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
484.b: A Levite musician during the transfer of the ark.
484.s: Benaiah, a Levite, played the lyre and served as a gatekeeper during the transfer of the ark to Jerusalem.

485.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
485.b: Father of Jehoiada, who succeeded Ahithophel as David's counselor.
485.s: Jehoiada, the son of Benaiah, succeeded Ahithophel as King David's counselor.

486.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
486.b: A Simeonite leader during the reign of Hezekiah.
486.s: Benaiah was one of the Simeonite leaders who, during the reign of Hezekiah, attacked the Hamites and Meunites in their dwellings.

487.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
487.b: A Levite of the sons of Asaph, filled with the Spirit.
487.s: Benaiah in <ref="2Ch.20.14">2Ch.20.14</ref> is the father of Jahaziel, a Levite of the sons of Asaph, during the reign of King Jehoshaphat

488.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
488.b: An overseer in the temple during Hezekiah's reign.
488.s: Benaiah was one of the overseers appointed by King Hezekiah to distribute the contributions to the priests and Levites in the temple.

489.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
489.b: A Pirathonite, one of David's mighty warriors.
489.s: Benaiah the Pirathonite was one of David's thirty mighty warriors and served as the leader of the Ephraimites.

490.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
490.b: Son of Jehoiada, a mighty warrior and loyal supporter of David and Solomon.
490.s: Benaiah, the son of Jehoiada, was a mighty warrior in David's army and later served as the commander of Solomon's army and a key advisor to the king.

491.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
491.b: Father of Pelatiah, a wicked prince of Israel.
491.s: Pelatiah son of Benaiah, a prince of Israel, was one of the wicked leaders who opposed Ezekiel's prophecy and died as a sign of judgment.

492.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
492.b: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
492.s: Benaiah, from the descendants of Parosh, was one of the men who had married foreign women during the Exile.

493.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
493.b: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
493.s: Benaiah, from the descendants of Pahath-moab, was one of the men who had married foreign women during the Exile.

494.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
494.b: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
494.s: Benaiah, from the descendants of Bani, was one of the men who had married foreign women during the Exile.

495.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
495.b: An Israelite who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
495.s: Benaiah, from the descendants of Nebo, was one of the men who had married foreign women during the Exile.

496.d: Ammonite living at the time of the Patriarchs
496.b: Son of Lot's younger daughter; father of the Ammonites.
496.s: Ben-ammi was the son of Lot's younger daughter and the ancestor of the Ammonites.

497.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
497.b: One of Solomon's twelve district governors.
497.s: Ben-deker was one of the twelve district governors appointed by Solomon to provide provisions for the king and his household.

924.d: Man living at the time of the New Testament
924.b: Roman proconsul of Achaia; refused to judge Paul.
924.s: Gallio, the Roman proconsul of Achaia, refused to judge Paul when the Jews brought charges against him in Corinth.

925.d: Man living at the time of the New Testament
925.b: Pharisee; teacher of the law; Paul's mentor.
925.s: Gamaliel, a respected Pharisee and teacher of the law, was Paul's mentor and advised the Sanhedrin to be cautious in their treatment of the apostles.

926.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
926.b: Leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the Exodus.
926.s: Gamaliel, the son of Pedahzur, was the leader of the tribe of Manasseh during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

927.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
927.b: Head of a priestly division in David's time.
927.s: Gamul was the head of the twenty-second priestly division organized during King David's reign.

928.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
928.b: One of David's mighty warriors; an Ithrite.
928.s: Gareb the Ithrite was one of David's mighty warriors, known for his military prowess.

929.d: People descended from the area of Garem(?)
929.s: The Garmite town of Keilah was founded by a son of Hodiah of Judah.

930.d: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
930.b: Son of Eliphaz; grandson of Esau; Edomite chief.
930.s: Gatam was a son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau, and one of the chiefs of Edom.

931.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
931.b: Son of Caleb and his concubine Ephah.
931.s: Gazez was a son of Caleb and his concubine Ephah, born after Haran.

932.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
932.s: Gazez was a grandson of Caleb, born to Haran's son Gazez.

933.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
933.b: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
933.s: Gazzam was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

934.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
934.b: Son of Uri; one of Solomon's twelve district governors.
934.s: Geber, the son of Uri, was one of the twelve district governors appointed by King Solomon to provide food for the royal household.

935.d: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
935.b: Son of Jeduthun; a temple musician during David's reign.
935.s: Gedaliah, a son of Jeduthun, was one of the temple musicians appointed by King David to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.

936.d: Governor living at the time of Divided Monarchy
936.b: Appointed governor of Judah by Babylonians; assassinated by Ishmael.
936.s: Gedaliah, appointed governor of Judah by the Babylonians after the fall of Jerusalem, was assassinated by Ishmael, leading to the flight of the remaining Jews to Egypt.

937.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
937.b: Priest who married a foreign woman during the Exile.
937.s: Gedaliah, a priest, was among those who had married foreign women during the Babylonian exile and pledged to put them away.

938.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
938.b: Son of Pashhur; an official during Zedekiah's reign.
938.s: Gedaliah, the son of Pashhur, was one of the officials who heard Jeremiah's message and urged King Zedekiah to put him to death.

939.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
939.s: Gedaliah was the grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah, who prophesied during the reign of King Josiah of Judah.

940.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
940.b: Son of Abiel, the founder of Gibeon.
940.s: Gedor was a son of Abiel (or 'Jeiel'), the  father (ie re-founder) of Gibeon, and an ancestor of King Saul.

941.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
941.b: Elisha's servant; punished with leprosy for greed and deceit.
941.s: Gehazi, the servant of the prophet Elisha, was punished with leprosy for his greed and deceit in the matter of Naaman's healing.

942.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
942.b: Father of Ammiel, the spy from the tribe of Dan.
942.s: Gemalli was the father of Ammiel, who represented the tribe of Dan as one of the twelve spies sent to explore Canaan.

943.d: Priest living at the time of Divided Monarchy
943.b: Son of Hilkiah; messenger sent by Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar.
943.s: Gemariah, the son of Hilkiah, was a messenger sent by King Zedekiah of Judah to deliver a letter to King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon.

944.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
944.b: Son of Shaphan; official during Jehoiakim's reign; opposed burning scroll.
944.s: Gemariah, the son of Shaphan, was an official during King Jehoiakim's reign who opposed the burning of Jeremiah's scroll.

945.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
945.b: Son of Hadad the Edomite; raised in Pharaoh's palace.
945.s: Genubath was the son of Hadad the Edomite and was raised in Pharaoh's palace alongside the Pharaoh's own children.

946.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
946.b: Son of Bela, grandson of Benjamin.
946.s: Gera was a son of Bela and a grandson of Benjamin.

947.s: Gera (or Heglam) was a son of Ehud, a Benjamite, and was among those who were carried into exile.

948.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
948.b: Benjamite; cursed David during Absalom's rebellion; later sought forgiveness.
948.s: Gera was a Benjamite who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion but later sought forgiveness when David returned to Jerusalem.

949.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
949.b: Descendant of Benjamin; ancestor of Ehud, a judge of Israel.
949.s: Gera was a descendant of Benjamin and an ancestor of Ehud, a left-handed judge who delivered Israel from Moabite oppression.

950.d: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
950.b: Son of Moses; father of Jonathan, a renegade priest.
950.s: Gershom was the firstborn son of Moses and Zipporah, and his descendant Jonathan served as a priest for the idolatrous Danites.

951.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
951.b: Descendant of Phinehas; returned to Jerusalem with Ezra.
951.s: Gershom, a descendant of Phinehas, was among the men who returned to Jerusalem with Ezra after the Babylonian exile.

952.d: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
952.b: Firstborn son of Levi; head of the Gershonite Levites.
952.s: Gershon was the firstborn son of Levi and the ancestor of the Gershonite Levites, who were responsible for the tabernacle curtains, coverings, and related duties.

953.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
953.b: Son of Jahdai, a descendant of Caleb.
953.s: Geshan was a son of Jahdai, a wife of Caleb, from the tribe of Judah.

954.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
954.b: Arab opponent of Nehemiah; tried to hinder wall rebuilding.
954.s: Geshem the Arab, along with Sanballat and Tobiah, opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem and tried to intimidate and discourage him.

955.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
955.b: Son of Aram; grandson of Shem; part of Table of Nations.
955.s: Gether was a son of Aram and a grandson of Shem, mentioned in the genealogies of the Table of Nations.

956.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
956.b: Son of Machi; representative of Gad among the twelve spies.
956.s: Geuel, the son of Machi, was the representative of the tribe of Gad among the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore Canaan.

957.d: Woman or town of the time of Divided Monarchy
957.b: With Machbenah, daughters or towns of Sheva.
957.s: Gibea, with Machbenah, daughters or cities founded by Sheva.

958.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
958.b: Son of Heman; a temple musician during David's reign.
958.s: Giddalti was one of the sons of Heman, appointed by King David as a temple musician to prophesy with lyres, harps, and cymbals.

959.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
959.b: Ancestor of temple servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
959.s: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

960.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
960.b: Ancestor of Solomon's servants who returned from Babylonian exile.
960.s: Giddel was an ancestor of a group of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile.

961.b: Judge of Israel; defeated Midianites; tested and reassured by God.
961.s: Gideon, also called Jerubbaal or Jerubbesheth, was a judge of Israel who, with God's help, defeated the Midianites and delivered Israel from oppression.

962.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
962.b: Leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Exodus.
962.s: Gideoni, the son of Abidan, was the leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the Israelites' journey through the wilderness.

963.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
963.b: Priest and musician during the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
963.s: Gilalai was a priest and musician who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

964.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
964.b: Descendant of Manasseh; son of Michael; father of Jaroah.
964.s: Gilead, a descendant of Manasseh, was the son of Michael and the father of Jaroah, as recorded in the genealogy of the tribe of Gad.

965.b: Father of Jephthah, a judge of Israel.
965.s: Gilead was the father of Jephthah, a mighty warrior and judge of Israel who delivered the Israelites from the Ammonites.

966.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
966.b: Son of Machir; grandson of Manasseh; father of six sons.
966.s: Gilead was the son of Machir, grandson of Manasseh, and father of six sons who became the heads of Gileadite clans.

967.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
967.b: Father of Tibni, who opposed Omri for kingship.
967.s: Ginath was the father of Tibni, who contended with Omri for the throne of Israel.

968.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
968.b: A priest who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
968.s: Ginnethon, a priest, was among those who sealed the covenant during Nehemiah's reforms.

969.b: A Canaanite people group living in the Promised Land.
969.s: The Girgashites were one of the Canaanite groups inhabiting the land promised to Abraham's descendants.

970.b: A people group David raided while living among the Philistines.
970.s: The Girzites were a people group David raided during his time living in Philistine territory.

971.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
971.b: An overseer of the temple servants during Nehemiah's time.
971.s: Gishpa was an overseer of the temple servants (Nethinim) during Nehemiah's time.

972.b: A people group mentioned in the Old Testament.
972.s: The Gizonites are mentioned in <ref="1Ch.11.34">1Ch.11.34</ref> without any additional context.

973.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
973.b: A descendant of Reuben, son of Joel.
973.s: Gog, a descendant of Reuben, is mentioned in the genealogy of Reuben in <ref="1Ch.5.4">1Ch.5.4</ref>.

974.b: A king of Goyim who fought alongside Chedorlaomer.
974.s: Tidal, king of Goiim (nations), was one of the kings who fought alongside Chedorlaomer in Genesis 14.

975.d: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
975.b: A Philistine giant defeated by David.
975.s: Goliath was the Philistine champion from Gath who was defeated by David in a battle.

976.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
976.b: Son of Japheth; father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.
976.s: Gomer, a son of Japheth, was the father of Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah, as listed in the Table of Nations.

977.d: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
977.s: Gomer, the daughter of Diblaim, was the wife of the prophet Hosea.

978.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
978.b: A descendant of Gad; father of Abdiel.
978.s: Guni, a descendant of Gad, was the father of Abdiel, as mentioned in the genealogy of Gad.

979.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
979.b: Son of Naphtali, grandson of Jacob.
979.s: Guni was a son of Naphtali and a grandson of Jacob, as listed in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.

980.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
980.b: A descendant of Judah through Hezron.
980.s: Haahashtari was a descendant of Judah through Hezron, as listed in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

981.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
981.b: A priest whose descendants were unable to prove their lineage.
981.s: Habaiah was a priest whose descendants were excluded from the priesthood due to insufficient genealogical records.

982.d: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
982.b: A prophet who questioned God's justice.
982.s: Habakkuk, a prophet, wrote the book bearing his name, which records his dialogue with God about justice and faith.

983.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
983.b: Grandfather of Jaazaniah, a Rechabite leader.
983.s: Habazziniah was the grandfather of Jaazaniah, a leader of the Rechabites during Jeremiah's time.

984.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
984.b: Father of Nehemiah, the governor of Judah.
984.s: Hacaliah was the father of Nehemiah, who served as the governor of Judah during the Persian period.

985.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
985.b: Father of Jehiel, one of David's family servants.
985.s: Hachmoni was the father of Jehiel who, with Jonathan attended King David's sons.

986.b: A clan or family known for their mighty warriors.
986.s: The Hachmonites, also known as the Tahchemonites, were a clan or family that produced some of David's mighty warriors.

987.d: King living at the time of United Monarchy
987.b: An Edomite prince who opposed Solomon.
987.s: Hadad, an Edomite prince, fled to Egypt and later became an adversary to King Solomon.

988.d: Arabian living at the time of the Patriarchs
988.b: A son of Ishmael, Abraham's son.
988.s: Hadad was one of the twelve sons of Ishmael, Abraham's son.

989.d: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
989.s: Hadad, son of Bedad, became king of Edom after Husham's death.

990.d: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
990.b: The last king of Edom before Israelite rule.
990.s: Hadad, also known as Hadar, was the last king of Edom before the Israelites established their monarchy.

991.d: King living at the time of United Monarchy
991.b: King of Zobah, defeated by David.
991.s: Hadadezer, king of Zobah, was defeated by King David in battle, and his allies, the Arameans, became subject to Israel.

992.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
992.b: Father of Amasa, who opposed taking captives from Judah.
992.s: Hadlai was the father of Amasa, who opposed taking captives from Judah during the reign of King Ahaz.

993.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
993.b: Son of Joktan, a descendant of Shem.
993.s: Hadoram was a son of Joktan and a descendant of Shem, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

994.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
994.b: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
994.s: Hagab was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity, as recorded in Ezra.

995.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
995.b: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
995.s: Hagabah, also known as Hagaba, was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

996.d: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
996.b: Sarah's Egyptian maidservant; mother of Ishmael.
996.s: Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian maidservant, bore Abraham a son named Ishmael and is also mentioned in Paul's allegory in Galatians.

997.d: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
997.b: A prophet who encouraged the rebuilding of the temple.
997.s: Haggai, a prophet during the post-exilic period, urged the people to rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.

998.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
998.b: A priest mentioned in Nehemiah's time.
998.s: Haggedolim was a priest during the time of Nehemiah, mentioned in the list of priests and Levites.

999.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
999.b: Son of Gad, grandson of Jacob.
999.s: Haggi was a son of Gad and a grandson of Jacob, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and Numbers.

1000.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1000.s: Haggiah, a Levite descended from Merari, is mentioned in the genealogy of the Levites in 1 Chronicles.

1001.d: Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
1001.b: One of David's wives; mother of Adonijah.
1001.s: Haggith was one of King David's wives and the mother of Adonijah, who attempted to claim the throne.

1002.d: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1002.b: A Gadite, father of Mibhar, one of David's mighty men.
1002.s: Hagri was the father of Mibhar, one of David's mighty men from the tribe of Gad.

1003.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1003.b: Father of Johanan, a leader who returned from Babylon.
1003.s: Hakkatan was the father of Johanan, a leader who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian exile.

1004.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1004.b: A priest in the time of David.
1004.s: Hakkoz was a priest who served during the reign of King David, as mentioned in the priestly divisions.

1005.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1005.b: A post-exilic priest whose descendants were excluded from the priesthood.
1005.s: Hakkoz was a priest whose descendants were unable to prove their priestly lineage after the Babylonian exile.

1006.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1006.b: A priest who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.
1006.s: Hakkoz, a priest, was involved in repairing sections of the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

1007.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1007.b: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
1007.s: Hakupha was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

1008.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1008.b: Father of Shallum, a leader who helped repair Jerusalem's wall.
1008.s: Hallohesh was the father of Shallum, a leader who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

1009.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
1009.b: One of Noah's three sons, father of Canaan.
1009.s: Ham, one of Noah's three sons, was the father of Canaan and the ancestor of various nations.

1010.d: Persian living at the time of Exile and Return
1010.b: A Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews.
1010.s: Haman, a high-ranking Persian official, conspired to kill all the Jews in the empire but was ultimately thwarted by Queen Esther and Mordecai.

1011.b: A Canaanite people group descended from Canaan.
1011.s: The Hamathites were a Canaanite people group descended from Canaan, son of Ham.

1012.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1012.b: A Kenite clan, descendants of Salma.
1012.s: Hammath was a Kenite clan, listed among the descendants of Salma, the  father (ie founder) of Bethlehem.

1013.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1013.b: The father of Haman, the enemy of the Jews.
1013.s: Hammedatha was the father of Haman, the Persian official who plotted to destroy the Jews in the book of Esther.

1014.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1014.b: Father of Jerahmeel and Malchijah (or 'Malchiah'), officials during Jeremiah's time.
1014.s: Hammelech, meaning "the king," was the father of Jerahmeel and Malchijah (or 'Malchiah'), officials mentioned in the book of Jeremiah.

1015.d: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1015.b: Sister of Gilead; mother of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.
1015.s: Hammolecheth, the sister of Gilead, was the mother of Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.

1016.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1016.b: Son of Mishma, a descendant of Simeon.
1016.s: Hammuel, a descendant of Simeon, was the son of Mishma.

1017.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
1017.b: A Hivite prince, father of Shechem.
1017.s: Hamor, a Hivite prince, was the father and founder of Shechem and negotiated with Jacob's sons after Shechem's assault on Dinah.

1018.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1018.b: Son of Perez, grandson of Judah.
1018.s: Hamul was a son of Perez and a grandson of Judah, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles.

1019.d: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1019.b: Mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah, kings of Judah.
1019.s: Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah, was the mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah, two kings of Judah.

1020.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1020.b: Jeremiah's cousin, from whom he bought a field.
1020.s: Hanamel, Jeremiah's cousin, sold a field to the prophet as a sign of future restoration during the Babylonian siege.

1021.d: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1021.b: One of David's mighty warriors, son of Maacah.
1021.s: Hanan, the son of Maacah, was one of King David's mighty warriors.

1022.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1022.s: Hanan, a Benjamite, was the son of Shashak, as mentioned in the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles.

1023.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1023.b: Son of Azel, a descendant of King Saul.
1023.s: Hanan, a descendant of King Saul, was the son of Azel, as mentioned in the genealogies of 1 Chronicles.

1024.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1024.b: A temple servant who returned from Babylonian exile.
1024.s: Hanan was among the temple servants who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity.

1025.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1025.b: Son of Igdaliah, associated with the Rechabites.
1025.s: Hanan, the son of Igdaliah, was associated with the Rechabites and had a chamber in the temple during Jeremiah's time.

1026.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1026.b: A Levite who signed Nehemiah's covenant.
1026.s: Hanan, a Levite, was among those who signed the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow God's Law.

1027.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1027.b: Another Levite who signed Nehemiah's covenant.
1027.s: Hanan, a Levite, was among the signatories of the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow God's Law.

1028.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1028.b: A treasurer appointed by Nehemiah for the storehouses.
1028.s: Hanan, the son of Zaccur, was appointed by Nehemiah as one of the treasurers responsible for the storehouses.

1029.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1029.b: A Levite who helped explain the Law to the people.
1029.s: Hanan, a Levite, assisted Ezra in teaching the Law to the people during the post-exilic period.

1030.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1030.b: A musician in the temple during David's reign.
1030.s: Hanani was a temple musician during King David's reign, assigned to the twenty-fifth division.

1031.d: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1031.b: A seer who prophesied during the reign of Asa.
1031.s: Hanani, a seer, prophesied during the reigns of Asa and Jehoshaphat, kings of Judah.

1032.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1032.b: A returnee from Babylon who had married a foreign wife.
1032.s: Hanani was among the returnees from Babylon who had married foreign wives during the time of Ezra.

1033.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1033.b: Nehemiah's brother, who reported on Jerusalem's condition.
1033.s: Hanani, Nehemiah's brother, brought a report about the dire situation in Jerusalem, prompting Nehemiah to take action.

1034.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1034.b: A priest who participated in the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
1034.s: Hanani, a priest, was among those who participated in the dedication ceremony of the rebuilt wall of Jerusalem.

1035.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1035.b: Son of Heman, a musician in David's time
1035.s: Hananiah, a son of Heman, appointed as a musician during King David's reign.

1036.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1036.b: Son of Zerubbabel, a descendant of King David.
1036.s: Hananiah, a descendant of King David, was the son of Zerubbabel and had a son named Pelatiah.

1037.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1037.b: Descendant of Benjamin mentioned in genealogy
1037.s: Hananiah, a descendant of Benjamin, is listed in the genealogy in <ref="1Ch.8.24">1Ch.8.24</ref>.

1038.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1038.b: Jeiel's son, an army secretary under King Uzziah
1038.s: Hananiah, son of Jeiel, served as an army secretary during King Uzziah's reign.

1039.d: Daniel's compatriot living at the time of Exile and Return
1039.b: One of Daniel's three friends in Babylon.
1039.s: Hananiah, also known as Shadrach, was one of Daniel's three friends who were thrown into the fiery furnace for refusing to worship Nebuchadnezzar's golden image.

1040.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1040.b: One who married a foreign wife during Ezra's time
1040.s: Hananiah, an Israelite who married a foreign wife during Ezra's time.

1041.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1041.b: A false prophet who opposed Jeremiah's prophecies.
1041.s: Hananiah, a false prophet, opposed Jeremiah's prophecies and falsely predicted the end of the Babylonian captivity within two years.

1042.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1042.b: An official during the reign of King Jehoiakim.
1042.s: Hananiah, an official during King Jehoiakim's reign, was present when Baruch read Jeremiah's scroll in the royal secretary's chamber.

1043.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1043.b: A gatekeeper during the time of Jeremiah.
1043.s: Hananiah, the son of Shelemiah, was a gatekeeper who arrested Jeremiah on suspicion of defecting to the Babylonians.

1044.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1044.b: A signatory of the covenant during Nehemiah's time.
1044.s: Hananiah was among the leaders who signed the covenant to follow God's law during Nehemiah's time.

1045.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1045.b: A priest during the high priesthood of Joiakim.

1177.s: Hilkiah, the high priest during King Josiah's reign, discovered the Book of the Law in the temple, sparking a religious reform.

1178.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1178.b: The father of the prophet Jeremiah.
1178.s: Hilkiah, a priest from Anathoth, was the father of the prophet Jeremiah.

1179.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1179.b: A priest who returned from Babylonian exile.
1179.s: Hilkiah was among the priests who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity and served during the high priesthood of Jeshua and Joiakim.

1180.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1180.s: Hilkiah was one of the priests who stood beside Ezra when he read the Book of the Law to the people.

1181.s: Hillel the Pirathonite, a father of judge Abdon of Israel, led the nation for ten years.

1182.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
1182.s: Hirah was an Adullamite who was a close friend of Judah, the son of Jacob.

1183.d: Syrian living at the time of United Monarchy
1183.s: Hiram, a skilled craftsman from Tyre, was commissioned by Solomon to create the bronze furnishings for the temple.

1184.d: King living at the time of United Monarchy
1184.b: King of Tyre, ally of David and Solomon.
1184.s: Hiram, king of Tyre, provided materials and craftsmen for the construction of David's palace and Solomon's temple and palace.

1185.s: The Hivites were one of the Canaanite tribes inhabiting the land promised to the Israelites.

1186.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1186.s: Hizki was a descendant of Elpaal from the tribe of Benjamin.

1187.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1187.b: A descendant of David through Jeconiah.
1187.s: Hizkiah was one of the descendants of King David through the line of Jeconiah.

1188.d: Midianite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1188.s: Hobab, the son of Jethro (or 'Reuel') the Midianite and Moses' brother-in-law, was invited by Moses to join the Israelites on their journey to the Promised Land.

1189.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1189.s: Hod was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.

1190.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1190.b: A descendant of David through Jeconiah.
1190.s: Hodaviah (also known as Hodaiah) was one of the descendants of King David through the line of Jeconiah.

1191.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1191.b: A leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh.
1191.s: Hodaviah was one of the leaders of the half-tribe of Manasseh during the time of King David.

1192.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1192.b: A Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem.
1192.s: Hodaviah was a descendant of Benjamin who resided in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

1193.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1193.b: A Levite who returned from exile.
1193.s: Hodaviah (also known as Hodevah or Judah) was a Levite who returned to Jerusalem from Babylonian captivity and assisted in rebuilding the temple.

1194.d: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1194.s: Hodesh was one of the wives of Shaharaim, a Benjamite, and the mother of several of his children.

1195.d: Woman (?) living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1195.b: Wife of a Judahite named Ishbar.
1195.s: Hodiah was the wife of Ishbar, a descendant of Judah, and the mother two clans.

1196.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1196.b: A leader who signed Nehemiah's covenant.
1196.s: Hodiah was one of the leaders of the people who signed the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow the Law of God.

1197.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1197.b: A priest who signed Nehemiah's covenant.
1197.s: Hodiah was one of the priests who signed the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow the Law of God.

1198.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1198.b: A Levite involved in teaching and worship.
1198.s: Hodiah (also known as Judah) was a Levite who assisted in teaching the Law and leading worship during the time of Ezra and Nehemiah.

1199.d: Woman living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1199.b: Daughter of Zelophehad, of the tribe of Manasseh.
1199.s: Hoglah was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad who received an inheritance in the Promised Land due to their father's lack of male heirs.

1200.b: King of Hebron, defeated by Joshua.
1200.s: Hoham, the Amorite king of Hebron, was one of the five kings who formed an alliance against Joshua and the Israelites, but was ultimately defeated.

1201.d: Priest living at the time of United Monarchy
1201.b: A corrupt priest, son of Eli.
1201.s: Hophni, along with his brother Phinehas, was a corrupt priest who served under his father Eli at the tabernacle in Shiloh.

1202.d: Pharaoh living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1202.s: Hophra, also known as Pharaoh Apries, was the king of Egypt during the time of the prophet Jeremiah and the Babylonian invasion of Judah.

1203.b: King of Gezer, defeated by Joshua.
1203.s: Horam, the king of Gezer, came to help Lachish but was defeated by Joshua and the Israelites.

1204.d: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
1204.s: The Horites were a people group who inhabited the region of Seir before the Edomites.

1205.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1205.b: A spy from the tribe of Simeon.
1205.s: Hori, the son of Shaphat, was one of the twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the land of Canaan.

1206.b: A people group opposed to Nehemiah's work.
1206.s: The Horonites were a people group who opposed Nehemiah's efforts to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

1207.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1207.b: A Levite gatekeeper during David's reign.
1207.s: Hosah was a Levite who served as a gatekeeper at the tabernacle during the reign of King David.

1208.d: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1208.b: A prophet to the northern kingdom of Israel.
1208.s: Hosea was a prophet who ministered to the northern kingdom of Israel during the reigns of several kings, calling the people to repent and return to God.

1209.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1209.b: A military leader during Jeremiah's time.
1209.s: Hoshaiah, the son of Maaseiah, was one of the military leaders who sought Jeremiah's counsel after the fall of Jerusalem but later disobeyed his prophetic warning.

1210.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1210.b: A leader during the dedication of Jerusalem's wall.
1210.s: Hoshaiah was one of the leaders who participated in the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem during the time of Nehemiah.

1211.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1211.b: A descendant of King Jeconiah of Judah.
1211.s: Hoshama was a descendant of Jeconiah, the exiled king of Judah, according to the genealogy in 1 Chronicles.

1212.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1212.b: Leader of the half-tribe of Ephraim.
1212.s: Hoshea, the son of Azaziah, was the leader of the half-tribe of Ephraim during King David's reign.

1213.d: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1213.b: The last king of Israel (northern kingdom).
1213.s: Hoshea was the last king of Israel, reigning from around 732 to 722 BC, until the Assyrian conquest of Samaria.

1214.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1214.b: A leader who sealed Nehemiah's covenant.
1214.s: Hoshea was one of the leaders of the people who signed the covenant led by Nehemiah to follow the Law of God.

1215.d: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1215.b: One of David's mighty warriors from Aroer.
1215.s: Hotham the Aroerite was listed among David's mighty warriors known for their military exploits.

1216.s: Hotham, also known as Helem, was a descendant of Asher mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher.

1217.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1217.b: A son of Heman, a musician in David's court.
1217.s: Hothir was one of the fourteen sons of Heman, appointed by King David to lead worship in the temple.

1218.d: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
1218.b: A huge man from Gath, killed by David's warriors.
1218.s: A huge man from Gath, possibly a descendant of the Rephaim, was killed by David's warriors during a battle with the Philistines.

1219.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
1219.b: A son of Aram, grandson of Shem.
1219.s: Hul was one of the sons of Aram and a grandson of Shem, mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

1220.d: Prophetess living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1220.b: A prophetess during the reign of King Josiah.
1220.s: Huldah was a prophetess who was consulted by King Josiah's officials regarding the authenticity of the Book of the Law discovered during temple repairs.

1221.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1221.s: Huppah was a priest who was assigned the thirteenth division of priestly service during King David's reign.

1222.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1222.s: Huppim is mentioned in the genealogy of Manasseh as a descendant of Ir or as a son of Machir.

1223.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1223.s: Huppim, also known as Hupham or Huram, was a descendant of Benjamin mentioned in the genealogies of Genesis, Numbers, and 1 Chronicles.

1224.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
1224.b: One of Solomon's twelve district governors.
1224.s: Hur was one of the twelve district governors appointed by King Solomon to oversee the provision of food for the royal household.

1225.d: Aaron's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1225.b: A companion of Moses and grandfather of Bezalel.
1225.s: Hur was a prominent figure during the Israelites' journey in the wilderness, serving as a support to Moses and the grandfather of Bezalel, the chief artisan of the tabernacle.

1226.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1226.b: A ruler who helped repair Jerusalem's wall.
1226.s: Hur, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, was involved in repairing a section of Jerusalem's wall during Nehemiah's time.

1227.d: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1227.b: A Midianite king killed by the Israelites.
1227.s: Hur was one of the five Midianite kings slain by the Israelites during the time of Moses.

1228.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1228.s: Huri was a descendant of Gad, mentioned in the genealogy of the Gadites.

1229.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1229.b: A son or town founded by Ezer.
1229.s: Hushah was either a descendant of Judah or a town founded by Ezer in the tribe of.

1230.d: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
1230.b: David's friend and advisor who helped him during Absalom's rebellion.
1230.s: Hushai the Arkite was a loyal friend and advisor to King David, who helped him during Absalom's rebellion by countering the advice of Ahithophel.

1231.d: King living at the time of the Patriarchs
1231.s: Husham was a king of Edom who reigned before the Israelites had kings, according to the genealogies in Genesis and 1 Chronicles.

1232.b: A clan or family known for their warriors.
1232.s: The Hushathites were a clan or family that produced several of David's mighty warriors, including Sibbecai and Mebunnai.

1233.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1233.b: A son of Aher, from the tribe of Dan.
1233.s: Hushim, a son of Aher, is mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Dan in 1 Chronicles.

1234.d: Woman living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1234.b: A son of Shaharaim, a Benjamite.
1234.s: Hushim was one of the sons of Shaharaim, a Benjamite, born to him in the country of Moab.

1235.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1235.b: Son of Dan, ancestor of the Shuhamites.
1235.s: Hushim, also known as Shuham, was the son of Dan and the ancestor of the Shuhamite clan within the tribe of Dan.

1236.d: Man living at the time of the New Testament
1236.b: A man who rejected faith and good conscience.
1236.s: Hymenaeus was a man who had rejected the faith and was handed over to Satan by Paul so that he might learn not to blaspheme.

1237.d: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
1237.b: One of King David's sons born in Jerusalem.
1237.s: Ibhar was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem, as recorded in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles.

1238.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1238.b: A Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem.
1238.s: Ibneiah, a descendant of Benjamin, was one of the Israelites who resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

1239.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1239.b: A Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem.
1239.s: Ibnijah, a descendant of Benjamin, was one of the Israelites who resettled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

1240.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1240.b: A Levite of the family of Merari.
1240.s: Ibri was a Levite of the family of Merari, mentioned in the context of the divisions of the Levitical priests during the reign of King David.

1241.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1241.s: Ibsam was a descendant of Issachar, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Issachar in 1 Chronicles.

1242.b: A judge of Israel from Bethlehem.
1242.s: Ibzan was a judge of Israel who led the nation for seven years, had thirty sons and thirty daughters, and was buried in Bethlehem.

1243.d: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
1243.b: Son of Phinehas, born when the ark was captured.
1243.s: Ichabod was the son of Phinehas, born when the ark of God was captured by the Philistines and named to reflect the departure of glory from Israel.

1244.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1244.s: Idbash was a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Judah in 1 Chronicles.

1245.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1245.b: Zechariah's son, a leader of Manasseh
1245.s: Iddo, the son of Zechariah, was a leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh during King David's reign.

1246.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1246.b: A Levite in the genealogy of temple singers
1246.s: Iddo (or Adaiah), a Levite in the genealogy of the temple singers.

1247.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
1247.b: Abinadab's son, an official under King Solomon
1247.s: Iddo, the son of Abinadab, was an official in Mahanaim during King Solomon's reign.

1248.d: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1248.b: A seer and prophet during the divided monarchy
1248.s: Iddo, a seer and prophet who recorded the events of the reigns of Solomon, Rehoboam, and Abijah.

1249.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1249.b: Zechariah's grandfather, a priest and prophet in post-exilic Judah
1249.s: Iddo, the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah, was a priest and prophet in post-exilic Judah.

1250.d: Prophet living at the time of Exile and Return
1250.b: A prophet in Casiphia during Ezra's time.
1250.s: Iddo was a prophet in Casiphia to whom Ezra sent a message requesting Levites to assist in the temple service.

1251.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1251.b: A priest during the time of Zerubbabel.
1251.s: Iddo, also known as Adaia, was a priest who returned to Jerusalem with Zerubbabel and was head of a priestly family during the time of Joiakim.

1252.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1252.s: Igal was a descendant of King David, mentioned in the genealogy of David's descendants through his son Jeconiah.

1253.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
1253.s: Igal son of Nathan of Zobah was listed among David's mighty warriors known for their military prowess and bravery.

1254.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1254.b: A scout from the tribe of Issachar.
1254.s: Igal son of Joseph, from the tribe of Issachar, was one of the twelve scouts sent by Moses to explore Canaan.

1255.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1255.b: A man of God during Jeremiah's time.
1255.s: Igdaliah, a man of God, was associated with a chamber in the house of the Lord during the time of the prophet Jeremiah.

1256.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
1256.b: Father of Ira, one of David's mighty warriors.
1256.s: Ikkesh the Tekoite was the father of Ira, one of King David's mighty warriors and a leader in his army.

1257.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1257.s: Imlah was the father of Micaiah, a prophet who spoke the truth to King Ahab of Israel, despite the king's displeasure.

1258.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1258.b: A priestly division and its descendants.
1258.s: Immer was the name of a priestly division during the time of David, and his descendants served as priests in the post-exilic period.

1259.d: Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
1259.b: A priestly family in post-exilic Jerusalem.
1259.s: The descendants of Immer were a priestly family who lived in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile, as recorded in 1 Chronicles and Nehemiah.

1260.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1260.b: Man who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall
1260.s: Immer was one of the people who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem during Nehemiah's time.

1261.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1261.s: Imna was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher in 1 Chronicles.

1262.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1262.s: Imnah, a Levite, was appointed as an overseer of the freewill offerings during the religious reforms of King Hezekiah.

1263.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1263.b: A son of Asher and ancestor of the Imnites.
1263.s: Imnah was a son of Asher and the ancestor of the Imnite clan within the tribe of Asher.

1264.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1264.s: Imrah was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher in 1 Chronicles.

1265.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1265.b: A descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem.
1265.s: Imri, a descendant of Perez from the tribe of Judah, was among those who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

1266.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1266.b: Father of Zaccur, helped rebuild Jerusalem's wall.
1266.s: Imri was the father of Zaccur, who helped rebuild the wall of Jerusalem.

1267.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1267.s: Iphdeiah was a descendant of Benjamin through Shashak.

1268.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
1268.b: Son of Bela, descendant of Benjamin.
1268.s: Ir was a son of Bela and descendant of Benjamin.

1269.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
1269.s: Ira the Jairite was a priest under King David.

1270.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
1270.b: One of David's Thirty warriors, from Tekoa.
1270.s: Ira the Tekoite was one of King David's Thirty mighty warriors.

1271.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
1271.b: One of David's Thirty warriors, an Ithrite.
1271.s: Ira the Ithrite was one of King David's Thirty mighty warriors.

1272.d: Man living at the time before the Flood
1272.b: Descendant of Cain; father of Mehujael.
1272.s: Irad was a descendant of Cain and the father of Mehujael.

1273.d: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
1273.s: Iram was an Edomite chief, a descendant of Esau.

1274.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1274.b: Son of Bela, grandson of Benjamin.
1274.s: Iri was a son of Bela and grandson of Benjamin.

1275.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1275.b: Captain who arrested Jeremiah for desertion.
1275.s: Irijah, a captain, arrested Jeremiah on suspicion of desertion to the Babylonians.

1276.b: Son of Caleb, brother of Elah and Naam.
1276.s: Iru was a son of Caleb, along with his brothers Elah and Naam.

1277.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
1277.b: Son of Abraham; father of Jacob and Esau.
1277.s: Isaac was the son of Abraham and Sarah, and the father of Jacob and Esau. God made a covenant with him, renewing the promises given to Abraham.

1278.d: Prophet living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1278.b: Prophet during reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, Hezekiah.
1278.s: Isaiah was a prophet in Judah during the reigns of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah. His prophecies are recorded in the biblical book bearing his name.

1279.d: Woman living at the time of the Patriarchs
1279.b: Daughter of Haran, Milcah's sister, Lot's sister.
1279.s: Iscah was the daughter of Haran and sister of Milcah and Lot.

1280.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1280.b: Son of Mered in the genealogy of Judah
1280.s: Ishbah's sons were the  father (ie founder) of Eshtemoa and Keilah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah..

1281.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
1281.s: Ishbak was a son of Abraham and his concubine Keturah.

1282.d: Giant living at the time of United Monarchy
1282.b: Philistine giant who fought against David's men.
1282.s: Ishbi-benob, a Philistine giant, was killed by David's warrior Abishai when he threatened David's life.

1283.d: Saul's son living at the time of United Monarchy
1283.b: Son of Saul, king over Israel.
1283.s: Ish-bosheth (also called Eshbaal), Saul's son, was made king over Israel by Abner but was ultimately assassinated, leading to David's rule over all Israel.

1284.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1284.s: Ishhod was the son of Hammoleketh, who was the sister of Manasseh.

1285.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1285.b: Son of Appaim, descendant of Judah.
1285.s: Ishi was a descendant of Judah through Appaim.

1286.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1286.b: Son of Shimon, descendant of Judah.
1286.s: Ishi was a son of Shimon, a descendant of Judah.

1287.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1287.b: Leader of Simeonites who attacked Hamites in Gedor.
1287.s: Ishi was one of the leaders of the Simeonites who attacked the Hamites in Gedor during the days of Hezekiah.

1288.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1288.b: Head of a father's house in Manasseh.
1288.s: Ishi was a head of a father's house in the half-tribe of Manasseh.

1289.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1289.b: Son of Hur, descendant of Judah.
1289.s: Ishma was a son of Hur, a descendant of Judah.

1290.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1290.b: Descendant of Benjamin through Saul's line.
1290.s: Ishmael was a descendant of Benjamin through King Saul's line.

1291.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1291.s: Ishmael son of Jehohanan was a leader in Judah during King Jehoshaphat's reign.

1292.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1292.b: Son of Jehohanan; supported Joash as king.
1292.s: Ishmael was the son of Jehohanan, who supported Jehoiada in making Joash king.

1293.d: Jeremiah's adversary living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1293.b: Assassinated Gedaliah the governor; led captives to Ammon.
1293.s: Ishmael, son of Nethaniah, assassinated Gedaliah the governor and led captives to Ammon before being pursued by Johanan.

1294.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1294.b: Priest who married a foreign woman during Ezra's time.
1294.s: Ishmael was a priest who had married a foreign woman and pledged to put her away during Ezra's reforms.

1295.d: Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
1295.b: Son of Abraham and Hagar; father of Arab tribes.
1295.s: Ishmael, the son of Abraham and Hagar, was the ancestor of various Arab tribes. Though not the chosen heir, he was still blessed by God.

1296.d: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1296.b: Gibeonite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
1296.s: Ishmaiah the Gibeonite was a mighty warrior among the Thirty who joined David at Ziklag.

1297.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1297.b: Leader of the tribe of Zebulun under David.
1297.s: Ishmaiah son of Obadiah was the leader of the tribe of Zebulun during King David's reign.

1298.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1298.s: Ishmerai was a descendant of Benjamin through Elpaal.

1299.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1299.s: Ishpah was a descendant of Benjamin through Beriah.

1300.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1300.s: Ishpan was a descendant of Benjamin through Shashak.

1301.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1301.b: Son of Asher, grandson of Jacob.
1301.s: Ishvah was a son of Asher and grandson of Jacob.

1302.d: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1302.b: Son of Asher, grandson of Jacob.
1302.s: Ishvi (or Isui) was a son of Asher and grandson of Jacob.

1303.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1303.b: Overseer under King Hezekiah during temple restoration.
1303.s: Ismachiah was one of the overseers appointed by King Hezekiah during the restoration of the temple and its services.

1304.d: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
1304.b: Patriarch, son of Isaac, father of twelve tribes
1304.s: Israel, also named Jacob, was the son of Isaac, the father of the twelve tribes of Israel, and a key patriarch of the Jewish people.

1305.d: Levite living at the time of United Monarchy
1305.b: Son of Obed-Edom, a gatekeeper in David's time.
1305.s: Issachar was a son of Obed-Edom, a gatekeeper in the time of King David.

1306.d: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
1306.b: Son of Jacob and Leah, forefather of tribe
1306.s: Issachar was the ninth son of Jacob and fifth by Leah, and he became the forefather of the Israelite tribe of Issachar.

1307.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1307.b: Korahite warrior who joined David at Ziklag.
1307.s: Isshiah the Korahite was one of the warriors who joined David at Ziklag.

1308.d: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1308.b: Levite, grandson of Rehabiah during David's reign.
1308.s: Isshiah was a Levite, the son of Rehabiah and grandson of Moses, who served during King David's reign.

1309.d: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1309.b: Levite, descendant of Rehabiah during David's reign.
1309.s: Isshiah (or Jeshaiah) was a Levite, a descendant of Rehabiah, who served during King David's reign.

1310.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1310.b: Son of Izrahiah, descendant of Issachar.
1310.s: Isshiah was a son of Izrahiah and a descendant of Issachar.

1311.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1311.b: Descendant of Harim; agreed to put away foreign wife.
1311.s: Isshijah, a descendant of Harim, was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's reforms.

1312.d: Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1312.b: Youngest son of Aaron; served as priest.
1312.s: Ithamar was the fourth and youngest son of Aaron, who served as a priest alongside his brothers Nadab, Abihu, and Eleazar.

1313.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1313.b: Descendant of Benjamin living in Jerusalem.
1313.s: Ithiel, a descendant of Benjamin, was among those who settled in Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

1314.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
1314.b: Mentioned in Agur's sayings; meaning uncertain.
1314.s: Ithiel is mentioned twice in <ref="Proverbs 30:1">Proverbs 30:1</ref>, but the meaning and context of the name are uncertain.

1315.d: Moabite warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1315.s: Ithmah the Moabite was one of the mighty warriors in David's army.

1316.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1316.b: Descendant of Asher, son of Zophah.
1316.s: Ithran (or Jether) was a descendant of Asher, the son of Zophah.

1317.d: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
1317.b: Descendant of Esau, son of Dishon the Horite.
1317.s: Ithran was a descendant of Esau and son of Dishon the Horite.

1318.d: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
1318.b: Son of David, born in Hebron to Eglah.
1318.s: Ithream was a son of David, born to him in Hebron by his wife Eglah.

1319.b: Clan descended from Kiriath-jearim; two of David's warriors.
1319.s: The Ithrites were a clan descended from Kiriath-jearim (<ref="1Ch.2.53">1Ch.2.53</ref>), and two of David's mighty warriors, Ira and Gareb, were Ithrites.

1320.d: David's compatriot living at the time of United Monarchy
1320.b: Gittite commander who remained loyal to David.
1320.s: Ittai the Gittite was a commander who remained loyal to David during Absalom's rebellion.

1321.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
1321.s: Ittai, one of King David's mighty men, was from Gibeah of Benjamin.

1322.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1322.b: Son of Asher listed in the genealogy in Chronicles
1322.s: Izhar was a descendant of Asher mentioned among the genealogies of the twelve tribes of Israel.

1323.d: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1323.b: Son of Kohath, grandson of Levi; father of Korah.
1323.s: Izhar (or Amminadab), son of Kohath and father of Korah, was a Levite.

1324.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1324.s: Izliah was a Benjamite, one of the sons of Elpaal.

1325.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1325.s: Izrahiah, a son of Uzzi, was a descendant of Issachar and a clan head.

1326.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1326.b: Descendant of Parosh; agreed to put away foreign wife.
1326.s: Izziah, a descendant of Parosh, was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's reforms.

1327.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1327.s: Jaakobah was a leader from the tribe of Simeon during the reign of King Hezekiah.

1328.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1328.b: Returned exile; descendant of Solomon's servants.
1328.s: Jaalah was among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian exile.

1329.d: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
1329.b: Father of Elhanan, who killed Goliath's brother.
1329.s: Jaare-oregim (or Jair) was the father of Elhanan, who killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath the Gittite.

1330.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1330.s: Jaareshiah was a descendant of Benjamin through Jeroham.

1331.d: Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1331.b: One of David's mighty warriors, the son of Abner.
1331.s: Jaasiel, the son of Abner, was one of David's mighty warriors.

1332.d: Man living at the time of United Monarchy
1332.b: Leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh during David's reign.
1332.s: Jaasiel, the son of Abner, was the leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh during King David's reign.

1333.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1333.b: Descendant of Bani; agreed to put away foreign wife.
1333.s: Jaasu, a descendant of Bani, was among those who agreed to put away their foreign wives during Ezra's reforms.

1334.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1334.b: Leader among the twenty-five men in Ezekiel's vision.
1334.s: Jaazaniah, the son of Azzur, was one of the twenty-five men in Ezekiel's vision who were devising iniquity and giving wicked counsel.

1335.d: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
1335.b: Israelite elder; participated in idolatry in the temple.
1335.s: Jaazaniah, the son of Shaphan, was one of the seventy elders of Israel who participated in idolatrous practices in the temple, as seen in Ezekiel's vision.

1336.d: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1336.b: Son of Jeremiah; a Rechabite during Jeremiah's time.
1336.s: Jaazaniah, the son of Jeremiah, was a Rechabite who was tested by the prophet Jeremiah for his obedience to his ancestor's commands.
