3207.s: Aroer, a city in Judah that received a share of the spoils from David's victory over the Amalekites.

3208.b: A city on the edge of the Arnon Valley.
3208.s: Aroer, a city situated on the edge of the Arnon Valley, near the border between Israel and Moab.

3209.b: A city in Gad, built by the Gadites.
3209.s: Aroer, a city in the territory of Gad, built by the Gadites.

3210.s: Arpad was a city in northern Syria conquered by the Assyrians.

3211.b: A district in Israel under Solomon's rule.
3211.s: Arubboth, a district governed by one of Solomon's twelve officers.

3212.b: A city associated with Abimelech and King Jehoiakim's mother.
3212.s: Arumah or Rumah, a city mentioned in connection with Abimelech's reign and as the hometown of King Jehoiakim's mother.

3213.b: An island city, known for its skilled mariners and soldiers.
3213.s: Arvad, an island city whose inhabitants served as sailors and soldiers for Tyre.

3214.b: A city allotted to Judah and Simeon.
3214.s: Ashan, a city assigned to the tribes of Judah and Simeon, later given to the Levites.

3215.b: A major Philistine city, known for Dagon worship.
3215.s: Ashdod or Azotus, one of the five major Philistine cities, was a center of Dagon worship and a target of prophetic judgment.

3216.b: A major Philistine city, often a target of prophecy.
3216.s: Ashkelon, one of the five principal Philistine cities, was captured by Judah but later became a symbol of judgment.

3217.b: A kingdom summoned to battle against Babylon.
3217.s: Ashkenaz, a kingdom called to join the fight against Babylon in Jeremiah's prophecy.

3218.b: Two cities in the Shephelah region of Judah.
3218.s: Ashnah, two cities in the lowlands of Judah, mentioned in the tribal allotment.

3219.b: A city of Og, king of Bashan.
3219.s: Ashtaroth or Beeshterah, a city in Bashan, ruled by King Og and later allotted to the Levites.

3220.s: Ashteroth-karnaim was a city east of the Jordan River defeated by King Chedorlaomer.

3221.b: A Roman province in western Asia Minor.
3221.s: Asia, a Roman province in western Asia Minor, with Ephesus as its capital.

3222.b: A seaport in Mysia, visited by Paul.
3222.s: Assos, a seaport in Mysia where Paul met his companions during his third missionary journey.

3223.b: A powerful ancient empire, often in conflict with Israel.
3223.s: Assyria, a major Mesopotamian empire, frequently mentioned in the Old Testament as an adversary of Israel and Judah.

3224.b: Threshing floor where Egyptians mourned Jacob
3224.s: Atad was a threshing floor near the Jordan River where the Egyptians mourned Jacob's death.

3225.b: A town on the border of Ephraim and Manasseh.
3225.s: Ataroth, a town on the border between the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh.

3226.b: Town in Gilead allotted to Gad
3226.s: Ataroth was a town in the region of Gilead allotted to the tribe of Gad.

3227.b: A town on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin.
3227.s: Ataroth-addar, a border town between the territories of Ephraim and Benjamin.

3228.b: A town that received spoils from David's victory.
3228.s: Athach, a town in Judah that received a share of the spoils from David's victory over the Amalekites.

3229.b: A place where the Canaanite king of Arad fought Israel.
3229.s: Atharim, a place near the Negev where the Canaanite king of Arad attacked the Israelites during their journey.

3230.b: A major city in Greece, visited by Paul.
3230.s: Athens, the intellectual and cultural center of ancient Greece, where Paul preached the gospel and addressed the Areopagus.

3231.b: Town associated with Joab from the tribe of Judah.
3231.s: Atroth-beth-joab was a town linked to Joab in Judah. (<ref="1Ch.2.54">1Ch.2.54</ref>)

3232.b: Town allotted to the tribe of Gad.
3232.s: Atroth-shophan was a town given to the tribe of Gad. (<ref="Numbers 32:35">Numbers 32:35</ref>)

3233.b: Seaport in Pamphylia visited by Paul and Barnabas.
3233.s: Attalia, a seaport in Pamphylia, was visited by Paul and Barnabas. (<ref="Act.14.25">Act.14.25</ref>)

3234.b: Plain near Damascus, prophesied to be destroyed.
3234.s: Aven Valley, a plain near Damascus, was prophesied to be destroyed. (<ref="Amo.1.5">Amo.1.5</ref>)

3235.b: Capital city of Edomite king Hadad.
3235.s: Avith was the capital city of Hadad, an early Edomite king.

3236.b: Town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.
3236.s: Avvim was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin. (<ref="Joshua 18:23">Joshua 18:23</ref>)

3237.b: Unidentified place near Jerusalem mentioned in Zechariah's prophecy.
3237.s: Azal was an unidentified place near Jerusalem mentioned in Zechariah's prophecy. (<ref="Zechariah 14:5">Zechariah 14:5</ref>)

3238.b: Judean town, site of battles and sieges.
3238.s: Azekah, a Judean town, was the site of several battles and sieges.

3239.b: Place on the southern border of Judah.
3239.s: Azmon was a place on the southern border of Judah.

3240.b: Border town of Naphtali near Mount Tabor.
3240.s: Aznoth-tabor was a border town of Naphtali near Mount Tabor. (<ref="Joshua 19:34">Joshua 19:34</ref>)

3241.b: Town allotted to the tribe of Simeon.
3241.s: Baalah was a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon. (<ref="Joshua 15:29">Joshua 15:29</ref>)

3242.b: Mountain marking the northern boundary of Judah.
3242.s: Mount Baalah marked the northern boundary of Judah's territory. (<ref="Joshua 15:11">Joshua 15:11</ref>)

3243.b: Town fortified by Solomon, possibly in the Lebanon region.
3243.s: Baalath was a town fortified by Solomon, possibly located in the Lebanon region. (<ref="1Ki.9.18; 2Ch.8.6">1Ki.9.18; 2Ch.8.6</ref>)

3244.b: Town allotted to the tribe of Dan.
3244.s: Baalath was a town allotted to the tribe of Dan. (<ref="Joshua 19:44">Joshua 19:44</ref>)

3245.b: Town in the Negev, allotted to Simeon.
3245.s: Baalath-beer (Bealoth, Baal, or Ramoth) was a town in the Negev, allotted to Simeon.

3246.b: Place where Absalom sheared his sheep.
3246.s: Baal-hazor was the place where Absalom sheared his sheep. (<ref="2Sa.13.23">2Sa.13.23</ref>)

3247.b: Moabite town, allotted to Reuben, later retaken by Moab.
3247.s: Baal-meon (Beth-baal-meon, Beth-meon, or Beon) was a Moabite town, allotted to Reuben, but later retaken by Moab.

3248.b: Place where David defeated the Philistines.
3248.s: Baal-perazim was the place where David defeated the Philistines. (<ref="2Sa.5.20; 1Ch.14.11">2Sa.5.20; 1Ch.14.11</ref>)

3249.b: Place where a man brought provisions to Elisha.
3249.s: Baal-shalishah was the place where a man brought provisions to Elisha. (<ref="2Ki.4.42">2Ki.4.42</ref>)

3250.b: Place near Gibeah where Israelites fought the Benjamites.
3250.s: Baal-tamar was a place near Gibeah where the Israelites fought against the Benjamites. (<ref="Judges 20:33">Judges 20:33</ref>)

3251.b: Egyptian location where the Israelites camped before crossing the Red Sea.
3251.s: Baal-zephon was an Egyptian location where the Israelites camped before crossing the Red Sea.

3252.b: Ancient Mesopotamian city, capital of Babylonian Empire, site of the Tower of Babel.
3252.s: Babylon, also known as Babel, Sheshak, Merathaim, or Pekod, was an ancient Mesopotamian city that served as the capital of the Babylonian Empire. (Multiple references, see article for details)

3253.b: Village near Jerusalem, home of Shimei, who cursed David.
3253.s: Bahurim (or Baharum) was a village near Jerusalem, known as the home of Shimei, who cursed David. (<ref="2Sa.3.16; 16:5; 17:18; 19:16; 1Ki.2.8; 2Sa.23.31; 1Ch.11.33">2Sa.3.16; 16:5; 17:18; 19:16; 1Ki.2.8; 2Sa.23.31; 1Ch.11.33</ref>)

3254.b: Moabite temple or high place mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy.
3254.s: Bajith (or "temple") was a Moabite temple or high place mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy against Moab. (<ref="Isaiah 15:2">Isaiah 15:2</ref>)

3255.b: Town allotted to the tribe of Simeon.
3255.s: Balah was a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon. (<ref="Joshua 19:3">Joshua 19:3</ref>)

3256.b: Israelite encampment in Moab during the Exodus.
3256.s: Bamoth was an Israelite encampment in Moab during the Exodus. (<ref="Numbers 21:19-20">Numbers 21:19-20</ref>)

3257.b: Moabite high place where Balak took Balaam.
3257.s: Bamoth-baal was a Moabite high place where Balak took Balaam to curse Israel.

3258.b: Region east of the Jordan, known for its fertility.
3258.s: Bashan was a region east of the Jordan River, known for its fertility and allotted to the half-tribe of Manasseh. (Multiple references, see article for details)

3259.b: Gate in Heshbon, mentioned in Song of Solomon.
3259.s: Bath-rabbim was a gate in Heshbon, mentioned in the Song of Solomon. (<ref="Sng.7.4">Sng.7.4</ref>)

3260.b: Gate of the Jerusalem temple, site of Peter's miracle.
3260.s: The Beautiful Gate was a gate of the Jerusalem temple, where Peter healed a lame man. (<ref="Act.3.2, 10">Act.3.2, 10</ref>)

3261.b: Site where God provided water for the Israelites.
3261.s: Beer was a site where God provided water for the Israelites during their wilderness journey. (<ref="Numbers 21:16">Numbers 21:16</ref>)

3262.b: Place mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy against Moab.
3262.s: Beer-elim was a place mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy against Moab. (<ref="Isaiah 15:8">Isaiah 15:8</ref>)

3263.b: Well where Hagar encountered the Angel of the Lord.
3263.s: Beer-lahai-roi was a well where Hagar encountered the Angel of the Lord, between Kadesh and Bered.

3264.b: Hivite city, later allotted to Benjamin.
3264.s: Beeroth (or Beer) was a Hivite city that later became part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.

3265.b: Important city in southern Israel, associated with the patriarchs.
3265.s: Beersheba (Sheba or Shibah) was an important city in southern Israel, associated with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. (Multiple references, see article for details)

3266.b: Town allotted to the tribe of Dan.
3266.s: Bene-berak was a town allotted to the tribe of Dan. (<ref="Joshua 19:45">Joshua 19:45</ref>)

3267.b: Israelite encampment during the wilderness wanderings.
3267.s: Bene-jaakan (Beeroth Bene-jaakan) was an Israelite encampment during the wilderness wanderings.

3268.b: Gate in Jerusalem, associated with the tribe of Benjamin.
3268.s: The Benjamin Gate was a gate in Jerusalem, associated with the tribe of Benjamin.

3269.b: Gate in Jerusalem's wall, mentioned in Zechariah's prophecy.
3269.s: The Benjamin Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, mentioned in Zechariah's prophecy about the city's restoration. (<ref="Zechariah 14:10">Zechariah 14:10</ref>)

3270.b: Valley where Jehoshaphat and his army blessed the Lord.
3270.s: The Beracah Valley was where Jehoshaphat and his army blessed the Lord after a miraculous victory. (<ref="2Ch.20.26">2Ch.20.26</ref>)

3271.b: City in Macedonia where Paul preached; home of Sopater.
3271.s: Berea was a city in Macedonia where Paul preached, and the home of Sopater, one of Paul's traveling companions.

3272.b: Place near where Hagar encountered the Angel of the Lord.
3272.s: Bered was a place near where Hagar encountered the Angel of the Lord when she fled from Sarah. (<ref="Genesis 16:14">Genesis 16:14</ref>)

3273.b: City mentioned in Ezekiel's vision and David's conquests.
3273.s: Berothah (Berothai or Cun) was a city mentioned in Ezekiel's vision of Israel's boundaries and in the account of David's conquests.

3274.b: Brook where David's men pursued the Amalekites.
3274.s: The Besor was a brook where David's men pursued the Amalekites who had raided Ziklag. (<ref="1Sa.30.9, 10, 21">1Sa.30.9, 10, 21</ref>)

3275.b: City from which David took bronze after defeating Hadadezer.
3275.s: Betah was a city from which David took a large amount of bronze after defeating Hadadezer, king of Zobah. (<ref="2Sa.8.8">2Sa.8.8</ref>)

3276.b: Town allotted to the tribe of Asher.
3276.s: Beten was a town allotted to the tribe of Asher in the division of the Promised Land. (<ref="Joshua 19:25">Joshua 19:25</ref>)

3277.b: Canaanite town allotted to Naphtali, but not fully conquered.
3277.s: Beth-anath was a Canaanite town allotted to the tribe of Naphtali, but the Naphtalites did not drive out its inhabitants.

3278.b: Town in the hill country of Judah.
3278.s: Beth-anoth was a town in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in the list of cities and villages within Judah's inheritance. (<ref="Joshua 15:59">Joshua 15:59</ref>)

3279.b: Village near Jerusalem, home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus.
3279.s: Bethany was a village near Jerusalem, known as the home of Mary, Martha, and Lazarus, where Jesus often visited and performed miracles. (Multiple references, see article for details)

3280.b: Town and wilderness area in Judah, also associated with Benjamin.
3280.s: Beth-arabah was a town and wilderness area allotted to Judah and Benjamin, and the Arbathite was a descendant of Abi-albon.

3281.b: Place destroyed by Shalman, mentioned in Hosea's prophecy.
3281.s: Beth-arbel was a place destroyed by Shalman, mentioned in Hosea's prophecy as an example of destruction. (<ref="Hosea 10:14">Hosea 10:14</ref>)

3282.b: Place associated with the families of the house of Ashbea.
3282.s: Beth-ashbea was a place associated with the families of the house of Ashbea, who were known for their fine linen work. (<ref="1Ch.4.21">1Ch.4.21</ref>)

3283.b: Philistine city where Saul's armor was put in a temple.
3283.s: Beth-Ashtoreth was a Philistine city where Saul's armor was put in the temple of Ashtoreth after his death. (<ref="1Sa.31.10">1Sa.31.10</ref>)

3284.b: Town and wilderness near Ai and Bethel.
3284.s: Beth-aven was a town and wilderness near Ai and Bethel, associated with idolatry and Israel's defeat.

3285.b: Town of Benjamin, home to some who returned from exile.
3285.s: Beth-azmaveth (Azmaveth) was a town in Benjamin, home to some who returned from the Babylonian exile.

3286.b: Place where Gideon stationed men to intercept the Midianites.
3286.s: Beth-barah (Bethabara) was a place where Gideon stationed men to intercept the fleeing Midianites, and where John the Baptist baptized.

3287.b: Town in Simeon, formerly called Bethul.
3287.s: Beth-biri was a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon, formerly known as Bethul. (<ref="1Ch.4.31">1Ch.4.31</ref>)

3288.b: Place where the Israelites pursued the Philistines.
3288.s: Beth-car was the place where the Israelites pursued the Philistines after the return of the Ark of the Covenant. (<ref="1Sa.7.11">1Sa.7.11</ref>)

3289.b: Town in Judah, named after the Philistine god Dagon.
3289.s: Beth-dagon was a town in Judah, likely named after the Philistine god Dagon. (<ref="Joshua 15:41">Joshua 15:41</ref>)

3290.b: Town in Asher, named after the Philistine god Dagon.
3290.s: Beth-dagon was a town in the territory of Asher, likely named after the Philistine god Dagon. (<ref="Joshua 19:27">Joshua 19:27</ref>)

3291.b: Place associated with the rulers of Aram (Syria).
3291.s: Beth-eden was a place associated with the rulers of Aram (Syria), mentioned in Amos's prophecy against Damascus. (<ref="Amo.1.5">Amo.1.5</ref>)

3292.b: Place where Jehu killed the brothers of Ahaziah.
3292.s: Beth-eked was a place where Jehu killed the forty-two brothers of Ahaziah, king of Judah. (<ref="2Ki.10.12, 14">2Ki.10.12, 14</ref>)

3293.b: Important city in Israel, associated with Abraham and Jacob.
3293.s: Bethel, also called Luz, was an important city in Israel, associated with the patriarchs Abraham and Jacob, later becoming a center of idolatry. (Multiple references, see article for details)

3294.b: Town in Judah that received spoils from David's victory.
3294.s: Bethel was a town in Judah that received spoils from David's victory over the Amalekites. (<ref="1Sa.30.27">1Sa.30.27</ref>)

3295.b: Town in Asher's territory, near the border.
3295.s: Beth-emek was a town in the territory of Asher, mentioned in the description of Asher's border. (<ref="Joshua 19:27">Joshua 19:27</ref>)

3296.b: Mountain or mountains mentioned in Song of Solomon.
3296.s: Bether is a mountain or mountains mentioned in the Song of Solomon, possibly symbolizing separation between lovers. (<ref="Sng.2.17">Sng.2.17</ref>)

3297.b: Pool in Jerusalem where Jesus healed a paralyzed man.
3297.s: Bethesda (Bethzatha) was a pool in Jerusalem with five roofed colonnades, where Jesus healed a man who had been an invalid for thirty-eight years. (<ref="Jhn.5.2">Jhn.5.2</ref>)

3298.b: Town mentioned in Micah's prophecy, possibly near Jerusalem.
3298.s: Beth-ezel was a town mentioned in Micah's prophecy, where the inhabitants could not offer support or refuge during a time of judgment. (<ref="Micah 1:11">Micah 1:11</ref>)

3299.b: Town associated with the descendants of Hareph.
3299.s: Beth-gader was a town associated with the descendants of Hareph, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah. (<ref="1Ch.2.51">1Ch.2.51</ref>)

3300.b: Moabite town mentioned in Jeremiah's prophecy against Moab.
3300.s: Beth-gamul was a Moabite town mentioned in Jeremiah's prophecy against Moab, likely destroyed or captured by the Babylonians. (<ref="Jeremiah 48:23">Jeremiah 48:23</ref>)

3301.b: Town in Judah, possibly fortified, mentioned by Jeremiah.
3301.s: Beth-haccherem was a town in Judah, possibly fortified, mentioned by Jeremiah as a place to raise a signal fire.

3302.b: Place near Jezreel where Ahaziah fled from Jehu.
3302.s: Beth-haggan was a place near Jezreel where Ahaziah, king of Judah, fled from Jehu before being killed. (<ref="2Ki.9.27">2Ki.9.27</ref>)

3303.b: Town in Gad, east of the Jordan, fortified by Gad.
3303.s: Beth-haram (Beth-haran) was a town allotted to the tribe of Gad, east of the Jordan River, which they fortified.

3304.b: Town on the border between Judah and Benjamin.
3304.s: Beth-hoglah was a town on the border between Judah and Benjamin, near the northern end of the Dead Sea. (<ref="Joshua 15:6; 18:19, 21">Joshua 15:6; 18:19, 21</ref>)

3305.b: Town in Ephraim and Dan, site of a famous battle.
3305.s: Lower Beth-horon was a town allotted to Ephraim and Dan, known for a battle where the sun stood still. (Multiple references, see article for details)

3306.b: Town in Ephraim, near Lower Beth-horon.
3306.s: Upper Beth-horon was a town in Ephraim, near Lower Beth-horon, fortified by Solomon.

3307.b: Town in Moab, allotted to Reuben, mentioned in prophecy.
3307.s: Beth-jeshimoth was a town in Moab, allotted to Reuben, near where the Israelites camped and mentioned in a prophecy against Moab.

3308.b: Town in Simeon, also called Lebaoth.
3308.s: Beth-lebaoth was a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon, also known as Lebaoth. (<ref="Joshua 19:6">Joshua 19:6</ref>)

3309.b: City of David's birth and Jesus' birth.
3309.s: Bethlehem, also called Ephrath or Ephrathah, was the city where David and Jesus were born, located in Judah. (Multiple references, see article for details)

3310.b: Town in Zebulun, distinct from Bethlehem in Judah.
3310.s: Bethlehem was a town allotted to the tribe of Zebulun, distinct from the more well-known Bethlehem in Judah. (<ref="Joshua 19:15">Joshua 19:15</ref>)

3311.b: Place near Jerusalem where David stayed during Absalom's revolt.
3311.s: Beth-merhak was a place near Jerusalem where David stayed with his household during Absalom's revolt. (<ref="2Sa.15.17">2Sa.15.17</ref>)

3312.b: Fortified place in Shechem, associated with Abimelech's rule.
3312.s: Beth-millo was a fortified place in Shechem where the men of the city made Abimelech king, later becoming his enemies. (<ref="Judges 9:6, 20">Judges 9:6, 20</ref>)

3313.b: Town in Gad, east of the Jordan River.
3313.s: Beth-nimrah (Nimrah) was a town allotted to the tribe of Gad, east of the Jordan River, which they built or fortified.

3314.s: Beth-pazzez, a town within the territory allotted to the tribe of Issachar.

3315.b: Town in southern Judah, resettled after the Babylonian exile.
3315.s: Beth-pelet was a town in southern Judah, allotted to Judah and later resettled by the people of Judah after the Babylonian exile.

3316.b: Place east of the Jordan, where Moses was buried.
3316.s: Beth-peor was a place east of the Jordan River, where the Israelites camped and Moses was buried in an unknown valley.

3317.b: Village near Bethany, where Jesus began His triumphal entry.
3317.s: Bethphage was a village near Bethany, where Jesus sent His disciples to find a donkey and a colt for His triumphal entry into Jerusalem.

3318.b: Aramean city and region, allied with Ammon against David.
3318.s: Beth-rehob (Rehob) was an Aramean city and region, allied with the Ammonites against David, located near the northern border of Israel.

3319.b: Town where Jesus performed miracles, home of several disciples
3319.s: Bethsaida was a fishing village on the Sea of Galilee, notable as the hometown of several of Jesus' disciples and a place where He performed miracles.

3320.b: City in Manasseh, where Saul's body was displayed.
3320.s: Beth-shean (Beth-shan) was a city allotted to Manasseh, where the Philistines fastened Saul's body to the wall after his death. (Multiple references, see article for details)

3321.b: City in Judah, associated with the Ark's return.
3321.s: Beth-shemesh was a city allotted to Judah and the Levites, associated with the return of the Ark of the Covenant from the Philistines. (Multiple references, see article for details)

3322.s: Beth-shemesh was a border town in the territory of Issachar. (<ref="Joshua 19:22">Joshua 19:22</ref>)

3323.b: Fortified city in Naphtali, not conquered by the tribe.
3323.s: Beth-shemesh was a fortified city in the territory of Naphtali, from which the Naphtalites did not drive out the Canaanites.

3324.b: Beth-shittah, place near where Midianites fled from Gideon
3324.s: Beth-shittah, a location near where the Midianites fled after being defeated by Gideon's army.

3325.b: Town in the hill country of Judah.
3325.s: Beth-tappuah was a town allotted to Judah, located in the hill country. (<ref="Joshua 15:53">Joshua 15:53</ref>)

3326.b: Region or people group trading with Tyre, allied with Gog.
3326.s: Beth-togarmah was a region or people group that traded horses and mules with Tyre and was allied with Gog, a future enemy of Israel.

3327.b: Town in Judah, fortified by Rehoboam, repaired by Nehemiah.
3327.s: Beth-zur was a town in the hill country of Judah, fortified by Rehoboam, later repaired by Nehemiah, and associated with Maon.

3328.s: Betonim was a town allotted to the tribe of Gad in the region of Gilead.

3329.s: Bezek was the place where Saul assembled the Israelite army to fight against the Ammonites.

3330.s: Bezek was a city where the tribe of Judah defeated the Canaanites and Perizzites.

3331.b: Levitical city of refuge in Reuben
3331.s: Bezer, also called Bozrah, was a Levitical city of refuge in the territory of Reuben.

3332.s: Bilhah was a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon in southern Judah.

3333.b: A ravine or region crossed by Abner's men
3333.s: Bithron, a ravine or region traversed by Abner and his men after a battle with Joab's forces.

3334.s: Bithynia, a region in Asia Minor, where Paul attempted to go but was prevented by the Holy Spirit.

3335.b: A town in the Negev, allotted to Judah
3335.s: Biziothiah, a town in the Negev region, was allotted to the tribe of Judah.

3336.s: Bor-ashan, a town in southern Judah, was one of the places where David sent spoils from his victory over the Amalekites.

3337.s: Bozez, one of the rocky crags that Jonathan and his armor-bearer crossed to attack the Philistine garrison.

3338.b: Town in Judah, birthplace of Josiah's mother
3338.s: Bozkath was a town in Judah and the birthplace of King Josiah's mother, Jedidah.

3339.s: Bozrah was an important city in Edom, often mentioned in prophecies of judgment.

3340.s: The Broad Wall was a section of Jerusalem's wall rebuilt during Nehemiah's time.

3341.b: Southwestern boundary of the Promised Land
3341.s: The Brook of Egypt (Shihor) marked the southwestern boundary of the Promised Land.

3342.b: Eastern boundary of Jeroboam II's kingdom
3342.s: The Brook of the Arabah was the eastern boundary of King Jeroboam II's kingdom.

3343.s: The Brook of the Willows was a boundary of Moab's territory, possibly near the Wadi Zered.

3344.b: Arabian tribe, possibly descendants of Nahor
3344.s: Buz was an Arabian tribe, possibly descended from Nahor, that was threatened with judgment.

3345.s: Cabbon was a town in the lowlands of Judah.

3346.b: Name given to 20 cities by Hiram
3346.s: Cabul was the name given by Hiram, king of Tyre, to the twenty cities given to him by Solomon.

3347.s: Cabul was a border town in the territory of Asher.

3348.b: Coastal city, center of Roman rule in Judea
3348.s: Caesarea was a coastal city in Judea that served as a center of Roman administration.

3349.b: City where Peter confessed Jesus as Messiah
3349.s: Caesarea Philippi was the location where Peter acknowledged Jesus as the Messiah and Son of God.

3350.b: Ancient Assyrian city built by Nimrod
3350.s: Calah was an ancient Assyrian city built by Nimrod, along with Nineveh and Resen.

3351.s: Caleb Ephrathah was the place where Hezron, the son of Perez, died.

3352.b: Ancient Mesopotamian city, possibly Kullania or Kullanhu
3352.s: Calneh (Calno) was an ancient city in Mesopotamia, mentioned as one of Nimrod's cities and later as a trading partner of Tyre.

3353.b: Ancient region; descendants of Ham; promised to Abraham's descendants
3353.s: Canaan was the ancient region between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea, named after Noah's grandson and later promised to Abraham's descendants.

3354.b: Town in Galilee; center of Jesus' ministry
3354.s: Capernaum was a fishing village on the Sea of Galilee that served as a center for Jesus' ministry in the region.

3355.b: Island home of the Philistines; visited by Paul
3355.s: Caphtor, identified as the island of Crete, was the original homeland of the Philistines and a place visited by the apostle Paul.

3356.b: Region in Asia Minor; home to early Christian believers
3356.s: Cappadocia was a region in Asia Minor where some early Christian believers lived.

3357.b: Ancient city; site of Babylonian victory over Egypt
3357.s: Carchemish was an ancient city on the Euphrates River where the Babylonians decisively defeated the Egyptians.

3358.b: Town in Judah; home of Nabal and Abigail
3358.s: Carmel was a town in Judah, known as the home of Nabal and his wife Abigail, who later married David.

3359.b: Mountain range; site of Elijah's confrontation with prophets of Baal
3359.s: Mount Carmel was a mountain range in northern Israel where the prophet Elijah confronted the prophets of Baal.

3360.b: Place where Levites were recruited for temple service
3360.s: Casiphia was a place in Babylon where Ezra sent for Levites to join the returning exiles in Jerusalem.

3361.b: Island where Paul's ship sought shelter
3361.s: Cauda was an island where the ship carrying Paul sought shelter during a storm on his journey to Rome.

3362.b: Port of Corinth; home of Phoebe
3362.s: Cenchreae was the eastern port of Corinth, where Paul had his hair cut in connection with a vow, and was the home of Phoebe, a deaconess of the church.

3363.b: Ancient Mesopotamian empire; known for astrology and wisdom
3363.s: Chaldea was an ancient Mesopotamian empire, known for its astrologers and wise men, that played a significant role in the history of Israel, particularly during the Babylonian exile.

3364.b: River in Babylonia; location of Ezekiel's visions
3364.s: The Chebar River was a waterway in Babylonia near which the prophet Ezekiel received visions from God during the Babylonian exile.

3365.s: Chephar-ammoni was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.

3366.b: Gibeonite town; later part of Benjamin and Judah
3366.s: Chephirah was one of the Gibeonite towns that became part of the territories of Benjamin and Judah.

3367.b: Brook where Elijah hid during drought
3367.s: The Brook Cherith was where the prophet Elijah hid and was fed by ravens during a drought in Israel.

3368.b: Babylonian location; home of some returning exiles
3368.s: Cherub was a place in Babylonia from which some Jewish exiles returned to Jerusalem after the Babylonian captivity.

3369.s: Chesalon, also known as Mount Jearim, was a landmark on the northern boundary of Judah, near Bethshemesh.

3370.s: Chesil was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the southern part of their territory.

3371.b: Border town of Issachar and Zebulun
3371.s: Chesulloth, also known as Chisloth-tabor or Tabor, was a town on the border between Issachar and Zebulun.

3372.s: Chilmad was a place mentioned by Ezekiel as one of Tyre's trading partners.

3373.b: Freshwater lake in northern Israel; location of Jesus' ministry
3373.s: Chinnereth, also known as the Sea of Galilee or the Sea of Tiberias, is a freshwater lake in northern Israel where Jesus conducted much of his ministry.

3374.b: Region and city near the Sea of Galilee
3374.s: Chinneroth, also known as Chinnereth, was a region and a city near the Sea of Galilee, which was also called the Sea of Chinnereth.

3375.b: Island visited by Paul on his journey
3375.s: Chios was an island in the Aegean Sea where Paul's ship stopped during his journey to Jerusalem.

3376.s: Chitlish was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the Shephelah region.

3377.b: Town in Galilee; rebuked by Jesus for unbelief
3377.s: Chorazin was a town in Galilee that Jesus rebuked for its lack of repentance despite the mighty works he had done there.

3378.b: Province in Asia Minor; Paul's birthplace and ministry area
3378.s: Cilicia, a province in southeast Asia Minor, was the birthplace of Paul and an area where he ministered to the early churches.

3379.b: Town in the wilderness of Judah
3379.s: The City of Salt was a town located in the wilderness of Judah, near the Dead Sea.

3380.b: City on the coast of Asia Minor
3380.s: Cnidus was a city on the southwest coast of Asia Minor, where Paul's ship stopped during his journey to Rome.

3381.b: City in Phrygia; recipient of Paul's epistle
3381.s: Colossae was a city in the region of Phrygia in Asia Minor, to which Paul addressed one of his epistles.

3382.b: Offering dedicated to God; temple treasury
3382.s: Corban refers to an offering dedicated to God, which the Pharisees used to avoid supporting their parents, and also to the temple treasury.

3383.b: Ancient Greek city; recipient of Paul's epistles
3383.s: Corinth, an important city in ancient Greece, was the location of a Christian church to which Paul wrote two epistles.

3384.s: The Corner Gate was a fortified gate in Jerusalem's wall, mentioned in connection with repairs and measurements of the city.

3385.b: Island visited by Paul on his journey
3385.s: Cos was an island in the Aegean Sea where Paul's ship stopped during his return journey to Jerusalem.

3386.b: Ancient region in Africa; associated with Egypt and Babylon
3386.s: Cush, often translated as Ethiopia, was an ancient region in Africa, mentioned in various contexts throughout the Bible.

3387.b: Unknown location, possibly related to Cush
3387.s: Cushan, a location mentioned in <ref="Habakkuk 3:7">Habakkuk 3:7</ref>, is possibly related to Cush or another unidentified place.

3388.b: Babylonian city; origin of Samaritan settlers
3388.s: Cuthah was a Babylonian city from which the Assyrian king brought people to settle in Samaria after the deportation of the Israelites.

3389.b: Island in the Mediterranean Sea; early Christian community
3389.s: Cyprus, also referred to as Kittim and Elishah, was an island in the Mediterranean Sea that played a significant role in the spread of early Christianity.

3390.b: City in North Africa; home of early Christians
3390.s: Cyrene, a city in North Africa, was the hometown of Simon, who carried Jesus' cross, and several early Christians mentioned in Acts.

3391.s: Dabbesheth was a town on the border of the territory allocated to the tribe of Zebulun.

3392.s: Daberath was a Levitical city located in the territory of Issachar, later given to the Levites of the Gershonite clan.

3393.b: Region on the eastern coast of the Adriatic Sea.
3393.s: Dalmatia, a region in Illyricum where Titus traveled (<ref="2Ti.4.10">2Ti.4.10</ref>).

3394.b: Ancient city, capital of Syria, important in biblical history.
3394.s: Damascus, an ancient city in Syria, played a significant role in biblical history.

3395.b: Israelite tribe; city in northern Israel; originally called Laish/Leshem.
3395.s: Dan, an Israelite tribe and a city in northern Israel, formerly called Laish or Leshem.

3396.b: A city in the hill country of Judah.
3396.s: Dannah, a city located in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:49">Joshua 15:49</ref>).

3397.b: Canaanite city captured by Joshua and Caleb's family.
3397.s: Debir, also known as Kiriath-sannah or Kiriath-sepher, was a Canaanite city captured by Joshua and later by Caleb's family.

3398.b: A place on the northern border of Judah.
3398.s: Debir, a place on the northern border of Judah, distinct from the city of Debir (<ref="Joshua 15:7">Joshua 15:7</ref>).

3399.b: A group of ten Hellenistic cities in ancient Palestine.
3399.s: The Decapolis was a group of ten Hellenistic cities located in ancient Palestine, mentioned in the New Testament.

3400.b: An Arabian people and region, involved in trade.
3400.s: Dedan was an Arabian people and region, known for their involvement in trade.

3401.b: City in Lycaonia visited by Paul on missionary journeys.
3401.s: Derbe, a city in Lycaonia, was visited by Paul during his missionary journeys.

3402.b: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings.
3402.s: Diblathaim, also known as Almon-diblathaim or Beth-diblathaim, was a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings.

3403.b: A city in Judah, inhabited by the tribe of Judah.
3403.s: Dibon, a city in Judah, was inhabited by the tribe of Judah after the Babylonian exile (<ref="Nehemiah 11:25">Nehemiah 11:25</ref>).

3404.b: Moabite city, allotted to Gad, later possessed by Moab.
3404.s: Dibon, also known as Dibon-gad, was a Moabite city allotted to the tribe of Gad, later repossessed by Moab.

3405.b: A city in the lowlands of Judah.
3405.s: Dilean, a city located in the lowlands of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:38">Joshua 15:38</ref>).

3406.b: A Levitical city in the territory of Zebulun.
3406.s: Dimnah, also known as Rimmon or Rimmono, was a Levitical city in the territory of Zebulun.

3407.b: A city in the Negev region of Judah.
3407.s: Dimonah, a city located in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:22">Joshua 15:22</ref>).

3408.b: The capital city of Edom during Bela's reign.
3408.s: Dinhabah, the capital city of Edom during the reign of King Bela (<ref="Genesis 36:32; 1Ch.1.43">Genesis 36:32; 1Ch.1.43</ref>).

3409.b: A tree near Shechem, associated with pagan divination practices.
3409.s: The Diviners' Oak was a tree near Shechem, likely associated with pagan divination practices (<ref="Judges 9:37">Judges 9:37</ref>).

3410.b: A place near where Moses delivered his final speeches.
3410.s: Dizahab, a place near where Moses delivered his final speeches to the Israelites (<ref="Deu.1.1">Deu.1.1</ref>).

3411.b: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings.
3411.s: Dophkah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings after leaving Egypt (<ref="Numbers 33:12-13">Numbers 33:12-13</ref>).

3412.b: A Canaanite city, later allotted to Manasseh but not conquered.
3412.s: Dor, also known as Naphath-dor, was a Canaanite city allotted to Manasseh but not fully conquered (<ref="Joshua 12:23; 17:11; Judges 1:27">Joshua 12:23; 17:11; Judges 1:27</ref>).

3413.b: A place where Joseph found his brothers and was sold.
3413.s: Dothan, a place where Joseph found his brothers and was later sold into slavery (<ref="Genesis 37:17">Genesis 37:17</ref>).

3414.b: A water source near Jerusalem, mentioned in Nehemiah's wall inspection.
3414.s: The Dragon Spring was a water source near Jerusalem, mentioned during Nehemiah's inspection of the city walls (<ref="Nehemiah 2:13">Nehemiah 2:13</ref>).

3415.b: A city or region in Arabia, recipient of a prophetic oracle.
3415.s: Dumah, a city or region in Arabia, was the recipient of a prophetic oracle in <ref="Isaiah 21:11">Isaiah 21:11</ref>.

3416.b: A city in the hill country of Judah.
3416.s: Dumah, a city located in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:52">Joshua 15:52</ref>).

3417.b: A gate in Jerusalem's wall, possibly used for waste removal.
3417.s: The Dung Gate was one of the gates in Jerusalem's wall, possibly used for removing waste from the city (<ref="Nehemiah 2:13; 3:13-14; 12:31">Nehemiah 2:13; 3:13-14; 12:31</ref>).

3418.b: A plain in Babylon where Nebuchadnezzar set up a statue.
3418.s: Dura, a plain in the province of Babylon where King Nebuchadnezzar set up a golden statue (<ref="Dan.3.1">Dan.3.1</ref>).

3419.b: A direction associated with invading armies and nomadic tribes.
3419.s: In the Bible, the East is often associated with invading armies and nomadic tribes (<ref="Judges 6:3, 33; 7:12; 8:10; Ezk.25.4, 10">Judges 6:3, 33; 7:12; 8:10; Ezk.25.4, 10</ref>).

3420.b: A gate in Jerusalem's wall, near the house of Shemaiah.
3420.s: The East Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, located near the house of Shemaiah (<ref="Nehemiah 3:29">Nehemiah 3:29</ref>).

3421.b: A mountain in Canaan, site of curses and blessings ceremony.
3421.s: Mount Ebal, also known as Mount Zalmon or Mount Ephraim, was a mountain in Canaan where the Israelites held a ceremony of curses and blessings (<ref="Deu.11.29; 27:4, 13; Joshua 8:30, 33; Judges 9:48; Psalm 68:14; Jeremiah 4:15">Deu.11.29; 27:4, 13; Joshua 8:30, 33; Judges 9:48; Psalm 68:14; Jeremiah 4:15</ref>).

3422.b: A stone memorial set up by Samuel to commemorate victory.
3422.s: Ebenezer was a stone memorial set up by Samuel to commemorate Israel's victory over the Philistines (<ref="1Sa.4.1; 5:1; 7:12">1Sa.4.1; 5:1; 7:12</ref>).

3423.b: A town allotted to the tribe of Issachar.
3423.s: Ebez was a town allotted to the tribe of Issachar (<ref="Joshua 19:20">Joshua 19:20</ref>).

3424.b: A city in Media where a significant scroll was found.
3424.s: Ecbatana was a city in Media where a scroll was found containing a decree by King Cyrus (<ref="Ezra 6:2">Ezra 6:2</ref>).

3425.b: A city or region, possibly in Mesopotamia or Syria.
3425.s: Eden, a city or region mentioned in the Old Testament, possibly located in Mesopotamia or Syria (<ref="2Ki.19.12; Isaiah 37:12; Ezk.27.23">2Ki.19.12; Isaiah 37:12; Ezk.27.23</ref>).

3426.b: The perfect garden where God placed Adam and Eve.
3426.s: Eden, the perfect garden created by God, where He placed Adam and Eve (<ref="Genesis 2:8, 10, 15; 3:23-24; 4:16; Isaiah 51:3; Ezk.28.13; 31:9, 16, 18; 36:35; Jol.2.3">Genesis 2:8, 10, 15; 3:23-24; 4:16; Isaiah 51:3; Ezk.28.13; 31:9, 16, 18; 36:35; Jol.2.3</ref>).

3427.b: A town in the Negev region of Judah.
3427.s: Eder, a town located in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:21">Joshua 15:21</ref>).

3428.b: Descendants of Esau; enemy nation southeast of Israel
3428.s: Edom, a nation descended from Esau that was often in conflict with Israel.

3429.b: Amorite city defeated by Moses and the Israelites
3429.s: Edrei, an Amorite city east of the Jordan defeated by the Israelites under Moses.

3430.b: Moabite city; its destruction prophesied by Isaiah
3430.s: Eglaim, a Moabite city whose destruction was prophesied by Isaiah.

3431.b: Moabite city; its destruction prophesied by Isaiah and Jeremiah
3431.s: Eglath-shelishiyah, a Moabite city whose destruction was prophesied by Isaiah and Jeremiah.

3432.b: Amorite king of Lachish; city in Judah
3432.s: Eglon, an Amorite king of Lachish defeated by Joshua, also a city in Judah.

3433.b: Ancient nation; Israelites enslaved there; plagues and Exodus
3433.s: Egypt, a powerful nation where the Israelites were enslaved until God delivered them in the Exodus.

3434.b: Likely the Gulf of Suez, part of the Red Sea
3434.s: The Egypt Sea, probably referring to the Gulf of Suez, an arm of the Red Sea.

3435.b: One of the five major Philistine city-states
3435.s: Ekron, one of the five principal Philistine cities, located in southwestern Canaan.

3436.b: Site of David's victory over Goliath
3436.s: The Elah Valley, where David defeated the Philistine giant Goliath.

3437.b: Ancient kingdom east of Babylon; ally and enemy of Israel
3437.s: Elam, an ancient nation east of Babylon, at times an ally and at times an enemy of Israel.

3438.b: Edomite port on the Red Sea; fortified by Judah
3438.s: Elath, an Edomite port on the Red Sea, was fortified by Judah during the reigns of Solomon and Uzziah.

3439.b: Moabite city assigned to Reuben; later prophecies of destruction
3439.s: Elealeh, a Moabite city assigned to the tribe of Reuben, later featured in prophecies of Moab's destruction.

3440.b: Desert oasis on Israel's journey from Egypt to Sinai
3440.s: Elim, a desert oasis where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Mount Sinai.

3441.s: Elkosh, the hometown of the prophet Nahum, probably located in Judah.

3442.b: Mesopotamian city-state; allied with Elam against Sodom and Gomorrah
3442.s: Ellasar, a Mesopotamian city-state whose king Arioch joined Chedorlaomer of Elam in battle against Sodom and Gomorrah.

3443.b: City in the territory of Dan
3443.s: Elon, a city allotted to the tribe of Dan during the division of the Promised Land.

3444.b: City under the jurisdiction of Solomon's governor Ben-Deker
3444.s: Elonbeth-hanan, a city under the jurisdiction of Ben-Deker, one of Solomon's twelve governors.

3445.b: Wilderness area where the Horites were defeated by Chedorlaomer
3445.s: El-paran, a wilderness region where Chedorlaomer and his allies defeated the Horites during their campaign.

3446.b: City in Dan's territory; later given to the Levites
3446.s: Eltekeh, a city in Dan's territory that was later given to the Levites.

3447.b: City in the hill country of Judah
3447.s: Eltekon, a city in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in the list of cities allotted to Judah.

3448.b: A town allotted to Judah and Simeon
3448.s: Eltolad, a town allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon in the Negev region.

3449.s: Emek-keziz, a town within the territory allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.

3450.b: Emmaus, village where Jesus appeared to two disciples after resurrection
3450.s: Emmaus, a village approximately seven miles from Jerusalem, where Jesus appeared to two disciples after His resurrection.

3451.b: Enaim, place where Tamar posed as a prostitute
3451.s: Enaim, the place where Tamar sat and posed as a prostitute to deceive Judah.

3452.b: Enam, town allotted to Judah in the Shephelah
3452.s: Enam, a town in the Shephelah region, allotted to the tribe of Judah.

3453.b: Canaanite city; site of Saul's consultation with medium
3453.s: En-dor, a Canaanite city where Saul consulted a medium before his final battle with the Philistines.

3454.b: Place mentioned in Ezekiel's vision of restored Israel
3454.s: Eneglaim, a place mentioned in Ezekiel's vision of the restored land of Israel.

3455.b: City in the lowlands of Judah
3455.s: En-gannim, a city in the lowlands of Judah, mentioned in the list of cities allotted to Judah.

3456.s: En-gannim (or Anem), a Levitical city in the territory of Issachar, given to the Gershonite Levites.

3457.b: Oasis in Judah; refuge for David; Chedorlaomer's victory
3457.s: Engedi (or Hazazon-tamar), an oasis in Judah where David sought refuge from Saul, also the site of Chedorlaomer's victory.

3458.b: City allotted to the tribe of Issachar
3458.s: En-haddah, a city allotted to the tribe of Issachar during the division of the Promised Land.

3459.b: Spring that appeared after Samson's victory over the Philistines
3459.s: En-hakkore, the spring that God provided for Samson after his victory over the Philistines at Lehi.

3460.b: City allotted to the tribe of Naphtali
3460.s: En-hazor, a city allotted to the tribe of Naphtali during the division of the Promised Land.

3461.b: Spring near Jerusalem; associated with Adonijah's and David's kingships
3461.s: En-rogel, a spring near Jerusalem, was the site of Adonijah's attempt to become king and later served as a meeting place for David's supporters.

3462.b: Spring on the border between Judah and Benjamin
3462.s: En-shemesh, a spring on the border between the territories of Judah and Benjamin, near Jerusalem.

3463.b: Arabian tribe; known for their camels and dromedaries
3463.s: Ephah, an Arabian tribe known for their camels and dromedaries, mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy of nations coming to Jerusalem.

3464.b: Place where the Philistines and Israelites fought; Goliath's challenge
3464.s: Ephes-dammim (or Pas-dammim), the place where the Philistines and Israelites faced each other in battle, and where Goliath challenged the Israelites.

3465.b: Major city in Asia Minor; important center for early Christianity
3465.s: Ephesus, a major city in Asia Minor, was an important center for early Christianity and the recipient of one of Paul's epistles.

3466.b: City near the Judean wilderness; Jesus withdrew there
3466.s: Ephraim, a city near the Judean wilderness where Jesus withdrew after the raising of Lazarus.

3467.b: Gate in Jerusalem's wall, broken down by King Jehoash
3467.s: The Ephraim Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall that was broken down by King Jehoash of Israel during his conflict with King Amaziah of Judah.

3468.b: Gate in Jerusalem's wall, rebuilt during Nehemiah's time
3468.s: The Ephraim Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall that was rebuilt during Nehemiah's time and used for public gatherings and proce∟ssions.

3469.b: Mountain on the border between Judah and Benjamin
3469.s: Mount Ephron, a mountain on the border between the territories of Judah and Benjamin, near Kiriath-jearim.

3470.b: Ancient Mesopotamian city; part of Nimrod's kingdom
3470.s: Erech, an ancient Mesopotamian city that was part of Nimrod's kingdom and later inhabited by people who opposed the rebuilding of the Jerusalem Temple.

3471.b: Mountainous region of Edom; judgment prophesied by Obadiah
3471.s: Mount Esau, the mountainous region of Edom, against which the prophet Obadiah declared God's judgment for their hostility toward Israel.

3472.b: Well dug by Isaac's servants; named after quarrel
3472.s: Esek, a well dug by Isaac's servants, named after a quarrel with local herdsmen.

3473.b: City in the hill country of Judah
3473.s: Eshan, a city in the hill country of Judah, allotted to the tribe of Judah.

3474.b: Valley where Israelite spies obtained a large cluster of grapes
3474.s: The Eshcol Valley, where the Israelite spies cut down a large cluster of grapes during their reconnaissance mission in Canaan.

3475.b: City allotted to Judah and Dan; associated with Samson
3475.s: Eshtaol, a city allotted to Judah and Dan, was the hometown of Samson and the starting point of the Danite migration.

3476.b: Levitical city in Judah; received spoils from David's victory
3476.s: Eshtemoa (or Eshtemoh), a Levitical city in Judah, was the home of several individuals and received spoils from David's victory over the Amalekites.

3477.b: Villages associated with Simeon; home of Judahite clan
3477.s: Etam, a village associated with the tribe of Simeon and the home of a Judahite clan.

3478.b: City fortified by Rehoboam in Judah
3478.s: Etam, a city in Judah fortified by King Rehoboam after the division of the kingdom.

3479.b: Cliff where Samson hid after defeating the Philistines
3479.s: Etam, the cliff where Samson hid after defeating the Philistines, located in Judah.

3480.b: Wilderness area where Israelites camped during the Exodus
3480.s: Etham, a wilderness area on the edge of the desert where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to the Promised Land.

3481.b: City allotted to Judah and Simeon
3481.s: Ether, a city allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon in the Shephelah region.

3482.b: Border town of Zebulun near Neah
3482.s: Eth-kazin, a border town of Zebulun located near Neah.

3483.b: Major river in ancient Near East; boundary of Promised Land
3483.s: The Euphrates, a major river in the ancient Near East, often served as a boundary marker for the Promised Land and was the site of significant events in biblical history.

3484.b: Location where David and Jonathan planned to meet
3484.s: The Stone of Ezel, a location where David and Jonathan planned to meet and communicate secretly during David's flight from King Saul.

3485.b: City allotted to Judah and Simeon
3485.s: Ezem, a city allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon in the Negev region.

3486.b: Israelite encampment; port city on Red Sea
3486.s: Ezion-geber, an Israelite encampment during the Exodus and later a port city on the Red Sea, known for its maritime trade and shipbuilding.

3487.b: Harbor on Crete; Paul's ship stopped during journey to Rome
3487.s: Fair Havens, a harbor on the island of Crete where Paul's ship stopped during his journey to Rome.

3488.b: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; rebuilt by Hassenaah during Nehemiah's time
3488.s: The Fish Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, was rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah during Nehemiah's time and was a location of judgment and trade.

3489.b: Location of the battle between David's forces and Absalom's army
3489.s: The Forest of Ephraim, where the battle between David's forces and Absalom's army took place during Absalom's rebellion.

3490.b: Marketplace on Appian Way; Christians met Paul on journey to Rome
3490.s: The Forum of Appius, a marketplace on the Appian Way, where Christians from Rome met Paul during his journey to the city as a prisoner.

3491.b: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; location of Levite singers during coronation
3491.s: The Foundation Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, where a third of the Levite singers were positioned during the coronation of Joash.

3492.b: Gate in Jerusalem's wall; rebuilt by Shallun during Nehemiah's time
3492.s: The Fountain Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall, was rebuilt by Shallun during Nehemiah's time and was a location for processions and gatherings.

3493.b: Mountain in Ephraim; burial place of Joshua
3493.s: Gaash, a mountain in the region of Ephraim, was the burial place of Joshua and the homeland of two of David's mighty men.

3494.b: Raised stone platform in Jerusalem; location of Jesus' trial
3494.s: Gabbatha, also known as the Stone Pavement, was the location in Jerusalem where Pontius Pilate sat in judgment over Jesus.

3495.b: A region in Asia Minor, recipient of Paul's epistle.
3495.s: Galatia, a region in Asia Minor, was the recipient of Paul's epistle to the Galatians and was visited by Paul on his missionary journeys (<ref="Act.16.6; 18:23; 1Co.16.1; Galatians 1:2; 3:1; 6:18; 2Ti.4.10; 1Pe.1.1">Act.16.6; 18:23; 1Co.16.1; Galatians 1:2; 3:1; 6:18; 2Ti.4.10; 1Pe.1.1</ref>).

3496.b: Region in northern Israel; key location in Jesus' ministry
3496.s: Galilee, a region in northern Israel, was a significant location in Jesus' life and ministry, as well as the homeland of many of his disciples.

3497.b: Town in Benjamin; home of Michal's husband Paltiel
3497.s: Gallim, a town in Benjamin, was the home of Paltiel, Michal's husband, and is mentioned in a prophecy of Isaiah.

3498.b: People group; defenders of the towers of Tyre
3498.s: The Gamad were a people group mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy as defenders of the towers of Tyre.

3499.s: Gareb, a hill mentioned in <ref="Jeremiah 31:39">Jeremiah 31:39</ref>, was located near Jerusalem and was to be included within the city's future boundaries.

3500.b: Philistine city; home of Goliath; refuge for David
3500.s: Gath, one of the five major Philistine cities, was the hometown of Goliath and a place of refuge for David during his flight from Saul.

3501.b: Town in Zebulun; hometown of prophet Jonah
3501.s: Gath-hepher, a town in the territory of Zebulun, was the hometown of the prophet Jonah.

3502.b: Levitical city in Dan and Manasseh
3502.s: Gath-rimmon, a Levitical city, was allotted to the Kohathite Levites within the territories of Dan and Manasseh.

3503.b: Philistine city; Samson's exploits; Philip's ministry
3503.s: Gaza, one of the five major Philistine cities, was the site of Samson's exploits and a place visited by Philip the evangelist in the early church.

3504.s: Geba, a Levitical city in the territory of Benjamin, was located on the northern border of the kingdom of Judah (<ref="Joshua 18:24; 1Ki.15.22">Joshua 18:24; 1Ki.15.22</ref>).

3505.b: Phoenician city; skilled builders; allied against Israel
3505.s: Gebal, a Phoenician city known for its skilled builders, was allied against Israel and provided materials for Solomon's temple.

3506.b: Town in Benjamin; mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy
3506.s: Gebim, a town in Benjamin, is mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy describing the advance of the Assyrian army towards Jerusalem.

3507.b: Town in Judah; home of Baal-hanan and Jozabad
3507.s: Gederah, a town in Judah, was the home of Baal-hanan, one of David's overseers, and Jozabad, one of his mighty men.

3508.b: Town in Judah; captured by Philistines during Ahaz's reign
3508.s: Gederoth, a town in Judah, was captured by the Philistines during the reign of King Ahaz.

3509.b: Town in Judah; mentioned in list of allotted cities
3509.s: Gederothaim, a town in Judah, is mentioned in the list of cities allotted to the tribe of Judah.

3510.b: Region where Simeonites sought pasture for their flocks
3510.s: Gedor, a region where some Simeonites went to find pasture for their flocks during the reign of King Hezekiah.

3511.b: Town in Judah; home of Judahite clan members
3511.s: Gedor (or Geder), a town in the hill country of Judah, was the home of several members of Judahite clans.

3512.b: Valley of craftsmen; inhabited by Benjamites after the exile
3512.s: Ge-harashim, the Valley of Craftsmen, was inhabited by some Benjamites after the return from the Babylonian exile.

3513.b: Plain on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee
3513.s: Gennesaret, a fertile plain on the northwest shore of the Sea of Galilee, was the location of several events in Jesus' ministry.

3514.b: Philistine city; Abraham and Isaac's encounters with Abimelech
3514.s: Gerar, a Philistine city, was the location of Abraham and Isaac's encounters with Abimelech and the site of a battle during King Asa's reign.

3515.b: Region where Jesus healed a demon-possessed man
3515.s: Gerasa (or Gadara), a region southeast of the Sea of Galilee, was the location where Jesus healed a demon-possessed man.

3516.b: Mountain in Samaria; site of blessings and Jotham's parable
3516.s: Mount Gerizim, a mountain in Samaria, was designated as the site for pronouncing blessings and was the location of Jotham's parable to the men of Shechem.

3517.b: Lodging place near Bethlehem; refuge for Johanan's group
3517.s: Geruth Chimham, a lodging place near Bethlehem, served as a temporary refuge for Johanan and his group after the murder of Gedaliah.

3518.b: Aramean kingdom; Talmai's domain; refuge for Absalom
3518.s: Geshur, an Aramean kingdom ruled by Talmai, was the homeland of David's wife Maacah and a refuge for Absalom after he murdered his half-brother Amnon.

3519.b: Garden near Jerusalem; site of Jesus' prayer and arrest
3519.s: Gethsemane, a garden at the Mount of Olives, was the site where Jesus prayed and was arrested before his crucifixion.

3520.b: A Canaanite city, conquered by Joshua and later by David.

3521.b: Location near Gibeon where Joab and Abishai pursued Abner.
3521.s: Giah was a place near Gibeon where Joab and Abishai pursued Abner after the battle at the pool of Gibeon.

3522.b: A Levitical city in the territory of Dan.
3522.s: Gibbethon, a Levitical city in the territory of Dan, was the site of conflict during the reigns of Nadab and Baasha (<ref="Joshua 19:44; 21:23; 1Ki.15.27; 16:15, 17">Joshua 19:44; 21:23; 1Ki.15.27; 16:15, 17</ref>).

3523.b: A town in the hill country of Judah.
3523.s: Gibeah, a town in the hill country of Judah, was the hometown of Maacah, the mother of King Abijah (<ref="Joshua 15:57; 2Ch.13.2">Joshua 15:57; 2Ch.13.2</ref>).

3524.b: A city of Benjamin, associated with Saul and atrocities.
3524.s: Gibeah, a city of Benjamin, was the hometown of Saul and the site of infamous atrocities during the time of the judges (<ref="Judges 19-20; 1Sa.10.5, 10, 26; 15:34; Hosea 9:9; 10:9">Judges 19-20; 1Sa.10.5, 10, 26; 15:34; Hosea 9:9; 10:9</ref>).

3525.b: A place with a garrison of Philistines, near Gibeah.
3525.s: Gibeath-elohim, meaning "Hill of God," was a place near Gibeah where a garrison of Philistines was located (<ref="1Sa.10.5">1Sa.10.5</ref>).

3526.b: Hivite city that tricked Joshua into a peace treaty.
3526.s: Gibeon was a prominent Hivite city that deceived Joshua into making a peace treaty, and later became a Levitical city and site of worship.

3527.b: A place near Gibeah, associated with the Benjamite War.
3527.s: Gidom was a place near Gibeah where the Benjamites were pursued and defeated during the Benjamite War (<ref="Judges 20:45">Judges 20:45</ref>).

3528.b: A river of Eden; a spring near Jerusalem.
3528.s: Gihon refers to both a river of Eden (<ref="Genesis 2:13">Genesis 2:13</ref>) and a spring near Jerusalem (<ref="1Ki.1.33, 38, 45; 2Ch.32.30; 33:14">1Ki.1.33, 38, 45; 2Ch.32.30; 33:14</ref>).

3529.b: A mountain range where Saul and his sons died.
3529.s: Mount Gilboa was the site of a battle where Saul and his sons were killed by the Philistines (<ref="1Sa.28.4; 2Sa.1.21; 21:12">1Sa.28.4; 2Sa.1.21; 21:12</ref>).

3530.b: A mountain range where Saul and his sons died.
3530.s: Mount Gilboa was the site where Saul and his sons were killed in battle against the Philistines (<ref="1Sa.31.1, 8; 2Sa.1.6; 1Ch.10.1, 8; Judges 7:3">1Sa.31.1, 8; 2Sa.1.6; 1Ch.10.1, 8; Judges 7:3</ref>).

3531.b: Mountainous region east of Jordan; tribal territory and personal name.
3531.s: Gilead refers to a mountainous region east of the Jordan River, as well as being a personal name for several individuals in the Old Testament.

3532.b: A place associated with the prophets Elijah and Elisha.
3532.s: Gilgal, a place associated with the prophets Elijah and Elisha, was the starting point of Elijah's final journey and the location of a prophetic community (<ref="2Ki.2.1; 4:38">2Ki.2.1; 4:38</ref>).

3533.b: A significant site during Israel's early history in Canaan.
3533.s: Gilgal, also known as Geliloth, Beth-gilgal, or Gibeath-haaraloth, was a significant site during Israel's early history in Canaan, serving as a base for Joshua and a place of worship (<ref="Deu.11.30; Joshua 4:19-20; 5:3,9-10; 14:6; Judges 2:1; 11:14-15; 15:12-33; Hosea 9:15">Deu.11.30; Joshua 4:19-20; 5:3,9-10; 14:6; Judges 2:1; 11:14-15; 15:12-33; Hosea 9:15</ref>).

3534.b: A city in Judah; home of Ahithophel, David's counselor.
3534.s: Giloh, also known as Gilo, was a city in Judah and the hometown of Ahithophel, David's counselor who later conspired with Absalom (<ref="Joshua 15:51; 2Sa.15.12; 23:34">Joshua 15:51; 2Sa.15.12; 23:34</ref>).

3535.b: A city in Judah captured by the Philistines.
3535.s: Gimzo was a city in the plain of Judah that was captured by the Philistines during the reign of Ahaz (<ref="2Ch.28.18">2Ch.28.18</ref>).

3536.b: Town where Beerothites fled; later inhabited by Benjamites.
3536.s: Gittaim was a town where the Beerothites fled and was later inhabited by the Benjamites after the Babylonian exile.

3537.b: A place near Jerusalem, mentioned in a prophetic context.
3537.s: Goah was a place near Jerusalem, mentioned in the context of a prophetic description of the city's future restoration (<ref="Jeremiah 31:39">Jeremiah 31:39</ref>).

3538.b: A symbolic enemy of God's people in prophetic literature.
3538.s: Gog is mentioned in the prophetic books of Ezekiel and Revelation as a symbolic enemy of God's people who will be defeated in the end times (<ref="Ezk.38.2, 3, 14, 16, 18; 39:1, 11; Revelation 20:8">Ezk.38.2, 3, 14, 16, 18; 39:1, 11; Revelation 20:8</ref>).

3539.b: A city of refuge in Bashan, allotted to Manasseh.
3539.s: Golan was a city of refuge in Bashan, allotted to the Levites of the family of Gershon and located in the territory of the half-tribe of Manasseh (<ref="Deu.4.43; Joshua 20:8; 21:27; 1Ch.6.71">Deu.4.43; Joshua 20:8; 21:27; 1Ch.6.71</ref>).

3540.b: The place where Jesus was crucified, meaning "Place of a Skull."
3540.s: Golgotha, also known as the Place of a Skull, was the site outside Jerusalem where Jesus was crucified (<ref="Matthew 27:33; Mrk.15.22; Luke 23:33; Jhn.19.17">Matthew 27:33; Mrk.15.22; Luke 23:33; Jhn.19.17</ref>).

3541.b: Wicked city destroyed by God along with Sodom.
3541.s: Gomorrah was a wicked city in the plain of Jordan that God destroyed with sulfur and fire, along with Sodom, due to their grave sins.

3542.b: A region in Egypt where the Israelites settled and prospered.
3542.s: Goshen was the region in Egypt where Jacob and his family settled during the time of Joseph, and where the Israelites lived and prospered until the Exodus (<ref="Genesis 45:10; 46:28-29, 34; 47:1, 4, 6, 27; 50:8; Exodus 8:22; 9:26">Genesis 45:10; 46:28-29, 34; 47:1, 4, 6, 27; 50:8; Exodus 8:22; 9:26</ref>).

3543.b: A town and region in the hill country of Judah.
3543.s: Goshen was a town and region in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in the accounts of Joshua's conquests (<ref="Joshua 10:41; 11:16; 15:51">Joshua 10:41; 11:16; 15:51</ref>).

3544.b: A region in Mesopotamia where Israelite captives were deported.
3544.s: Gozan was a region in Mesopotamia where Israelite captives from the northern kingdom were deported by the Assyrians (<ref="2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 19:12; 1Ch.5.26; Isaiah 37:12">2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 19:12; 1Ch.5.26; Isaiah 37:12</ref>).

3545.b: The Mediterranean Sea, the western boundary of the Promised Land.
3545.s: The Great Sea, also known as the Sea of the Philistines, refers to the Mediterranean Sea, which formed the western boundary of the Promised Land (<ref="Numbers 34:6-7; Joshua 1:4; 9:1; 15:12, 47; 23:4; Ezk.47.10, 15, 19-20; 48:28; Exodus 23:31">Numbers 34:6-7; Joshua 1:4; 9:1; 15:12, 47; 23:4; Ezk.47.10, 15, 19-20; 48:28; Exodus 23:31</ref>).

3546.b: A nation and culture, often in opposition to Israel
3546.s: Greece (Javan), a nation and culture mentioned in both the Old and New Testaments.

3547.b: A gate in Jerusalem's wall, likely the Muster Gate.
3547.s: The Guard Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, mentioned in <ref="Nehemiah 12:39">Nehemiah 12:39</ref>, likely the same as the Muster Gate near the Temple.

3548.b: A place near Ibleam where Ahaziah was wounded.
3548.s: Gur was a place near Ibleam where Ahaziah, king of Judah, was wounded by Jehu's men while fleeing (<ref="2Ki.9.27">2Ki.9.27</ref>).

3549.b: A place inhabited by Arabians, attacked by Uzziah's army.
3549.s: Gurbaal was a place inhabited by Arabians, against whom Uzziah, king of Judah, waged war and prevailed (<ref="2Ch.26.7">2Ch.26.7</ref>).

3550.b: A river in Assyria where Israelite captives were settled.
3550.s: Habor was a river in Assyria along which the Israelite captives from the northern kingdom were settled by the Assyrians (<ref="2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 1Ch.5.26">2Ki.17.6; 18:11; 1Ch.5.26</ref>).

3551.b: A hill in the Wilderness of Ziph, near David's hideout.
3551.s: Hachilah was a hill in the Wilderness of Ziph, where David hid from Saul and where the Ziphites revealed David's location to Saul (<ref="1Sa.23.19; 26:1">1Sa.23.19; 26:1, 3</ref>).

3552.b: A place near Megiddo associated with mourning for Josiah.
3552.s: Hadad-rimmon was a place near Megiddo where a great lamentation was held for King Josiah, who was mortally wounded there.

3553.b: A town in the Shephelah region of Judah.
3553.s: Hadashah was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah, located in the Shephelah region (<ref="Joshua 15:37">Joshua 15:37</ref>).

3554.b: A town in Benjamin, resettled after the Babylonian exile.
3554.s: Hadid was a town in Benjamin, whose inhabitants returned from the Babylonian exile and resettled in the town (<ref="Ezra 2:33; Nehemiah 7:37; 11:34">Ezra 2:33; Nehemiah 7:37; 11:34</ref>).

3555.b: A region mentioned in a prophetic oracle of judgment.
3555.s: Hadrach was a region mentioned in a prophetic oracle of judgment, possibly located in Syria (<ref="Zechariah 9:1">Zechariah 9:1</ref>).

3556.b: A town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.
3556.s: Haeleph was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (<ref="Joshua 18:28">Joshua 18:28</ref>).

3557.b: A place where Israelites were exiled by the Assyrians.
3557.s: Halah was one of the places where the Assyrians settled the exiled Israelites after conquering the Northern Kingdom.

3558.b: A mountain marking the southern boundary of Joshua's conquests.
3558.s: Mount Halak was a mountain that marked the southern boundary of the territory conquered by Joshua (<ref="Joshua 11:17; 12:7">Joshua 11:17; 12:7</ref>).

3559.b: A town in the hill country of Judah.
3559.s: Halhul was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah, located in the hill country (<ref="Joshua 15:58">Joshua 15:58</ref>).

3560.b: A town allotted to the tribe of Asher.
3560.s: Hali was a town allotted to the tribe of Asher (<ref="Joshua 19:25">Joshua 19:25</ref>).

3561.b: A hall in Solomon's palace where he administered justice.
3561.s: The Hall of Judgment was a hall in Solomon's palace where he sat to judge and administer justice (<ref="1Ki.7.7">1Ki.7.7</ref>).

3562.b: A porch with pillars in Solomon's palace.
3562.s: The Hall of Pillars was a porch in Solomon's palace, measuring fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide, with a portico of pillars and a canopy.

3563.b: Another name for the Hall of Judgment in Solomon's palace.
3563.s: The Hall of the Throne was another name for the Hall of Judgment in Solomon's palace, where he sat to administer justice (<ref="1Ki.7.7">1Ki.7.7</ref>).

3564.b: A place where Chedorlaomer defeated the Zuzim in battle.
3564.s: Ham was a place where Chedorlaomer and his allies defeated the Zuzim in battle during the war of the kings (<ref="Genesis 14:5">Genesis 14:5</ref>).

3565.b: A major city and kingdom in Syria, often mentioned in the Bible.
3565.s: Hamath, also known as Hamath Rabbah or Lebo-hamath, was a significant city and kingdom in Syria, frequently mentioned in the Bible as a reference point for the northern border of Israel and in the context of political and military events (<ref="Num.13:21; Judges 3:3; 2Ki.14.25, 28; Jeremiah 39:5; 49:23; 52:9, 27">Num.13:21; Judges 3:3; 2Ki.14.25, 28; Jeremiah 39:5; 49:23; 52:9, 27</ref>).

3566.b: A fortified city and Levitical town in Naphtali.
3566.s: Hammath, also known as Hammoth-dor or Hammon, was a fortified city in Naphtali allotted to the Levites (<ref="Joshua 19:35; 21:32; 19:28; 1Ch.6.76">Joshua 19:35; 21:32; 19:28; 1Ch.6.76</ref>).

3567.b: A city in Ezekiel's vision, meaning "multitude" or "horde."
3567.s: Hamonah is a city mentioned in Ezekiel's vision (<ref="Ezk.39.16">Ezk.39.16</ref>), its name meaning "multitude" or "horde," likely referring to the burial place of Gog's army.

3568.b: A valley where Gog and his army will be buried.
3568.s: The Valley of Hamon-gog is the place where Gog and his army will be buried after their defeat, as prophesied by Ezekiel (<ref="Ezk.39.11, 15">Ezk.39.11, 15</ref>).

3569.b: An Egyptian city mentioned in a prophecy against Judah.
3569.s: Hanes was an Egyptian city to which Judah sent envoys, as mentioned in a prophecy by Isaiah (<ref="Isaiah 30:4">Isaiah 30:4</ref>).

3570.b: A border town in the territory of Zebulun.
3570.s: Hannathon was a border town in the territory allotted to the tribe of Zebulun (<ref="Joshua 19:14">Joshua 19:14</ref>).

3571.b: A place where Israelite tribes were exiled by Tiglath-pileser.
3571.s: Hara was a place, possibly in Media, where the Reubenites, Gadites, and half-tribe of Manasseh were exiled by Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria (<ref="1Ch.5.26">1Ch.5.26</ref>).

3572.b: A desert campsite during Israel's journey from Egypt.
3572.s: Haradah was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their journey through the wilderness after leaving Egypt.

3573.b: A city in Mesopotamia, associated with Abraham and his family.
3573.s: Haran was a city in Mesopotamia where Abraham and his family settled after leaving Ur, and from where Abraham later departed for Canaan (<ref="Genesis 11:31-32; 12:4-5; 27:43; 28:10; 29:4; Act.7.2, 4">Genesis 11:31-32; 12:4-5; 27:43; 28:10; 29:4; Act.7.2, 4</ref>).

3574.b: A place mentioned in Amos's prophecy against Israel.
3574.s: Harmon is a place mentioned in Amos's prophecy, possibly referring to the destination of the exiled Israelites (<ref="Amo.4.3">Amo.4.3</ref>).

3575.b: A spring near where Gideon gathered his army.
3575.s: Harod was a spring near the hill of Moreh, where Gideon gathered his army before battling the Midianites (<ref="Judges 7:1">Judges 7:1</ref>).

3576.s: Harosheth-hagoyim was a Canaanite city that served as the base for Sisera, the commander of King Jabin's army (<ref="Judg 4:2">Judg 4:2</ref>).

3577.b: A desert campsite during Israel's journey from Egypt.
3577.s: Hashmonah was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings after leaving Egypt.

3578.b: Region east of the Sea of Galilee
3578.s: Hauran was a fertile region located east of the Sea of Galilee, mentioned as part of Israel's future boundaries (<ref="Ezk.47.16">Ezk.47.16,18</ref>).

3579.b: Land near Eden with gold, bdellium, and onyx
3579.s: Havilah was a land mentioned in the description of Eden, known for its pure gold, aromatic resin (bdellium), and onyx stone (<ref="Gen.2.11-12">Gen.2.11-12</ref>).

3580.b: Region inhabited by Ishmaelites, raided by Saul
3580.s: Havilah was a region inhabited by the descendants of Ishmael (<ref="Gen.25.18">Gen.25.18</ref>), which was later raided by King Saul during his campaign against the Amalekites (<ref="1Sa.15.7">1Sa.15.7</ref>).

3581.b: Villages in Gilead captured by Jair
3581.s: Havvoth-jair were villages in Gilead captured by Jair, a leader from the tribe of Manasseh, during the Israelite conquest of the region (<ref="Num.32.41; Deut 3:14; Judg 10:4; 1Ch.2.23">Num.32.41; Deut 3:14; Judg 10:4; 1Ch.2.23</ref>).

3582.b: A town on the southern border of Canaan.
3582.s: Hazar-addar was a town on the southern border of Canaan, mentioned in the description of the land's boundaries.

3583.b: Town on the northern border of Israel
3583.s: Hazar-enan was a town located on the northern border of the Promised Land (Num.34.9-10) and the future inheritance of the tribe of Dan (<ref="Ezk.48.1">Ezk.48.1</ref>).

3584.b: Town allotted to the tribe of Judah
3584.s: Hazar-gaddah was a town in the Negev region, allotted to the tribe of Judah during the division of the Promised Land (<ref="Josh 15:27">Josh 15:27</ref>).

3585.b: Town allotted to Judah and Simeon
3585.s: Hazar-shual was a town in the Negev allotted to Judah (<ref="Josh 15:28">Josh 15:28</ref>), later given to the tribe of Simeon (<ref="Josh 19:3; 1Ch.4.28">Josh 19:3; 1Ch.4.28</ref>), and inhabited by Jews after the Babylonian exile (<ref="Neh.11.27">Neh.11.27</ref>).

3586.b: Town allotted to the tribe of Simeon
3586.s: Hazar-susah was a town in the Negev region, allotted to the tribe of Simeon during the division of the Promised Land (<ref="Josh 19:5">Josh 19:5</ref>).

3587.b: A town allotted to the tribe of Simeon.
3587.s: Hazar-susim was a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon, mentioned in the list of their cities in 1 Chronicles.

3588.b: Place on the ideal border of Israel
3588.s: Hazer-hatticon, meaning "the middle village," was a place named on the ideal border of Israel in Ezekiel's vision (<ref="Ezk.47.16">Ezk.47.16</ref>), likely identical to Hazar-enan.

3589.s: Hazerim, meaning "villages," refers to the settlements inhabited by the Avvim, a people group dispossessed by the Caphtorim (<ref="Deut 2:23">Deut 2:23</ref>).

3590.b: Israelite encampment during the wilderness wanderings
3590.s: Hazeroth was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings, mentioned in the context of Moses' leadership challenges (<ref="Num.11.35; 12:16; 33:17-18; Deut 1:1">Num.11.35; 12:16; 33:17-18; Deut 1:1</ref>).

3591.b: Region in Arabia, possibly Ituraea, threatened by Nebuchadnezzar
3591.s: Hazor refers to a region in Arabia, possibly Ituraea, against which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, launched a military campaign (<ref="Jer.49.28,30,33">Jer.49.28,30,33</ref>).

3592.b: Major Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
3592.s: Hazor was a major Canaanite city, whose king Jabin led a coalition against Israel; it was captured and destroyed by Joshua (<ref="Josh 11:1,10-11,13">Josh 11:1,10-11,13</ref>), later oppressing Israel before being defeated by Deborah and Barak (<ref="Judg 4:2">Judg 4:2,17</ref>).

3593.b: A town in the southland of Judah.
3593.s: Hazor was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the Negev region.

3594.b: Town in the Negev region of Judah
3594.s: Hazor was a town in the Negev region, part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah (<ref="Josh 15:23">Josh 15:23</ref>).

3595.b: Town resettled by Benjamites after the Babylonian exile
3595.s: Hazor was a town resettled by the Benjamites after their return from the Babylonian exile (<ref="Neh.11.33">Neh.11.33</ref>).

3596.b: Town in the Negev region of Judah
3596.s: Hazor-hadattah, meaning "New Hazor," was a town in the Negev region, part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah (<ref="Josh 15:25">Josh 15:25</ref>).

3597.b: An important city in Judah; burial place of patriarchs.
3597.s: Hebron, also known as Kiriath-arba, was a significant city in Judah, associated with the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and later became a Levitical city and a city of refuge.

3598.b: Valley near Hebron where Joseph sought his brothers
3598.s: The Hebron Valley was the location where Joseph was sent by his father, Jacob, to check on his brothers who were pasturing their flocks near Shechem (<ref="Gen.37.14">Gen.37.14</ref>).

3599.b: Place where David defeated the Arameans
3599.s: Helam was the location of a battle between David's forces and the Arameans, where David defeated Hadadezer, king of Zobah, and his allies (<ref="2Sa.10.16-17">2Sa.10.16-17</ref>).

3600.b: Canaanite town not conquered by the tribe of Asher
3600.s: Helbah was a Canaanite town that the tribe of Asher failed to conquer during the period of the judges (<ref="Judg 1:31">Judg 1:31</ref>).

3601.b: City known for its fine wine
3601.s: Helbon was a city mentioned in <ref="Ezk.27.18">Ezk.27.18</ref> as a trading partner of Tyre, known for its fine wine.

3602.b: A place or people mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy.
3602.s: Helech was either a place, possibly in Cilicia, or a term referring to the army of Tyre, mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy against Tyre.

3603.s: Heleph was a town marking the border of the territory allocated to the tribe of Naphtali (<ref="Josh 19:33">Josh 19:33</ref>).

3604.b: Levitical city in the territory of Asher
3604.s: Helkath (or Hukok) was a city allocated to the Levites within the territory of the tribe of Asher (<ref="Josh 19:25; 21:31; 1Ch.6.75">Josh 19:25; 21:31; 1Ch.6.75</ref>).

3605.b: Site of a battle between David's and Ish-bosheth's men
3605.s: Helkath-hazzurim, meaning "Field of Swords," was the site of a battle between David's men and those of Ish-bosheth, resulting in Abner's defeat (<ref="2Sa.2.16">2Sa.2.16</ref>).

3606.s: Hena was a Mesopotamian city conquered by the Assyrians before the time of Sennacherib, possibly located near Sippara (<ref="2Ki.18.34; 19:13; Isa.37.13">2Ki.18.34; 19:13; Isa.37.13</ref>).

3607.b: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua; later a Solomonic district.
3607.s: Hepher was a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua and later became part of a district under Solomon's rule.

3608.b: Place near where Gideon defeated the Midianites
3608.s: Heres was a place near the site where Gideon and his men defeated the Midianites (<ref="Judg 8:13">Judg 8:13</ref>).

3609.b: Forest where David hid from Saul
3609.s: The forest of Hereth was where David sought refuge when fleeing from King Saul (<ref="1Sa.22.5">1Sa.22.5</ref>).

3610.b: Mountain on the northern border of Israel
3610.s: Mount Hermon, also known as Baal-hermon, Baal-hamon, Baal-gad, Senir, or Sirion, was a prominent mountain on the northern border of Israel (<ref="Deut 3:8-9; 4:48; Josh 11:3,17; 12:1,5,7; 13:5,11; 1Ch.5.23; Psa.29.6; 42:6; 89:12; 133:3; Sng.4.8; 8:11; Jer.18.14; Ezk.27.5">Deut 3:8-9; 4:48; Josh 11:3,17; 12:1,5,7; 13:5,11; 1Ch.5.23; Psa.29.6; 42:6; 89:12; 133:3; Sng.4.8; 8:11; Jer.18.14; Ezk.27.5</ref>).

3611.b: Amorite city conquered by Moses, allotted to Reuben
3611.s: Heshbon, an Amorite city conquered by Moses (<ref="Num.21.25-30">Num.21.25-30</ref>), was allotted to Reuben (<ref="Num.32.37; Josh 13:17">Num.32.37; Josh 13:17</ref>) but later given to the Levites (<ref="Josh 21:39">Josh 21:39</ref>); it was a significant city in the region (<ref="Isa.15.4; 16:8-9; Jer.48.2, 34, 45; 49:3">Isa.15.4; 16:8-9; Jer.48.2, 34, 45; 49:3</ref>).

3612.b: A town in the southland of Judah.
3612.s: Heshmon was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the Negev region.

3613.b: Place on the northern border of Israel
3613.s: Hethlon was a place on the northern border of Israel, mentioned in Ezekiel's vision of the restored land (<ref="Ezk.47.15; 48:1">Ezk.47.15; 48:1</ref>).

3614.b: City in Phrygia, home to a Christian community
3614.s: Hierapolis, a city in Phrygia, was home to a Christian community mentioned by Paul in his letter to the Colossians (<ref="Col.4.13">Col.4.13</ref>).

3615.b: Place north of Damascus pursued by Abraham
3615.s: Hobah was a place north of Damascus where Abraham pursued the defeated army of Chedorlaomer after rescuing Lot (<ref="Gen.14.15">Gen.14.15</ref>).

3616.s: Holon, a city of Moab mentioned in Jeremiah's oracle against Moab.

3617.b: Levitical city in the hill country of Judah
3617.s: Holon, a Levitical city in Judah's hill country, also called Hilen.

3618.b: The inner sanctuary of the Tabernacle and Temple
3618.s: The Holy Place was the inner sanctuary of the Tabernacle and Temple.

3619.b: Mountain where Aaron died and was buried
3619.s: Mount Hor, where Aaron died and was buried during Israel's wilderness journey.

3620.b: A mountain marking Israel's northern boundary
3620.s: Mount Hor, a mountain at the northern extent of Israel's inheritance.

3621.s: Horem, a fortified city in the territory of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 19:38">Joshua 19:38</ref>).

3622.b: A wilderness area where David hid from Saul
3622.s: Horesh, a wilderness area in Judah where David hid from Saul.

3623.b: An Israelite campsite during the wilderness wanderings
3623.s: Hor-haggidgad (Gudgodah), an Israelite campsite between Bene-jaakan and Jotbathah.

3624.b: A Moabite city mentioned in prophecies of judgment
3624.s: Horonaim, a Moabite city featured in prophecies against Moab.

3625.b: A gate in Jerusalem's wall near the temple
3625.s: The Horse Gate, a gate in Jerusalem's wall near the temple.

3626.s: Hosah, a Levitical city on the border of Asher (<ref="Joshua 19:29">Joshua 19:29</ref>).

3627.b: A building in Solomon's palace complex
3627.s: The House of the Forest of Lebanon, a building in Solomon's palace.

3628.b: A town on the border of Naphtali
3628.s: Hukkok, a town on the border of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 19:34">Joshua 19:34</ref>).

3629.b: A town in the hill country of Judah
3629.s: Humtah, a town in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:54">Joshua 15:54</ref>).

3630.s: Ibleam (Bileam, Gath-rimmon), a Levitical city in Issachar.

3631.b: A city in Asia Minor visited by Paul
3631.s: Iconium, a city in Asia Minor where Paul preached the gospel.

3632.s: Idalah, a town in the territory of Zebulun (<ref="Joshua 19:15">Joshua 19:15</ref>).
