3633.s: Idumea, a region south of Judea, inhabited by Edomites.

3634.b: A town in the Negev of Judah
3634.s: Iim, a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:29">Joshua 15:29</ref>).

3635.b: A town in northern Israel conquered by Assyria
3635.s: Ijon (Jaan), a town in northern Israel conquered by the Assyrians.

3636.b: A region where Paul preached the gospel
3636.s: Illyricum, a region where Paul preached the gospel (<ref="Romans 15:19">Romans 15:19</ref>).

3637.b: A place from which exiles returned to Jerusalem
3637.s: Immer, a place from which exiles returned to Jerusalem (<ref="Ezra 2:59; Nehemiah 7:61">Ezra 2:59; Nehemiah 7:61</ref>).

3638.b: The eastern extent of Ahasuerus' Persian Empire
3638.s: India, the eastern extent of Ahasuerus' Persian Empire (<ref="Esther 1:1; 8:9">Esther 1:1; 8:9</ref>).

3639.b: A town in the Shephelah of Judah
3639.s: Iphtah, a town in the Shephelah region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:43">Joshua 15:43</ref>).

3640.b: A valley on the border of Zebulun and Asher
3640.s: The Iphtahel Valley, on the border between Zebulun and Asher (<ref="Joshua 19:14, 27">Joshua 19:14, 27</ref>).

3641.b: A town associated with the descendants of Eshton
3641.s: Ir-nahash, a town associated with the descendants of Eshton (<ref="1Ch.4.12">1Ch.4.12</ref>).

3642.s: Irpeel, a town in the territory of Benjamin (<ref="Joshua 18:27">Joshua 18:27</ref>).

3643.b: A region in southern Europe, home to the Roman Empire
3643.s: Italy, a region in southern Europe, home to the Roman Empire.

3644.s: Ithlah, a town in the territory of Dan (<ref="Joshua 19:42">Joshua 19:42</ref>).

3645.b: A town in the Negev of Judah
3645.s: Ithnan, a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:23">Joshua 15:23</ref>).

3646.b: City conquered by Assyria, people resettled in Samaria.
3646.s: Ivvah (or Avva) was a city conquered by Assyria, whose people were resettled in Samaria. (<ref="2Ki.18.34, 19:13; Isaiah 37:13; 2Ki.17.24, 31">2Ki.18.34, 19:13; Isaiah 37:13; 2Ki.17.24, 31</ref>)

3647.s: Iye-abarim, an Israelite campsite on the border of Moab (<ref="Numbers 21:11; 33:44">Numbers 21:11; 33:44</ref>).

3648.b: An Israelite campsite in the wilderness
3648.s: Iyim, an Israelite campsite during the wilderness journey (<ref="Numbers 33:45">Numbers 33:45</ref>).

3649.b: A river east of the Jordan, associated with Jacob
3649.s: The Jabbok, a river east of the Jordan, where Jacob wrestled with God.

3650.b: A town in Gilead, loyal to Saul
3650.s: Jabesh-gilead, a town in Gilead known for its loyalty to King Saul.

3651.b: A place associated with the families of scribes
3651.s: Jabez, a place associated with the families of scribes (<ref="1Ch.2.55">1Ch.2.55</ref>).

3652.b: A town on the border of Judah, later fortified
3652.s: Jabneel (Jabneh), a town on the border of Judah, later fortified by Uzziah.

3653.b: A town on the border of Naphtali
3653.s: Jabneel, a town on the border of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 19:33">Joshua 19:33</ref>).

3654.b: A town in the Negev of Judah
3654.s: Jagur, a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:21">Joshua 15:21</ref>).

3655.b: A town in Moab, site of Israelite victories
3655.s: Jahaz (Jahzah), a Moabite town where the Israelites defeated Sihon and later allotted to Reuben.

3656.b: An Israelite who possessed towns in Gilead
3656.s: Jair, an Israelite who possessed towns in Gilead (<ref="Joshua 13:30">Joshua 13:30</ref>).

3657.b: A place mentioned in the Septuagint
3657.s: Janen, a place mentioned in the Septuagint version of <ref="Numbers 21:19">Numbers 21:19</ref>.

3658.b: A town in the hill country of Judah
3658.s: Janim, a town in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:53">Joshua 15:53</ref>).

3659.b: A town captured by the Assyrians from Israel
3659.s: Janoah, a town captured by the Assyrians during the reign of Pekah, king of Israel (<ref="2Ki.15.29">2Ki.15.29</ref>).

3660.b: A town on the border of Ephraim
3660.s: Janoah, a town on the border of Ephraim's territory (<ref="Joshua 16:6,7">Joshua 16:6,7</ref>).

3661.b: A town on the border of Zebulun
3661.s: Japhia, a town on the border of Zebulun's territory (<ref="Joshua 19:12">Joshua 19:12</ref>).

3662.b: A Canaanite city, later allotted to Judah
3662.s: Jarmuth, a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua, later allotted to Judah.

3663.s: Jarmuth, a Levitical city in the territory of Issachar (<ref="Joshua 21:29">Joshua 21:29</ref>).

3664.b: A town in the hill country of Judah
3664.s: Jattir, a town in the hill country of Judah, later a Levitical city.

3665.b: A town in Gilead, allotted to Gad
3665.s: Jazer, a town in Gilead, allotted to Gad, known for its fertile land and vineyards.

3666.b: A poetic reference to the abundant vineyards of Jazer
3666.s: The Sea of Jazer, a poetic reference to the abundant vineyards of Jazer (<ref="Jeremiah 48:32">Jeremiah 48:32</ref>).

3667.s: Jehud, a town allotted to the tribe of Dan (<ref="Joshua 19:45">Joshua 19:45</ref>).

3668.b: A town in Judah inhabited after the Babylonian exile
3668.s: Jekabzeel, a town in Judah inhabited by the people of Judah after the Babylonian exile (<ref="Nehemiah 11:25">Nehemiah 11:25</ref>).

3669.b: A place mentioned in the Septuagint version of Joshua
3669.s: Jemnath, a place mentioned in the Septuagint version of <ref="Joshua 15:46">Joshua 15:46</ref>.

3670.b: An ancient city in Canaan, famously conquered by Israel
3670.s: Jericho, an ancient Canaanite city famously conquered by the Israelites under Joshua's leadership.

3671.b: The valley where the city of Jericho is located
3671.s: The Jericho Valley, the location of the ancient city of Jericho (<ref="Deu.34.3">Deu.34.3</ref>).

3672.b: A wilderness where Jehoshaphat defeated his enemies
3672.s: The Wilderness of Jeruel, where Jehoshaphat and Judah defeated their enemies (<ref="2Ch.20.16">2Ch.20.16</ref>).

3673.b: The capital of Israel, a holy city for three religions
3673.s: Jerusalem, the capital of Israel and a holy city for Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

3674.b: A town captured by Abijah from Jeroboam
3674.s: Jeshanah, a town captured by King Abijah of Judah from Jeroboam of Israel (<ref="2Ch.13.19">2Ch.13.19</ref>).

3675.b: A wilderness near Ziph, where David hid from Saul
3675.s: Jeshimon, a wilderness near Ziph where David hid from Saul (<ref="1Sa.23.19, 24; 26:1, 3">1Sa.23.19, 24; 26:1, 3</ref>).

3676.b: A town in Judah inhabited after the Babylonian exile
3676.s: Jeshua, a town in Judah inhabited by the people of Judah after the Babylonian exile (<ref="Nehemiah 11:26">Nehemiah 11:26</ref>).

3677.b: A descendant of Ishmael and a region in Syria
3677.s: Jetur, a descendant of Ishmael, also a region (Ituraea) mentioned in the New Testament.

3678.b: A son of Saul's son Jonathan, also called Merib-baal
3678.s: Jezreel, a son of Jonathan, who was also known as Merib-baal (<ref="2Sa.4.4">2Sa.4.4</ref>).

3679.b: A town in Judah, home of David's wife Ahinoam
3679.s: Jezreel, a town in Judah, home of Ahinoam, one of David's wives (<ref="Joshua 15:56; 1Sa.25.43">Joshua 15:56; 1Sa.25.43</ref>).

3680.b: A city in Issachar, associated with Ahab and Jezebel
3680.s: Jezreel, a city in Issachar, known for its association with King Ahab and Queen Jezebel.

3681.b: A fertile valley in northern Israel, site of many battles
3681.s: The Jezreel Valley, a strategically important and fertile valley in northern Israel, was the site of several significant battles in the Bible.

3682.b: A town in Gilead, fortified by the Gadites
3682.s: Jogbehah, a town in Gilead fortified by the Gadites (<ref="Numbers 32:35">Numbers 32:35</ref>), was located near the route Gideon took when pursuing the Midianites (<ref="Judges 8:11">Judges 8:11</ref>).

3683.b: A town in the hill country of Judah
3683.s: Jokdeam, a town in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:56">Joshua 15:56</ref>).

3684.b: A Canaanite city, later a Levitical city in Zebulun
3684.s: Jokneam (or Jokmeam), a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua, later allotted to the Levites within the territory of Zebulun.

3685.b: A town in the Shephelah region of Judah
3685.s: Joktheel, a town in the Shephelah (lowland) region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:38">Joshua 15:38</ref>).

3686.b: An ancient seaport, the main port for Jerusalem
3686.s: Joppa, an ancient seaport on the Mediterranean coast, served as the main port for Jerusalem in biblical times.

3687.b: A river and region, significant in Israel's history
3687.s: The Jordan River and its surrounding region played a significant role in the history of Israel, from the time of the patriarchs to the New Testament era.

3688.b: The hometown of Amon's mother, Meshullemeth
3688.s: Jotbah, the hometown of Meshullemeth; mother of King Amon of Judah (<ref="2Ki.21.19">2Ki.21.19</ref>).

3689.b: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey
3689.s: Jotbathah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey, known for its streams of water (<ref="Numbers 33:33-34; Deu.10.7">Numbers 33:33-34; Deu.10.7</ref>).

3690.b: The southern region of Israel, centered around Jerusalem
3690.s: Judea, the southern region of Israel, was the center of Jewish life and culture in biblical times, with Jerusalem as its capital.

3691.b: A town in the hill country of Judah, a Levitical city
3691.s: Juttah, a town in the hill country of Judah, was designated as a Levitical city (<ref="Joshua 15:55; 21:16">Joshua 15:55; 21:16</ref>).

3692.b: A town in the Negev, home of Benaiah
3692.s: Kabzeel, a town in the Negev, was the hometown of Benaiah, one of David's mighty men (<ref="Joshua 15:21; 2Sa.23.20; 1Ch.11.22">Joshua 15:21; 2Sa.23.20; 1Ch.11.22</ref>).

3693.b: A place visited during David's census of Israel
3693.s: Kadesh, a place visited by Joab during David's census of Israel (<ref="2Sa.24.6">2Sa.24.6</ref>).

3694.b: An important oasis in the Wilderness of Zin
3694.s: Kadesh (Kadesh-barnea, En-mishpat), an important oasis in the Wilderness of Zin, was a key location during the Israelites' wilderness wanderings.

3695.b: A town in the hill country of Judah
3695.s: Kain, a town in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:57">Joshua 15:57</ref>), is possibly associated with the Kenites mentioned in <ref="Numbers 24:22">Numbers 24:22</ref>.

3696.b: The burial place of Jair, a judge of Israel
3696.s: Kamon, a city in Gilead where Jair, a judge of Israel, was buried (<ref="Judges 10:5">Judges 10:5</ref>).

3697.b: A brook marking the border between Ephraim and Manasseh
3697.s: The Brook of Kanah formed part of the border between the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh (<ref="Joshua 16:8; 17:9">Joshua 16:8; 17:9</ref>).

3698.b: Town in Asher's territory; village where Jesus performed miracles
3698.s: Kanah was a border town in Asher's territory, while Cana was the village in Galilee where Jesus performed his first miracle.

3699.b: A place on the southern border of Judah
3699.s: Karka, a location along the southern border of the tribe of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:3">Joshua 15:3</ref>).

3700.b: A place where Gideon defeated Zebah and Zalmunna
3700.s: Karkor, the place where Gideon defeated the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna (<ref="Judges 8:10">Judges 8:10</ref>).

3701.b: A Levitical city in the territory of Naphtali
3701.s: Kartan, a city given to the Levites within the territory of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 21:32">Joshua 21:32</ref>).

3702.b: A town in Moab, later a Levitical city in Reuben
3702.s: Kedemoth, a town in Moab from which Moses sent messengers to Sihon, later became a Levitical city within the territory of Reuben (<ref="Deu.2.26; Joshua 13:18; 21:37; 1Ch.6.79">Deu.2.26; Joshua 13:18; 21:37; 1Ch.6.79</ref>).

3703.b: A Canaanite city, later a Levitical city of refuge in Naphtali
3703.s: Kedesh (Kedesh-naphtali), a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua, became a Levitical city and a city of refuge in the territory of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 12:22; 19:37; 20:7; 21:32">Joshua 12:22; 19:37; 20:7; 21:32</ref>).

3704.b: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey
3704.s: Kehelathah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings after leaving Mount Sinai (<ref="Numbers 33:22-23">Numbers 33:22-23</ref>).

3705.b: A town in the Shephelah of Judah, rescued by David
3705.s: Keilah, a town in the Shephelah of Judah, was rescued by David from Philistine attack but later threatened to betray him to Saul (<ref="Joshua 15:44; 1Samuel 23">Joshua 15:44; 1Samuel 23</ref>).

3706.b: A city in Gilead, captured by Nobah and renamed
3706.s: Kenath, a city in Gilead captured by Nobah and renamed after himself, was later recaptured by Geshur and Aram (<ref="Numbers 32:42; Judges 8:11; 1Ch.2.23">Numbers 32:42; Judges 8:11; 1Ch.2.23</ref>).

3707.b: A town in the Negev region of Judah
3707.s: Kerioth-hezron, also known as Hazor, was a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:25">Joshua 15:25</ref>).

3708.b: A place where the Israelites complained and were punished
3708.s: Kibroth-hattaavah, meaning "graves of craving," was a place where the Israelites complained about the lack of meat and were punished with a plague (<ref="Numbers 11:34-35; 33:16-17; Deu.9.22">Numbers 11:34-35; 33:16-17; Deu.9.22</ref>).

3709.b: A Levitical city in the territory of Ephraim
3709.s: Kibzaim, also known as Jokmeam, was a Levitical city within the territory of Ephraim (<ref="Joshua 21:22; 1Ch.6.68">Joshua 21:22; 1Ch.6.68</ref>).

3710.b: A valley east of Jerusalem, site of significant events
3710.s: The Kidron Valley, also known as the Valley of Jehoshaphat, is located east of Jerusalem and was the site of several significant events in the Bible.

3711.b: A town in the Negev region of Judah
3711.s: Kinah, a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:22">Joshua 15:22</ref>).

3712.b: An ancient trade route through Edom and Moab
3712.s: The King's Highway, an ancient trade route through Edom and Moab, was the path the Israelites sought to use during their journey to Canaan (<ref="Numbers 20:17; 21:22">Numbers 20:17; 21:22</ref>).

3713.b: A valley near Salem (Jerusalem), site of significant events
3713.s: The King's Valley, located near Salem (Jerusalem), was the site where Melchizedek met Abraham and where Absalom erected a pillar for himself (<ref="Genesis 14:17; 2Sa.18.18">Genesis 14:17; 2Sa.18.18</ref>).

3714.b: A Moabite city, later destroyed by the Babylonians
3714.s: Kir, also known as Mizpeh, was a Moabite city that faced destruction by the Babylonians (<ref="Isaiah 15:1; Jeremiah 48:1">Isaiah 15:1; Jeremiah 48:1, 23</ref>).

3715.b: A city or region in Mesopotamia, possibly Elam
3715.s: Kir, a city or region in Mesopotamia, possibly Elam, was the place where the Arameans were exiled and from where they originally came (<ref="2Ki.16.9; Amo.9.7">2Ki.16.9; Amo.9.7</ref>).

3716.s: Kiriathaim, a Levitical city in the territory of Reuben (<ref="1Ch.6.76">1Ch.6.76</ref>).

3717.b: A Moabite city, later allotted to Reuben
3717.s: Kiriathaim, also known as Kerioth, was a Moabite city later allotted to the tribe of Reuben (<ref="Numbers 32:37; Joshua 13:19; Jeremiah 48:1">Numbers 32:37; Joshua 13:19; Jeremiah 48:1, 23</ref>).

3718.s: Kiriath-huzoth, a place where Balak took Balaam (<ref="Numbers 22:39">Numbers 22:39</ref>).

3719.b: A city where the ark resided
3719.s: Kiriath-jearim, a city where the ark of the covenant resided for 20 years (<ref="1Sa.7.1-2">1Sa.7.1-2</ref>).

3720.s: Kishion (Kedesh), a Levitical city in the territory of Issachar (<ref="Joshua 19:20, 21:28; 1Ch.6.72">Joshua 19:20, 21:28; 1Ch.6.72</ref>).

3721.s: Kishon, a river in northern Israel, where Deborah and Barak defeated Sisera's army (<ref="Judges 4:7, 13; 5:21">Judges 4:7, 13; 5:21</ref>).

3722.b: A city in Zebulun not conquered
3722.s: Kitron (Kartah or Kattath), a city in Zebulun that was not conquered by the tribe (<ref="Judges 1:30; Joshua 21:34, 19:15">Judges 1:30; Joshua 21:34, 19:15</ref>).

3723.b: A people group mentioned by Ezekiel
3723.s: Koa, a people group mentioned by Ezekiel (<ref="Ezk.23.23">Ezk.23.23</ref>).

3724.s: Kue, a place from which Solomon obtained horses (<ref="1Ki.10.28; 2Ch.1.16">1Ki.10.28; 2Ch.1.16</ref>).

3725.b: A place Moses spoke to Israel
3725.s: Laban, a place where Moses spoke to the Israelites (<ref="Deu.1.1">Deu.1.1</ref>).

3726.s: Lachish, a fortified city in Judah, captured by Joshua and later by the Assyrians (<ref="Joshua 10; 2Ki.18.14, 19:8">Joshua 10; 2Ki.18.14, 19:8</ref>).

3727.b: A city in the lowlands of Judah
3727.s: Lahmam, a city in the lowlands of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:40">Joshua 15:40</ref>).

3728.b: A place near Anathoth and Gallim
3728.s: Laishah, a place near Anathoth and Gallim, mentioned in a prophecy of Isaiah (<ref="Isaiah 10:30">Isaiah 10:30</ref>).

3729.s: Lakkum, a border town of the tribe of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 19:33">Joshua 19:33</ref>).

3730.s: Laodicea, a city in Asia Minor, known for its lukewarm faith (<ref="Revelation 3:14-16">Revelation 3:14-16</ref>).

3731.b: A city near Fair Havens, Crete
3731.s: Lasea, a city near Fair Havens on the island of Crete (<ref="Act.27.8">Act.27.8</ref>).

3732.b: A place marking Canaanite territory; a stop in Israel's journey
3732.s: Lasha (Nahaliel), a place marking the extent of Canaanite territory (<ref="Genesis 10:19">Genesis 10:19</ref>) and a stop in Israel's wilderness journey (<ref="Numbers 21:19">Numbers 21:19</ref>).

3733.b: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
3733.s: Lasharon, a Canaanite city whose king was defeated by Joshua (<ref="Joshua 12:18">Joshua 12:18</ref>).

3734.b: A mountainous region known for its cedar trees
3734.s: Lebanon, a mountainous region north of Israel, known for its cedar trees and as a symbol of strength and beauty (<ref="1Ki.4.33; Psalm 92:12">1Ki.4.33; Psalm 92:12</ref>).

3735.b: A mountain range marking the northern border of Israel
3735.s: Mount Lebanon, a mountain range marking the northern border of the Promised Land (<ref="Judges 3:3">Judges 3:3</ref>).

3736.b: A valley in the Promised Land conquered by Joshua
3736.s: The Valley of Lebanon, a valley in the Promised Land conquered by Joshua (<ref="Joshua 11:17; 12:7">Joshua 11:17; 12:7</ref>).

3737.b: A town in the Negev of Judah
3737.s: Lebaoth, a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:32">Joshua 15:32</ref>).

3738.b: A place near Shiloh in Ephraim
3738.s: Lebonah, a place near Shiloh in the territory of Ephraim (<ref="Judges 21:19">Judges 21:19</ref>).

3739.b: A place where Samson fought the Philistines
3739.s: Lehi, a place where Samson fought against the Philistines and God provided him with water (<ref="Judges 15:9, 14, 19">Judges 15:9, 14, 19</ref>).

3740.b: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua; a Levitical city
3740.s: Libnah, a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua (<ref="Joshua 10:29-30">Joshua 10:29-30</ref>) and later designated as a Levitical city (<ref="Joshua 21:13">Joshua 21:13</ref>).

3741.b: A place where Israel camped in the wilderness
3741.s: Libnah, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey (<ref="Numbers 33:20-21">Numbers 33:20-21</ref>).

3742.s: Libya (Put or Pul), a country in North Africa mentioned in various Old Testament prophecies (<ref="Ezk.30.5; 38:5; Nam.3.9">Ezk.30.5; 38:5; Nam.3.9</ref>).

3743.b: A city in Benjamin; home of Aeneas healed by Peter
3743.s: Lod (Lydda), a city in the territory of Benjamin (<ref="1Ch.8.12">1Ch.8.12</ref>), where Peter healed Aeneas <ref="(Act.9.32-35">(Act.9.32-35</ref>).

3744.b: A town in Gilead; home of Mephibosheth
3744.s: Lo-debar (Debir), a town in Gilead where Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, lived (<ref="2Sa.9.4-5">2Sa.9.4-5</ref>).

3745.s: Luhith, a place in Moab mentioned in prophecies of Isaiah and Jeremiah (<ref="Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:5">Isaiah 15:5; Jeremiah 48:5</ref>).

3746.b: A Canaanite city; a man built another city named Luz
3746.s: Luz, a Canaanite city that was destroyed, and another city built by a man who had betrayed the first Luz (<ref="Judges 1:26">Judges 1:26</ref>).

3747.b: A region in Asia Minor; Paul and Barnabas preached there
3747.s: Lycaonia, a region in Asia Minor where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel (<ref="Act.14.6, 11">Act.14.6, 11</ref>).

3748.b: A region on the southwest coast of Asia Minor
3748.s: Lycia, a region on the southwest coast of Asia Minor, passed by Paul on his journey to Rome (<ref="Act.27.5">Act.27.5</ref>).

3749.b: A city in Lycaonia; Paul and Barnabas preached there
3749.s: Lystra, a city in Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas preached and Paul healed a lame man (<ref="Act.14.6-21">Act.14.6-21</ref>).

3750.s: Maacah (Maacath), a region near Geshur (<ref="Deu.3.14; Joshua 12:5">Deu.3.14; Joshua 12:5</ref>).

3751.b: A town in the hill country of Judah
3751.s: Maarath, a town in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:59">Joshua 15:59</ref>).

3752.b: A place near Gibeah where an ambush was set
3752.s: Maareh-geba, a place near Gibeah where the Israelites set an ambush against the Benjamites (<ref="Judges 20:33">Judges 20:33</ref>).

3753.b: A region in northern Greece; Paul preached there
3753.s: Macedonia, a region in northern Greece where Paul preached the gospel and established churches (<ref="Act.16.9-12; 20:1-3">Act.16.9-12; 20:1-3</ref>).

3754.b: A cave near Hebron; burial place of patriarchs
3754.s: Machpelah, a cave near Hebron purchased by Abraham as a burial place for Sarah and later used for other patriarchs (<ref="Genesis 23:9, 17-19">Genesis 23:9, 17-19</ref>).

3755.b: A town in the Negev of Judah
3755.s: Madmannah (Beth-marcaboth), a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:31; 19:5; 1Ch.4.31">Joshua 15:31; 19:5; 1Ch.4.31</ref>).

3756.b: A place in Moab threatened with destruction
3756.s: Madmen, a place in Moab against which Jeremiah prophesied destruction (<ref="Jeremiah 48:2">Jeremiah 48:2</ref>).

3757.s: Madmenah, a place near Jerusalem mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy (<ref="Isaiah 10:31">Isaiah 10:31</ref>).

3758.b: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
3758.s: Madon, a Canaanite city whose king joined a coalition against Joshua but was defeated (<ref="Joshua 11:1; 12:19">Joshua 11:1; 12:19</ref>).

3759.b: A place on the Sea of Galilee; home of Mary Magdalene
3759.s: Magadan (Dalmanutha), a place on the shore of the Sea of Galilee visited by Jesus (<ref="Matthew 15:39; Mrk.8.10">Matthew 15:39; Mrk.8.10</ref>), possibly the hometown of Mary Magdalene (<ref="Matthew 27:56, 61; 28:1; Mrk.15.40, 47; 16:1, 9; Luke 8:2; 24:10; Jhn.19.25; 20:1, 18">Matthew 27:56, 61; 28:1; Mrk.15.40, 47; 16:1, 9; Luke 8:2; 24:10; Jhn.19.25; 20:1, 18</ref>).

3760.b: A place whose people returned from Babylonian exile
3760.s: Magbish, a place whose people are listed among those who returned to Judah from Babylonian exile (<ref="Ezra 2:30">Ezra 2:30</ref>).

3761.b: A nation that will attack Israel in the future
3761.s: Magog, a nation that will join forces with Gog to attack Israel in the future, as prophesied in Ezekiel and Revelation (<ref="Ezk.38.2; 39:6; Revelation 20:8">Ezk.38.2; 39:6; Revelation 20:8</ref>).

3762.b: A place east of the Jordan; David's refuge
3762.s: Mahanaim, a place east of the Jordan River where Jacob met angels and David found refuge during Absalom's rebellion (<ref="Genesis 32:2; 2Sa.17.24, 27">Genesis 32:2; 2Sa.17.24, 27</ref>).

3763.b: A place between Zorah and Eshtaol; Samson's birthplace
3763.s: Mahaneh-dan, a place between Zorah and Eshtaol where the Spirit of the Lord began to stir Samson (<ref="Judges 13:25; 18:12">Judges 13:25; 18:12</ref>).

3764.b: A place in one of Solomon's administrative districts
3764.s: Makaz, a place in one of the twelve administrative districts established by Solomon (<ref="1Ki.4.9">1Ki.4.9</ref>).

3765.b: A place where the Israelites camped in the wilderness
3765.s: Makheloth, a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey (<ref="Numbers 33:25-26">Numbers 33:25-26</ref>).

3766.b: A Canaanite city conquered by Joshua
3766.s: Makkedah, a Canaanite city where Joshua defeated and executed five Amorite kings who had hidden in a cave (<ref="Joshua 10:16-28">Joshua 10:16-28</ref>).

3767.b: An island where Paul was shipwrecked
3767.s: Malta, an island in the Mediterranean Sea where Paul was shipwrecked on his journey to Rome (<ref="Act.28.1">Act.28.1</ref>).

3768.b: A place near Hebron; associated with Abraham
3768.s: Mamre, a place near Hebron where Abraham lived and built an altar to the Lord (<ref="Genesis 13:18; 18:1">Genesis 13:18; 18:1</ref>).

3769.b: A place where Benjamites lived after the exile
3769.s: Manahath (Nohah), a place where some Benjamites lived after returning from the Babylonian exile (<ref="1Ch.8.6">1Ch.8.6</ref>).

3770.b: A city in Judah; home of Nabal and Abigail
3770.s: Maon, a city in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:55">Joshua 15:55</ref>), home of Nabal and Abigail (<ref="1Sa.25.2">1Sa.25.2</ref>).

3771.b: A place with bitter water on the Exodus route
3771.s: Marah, a place where the Israelites found bitter water that Moses made drinkable by casting a tree into it (<ref="Exodus 15:23-25; Numbers 33:8-9">Exodus 15:23-25; Numbers 33:8-9</ref>).

3772.b: A place on the border of Zebulun
3772.s: Mareal, a place mentioned in describing the border of the territory of Zebulun (<ref="Joshua 19:11">Joshua 19:11</ref>).

3773.b: A town in Judah; fortified by Rehoboam
3773.s: Mareshah, a town in the Shephelah of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:44">Joshua 15:44</ref>), fortified by Rehoboam (<ref="2Ch.11.8">2Ch.11.8</ref>) and the site of Asa's victory over Zerah the Ethiopian (<ref="2Ch.14.9-10">2Ch.14.9-10</ref>).

3774.s: Maroth, a town in Judah mentioned in Micah's prophecy (<ref="Micah 1:12">Micah 1:12</ref>).

3775.b: The royal city of Samlah, an Edomite king
3775.s: Masrekah, the royal city of Samlah, one of the ancient kings of Edom before any Israelite king reigned (<ref="Genesis 36:36; 1Ch.1.47">Genesis 36:36; 1Ch.1.47</ref>).

3776.b: A place where the Israelites tested God
3776.s: Massah, a place in the wilderness where the Israelites tested the Lord by demanding water (<ref="Exodus 17:7; Deu.6.16; 9:22; 33:8; Psalm 95:8">Exodus 17:7; Deu.6.16; 9:22; 33:8; Psalm 95:8</ref>).

3777.b: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey
3777.s: Mattanah, a place where the Israelites camped during their journey through the wilderness (<ref="Numbers 21:18-19">Numbers 21:18-19</ref>).

3778.s: Mearah, a place near Sidon, mentioned in the description of the land yet to be conquered by the Israelites (<ref="Joshua 13:4">Joshua 13:4</ref>).

3779.b: A town inhabited by the people of Judah after the exile
3779.s: Meconah, a town inhabited by the people of Judah after their return from the Babylonian exile (<ref="Nehemiah 11:28">Nehemiah 11:28</ref>).

3780.b: A Moabite city captured by the Israelites
3780.s: Medeba, a city in Moab captured by the Israelites (<ref="Numbers 21:30; Joshua 13:9, 16">Numbers 21:30; Joshua 13:9, 16</ref>), later a site of battle between the Ammonites and David's army (<ref="1Ch.19.7">1Ch.19.7</ref>).

3781.b: An ancient kingdom; part of the Persian Empire
3781.s: Media (Medes), an ancient kingdom in western Iran that, along with Persia, conquered Babylon and formed the Persian Empire (<ref="2Ki.17.6; 18:11; Esther 1:3, 14, 18; 10:2; Isaiah 21:2; Jeremiah 25:25; Dan.8.20">2Ki.17.6; 18:11; Esther 1:3, 14, 18; 10:2; Isaiah 21:2; Jeremiah 25:25; Dan.8.20</ref>).

3782.b: A strategic city in the Jezreel Valley
3782.s: Megiddo, a strategically important city in the Jezreel Valley (<ref="Joshua 12:21; 17:11; Judges 1:27; 5:19">Joshua 12:21; 17:11; Judges 1:27; 5:19</ref>), fortified by Solomon (<ref="1Ki.9.15">1Ki.9.15</ref>), and the site of King Josiah's death (<ref="2Ki.23.29-30; 2Ch.35.22">2Ki.23.29-30; 2Ch.35.22</ref>).

3783.b: A place in the territory of Dan
3783.s: Me-jarkon, a place in the territory allotted to the tribe of Dan (<ref="Joshua 19:46">Joshua 19:46</ref>).

3784.b: An important city in ancient Egypt
3784.s: Memphis, an ancient Egyptian city mentioned in prophecies of judgment against Egypt (<ref="Isaiah 19:13; Jeremiah 2:16; 44:1; 46:14, 19; Ezk.30.13, 16; Hosea 9:6">Isaiah 19:13; Jeremiah 2:16; 44:1; 46:14, 19; Ezk.30.13, 16; Hosea 9:6</ref>).

3785.b: A Levitical city in Reuben, later Moabite
3785.s: Mephaath, a Levitical city in the territory of Reuben (<ref="Joshua 13:18; 21:37; 1Ch.6.79">Joshua 13:18; 21:37; 1Ch.6.79</ref>), later mentioned in a prophecy against Moab (<ref="Jeremiah 48:21">Jeremiah 48:21</ref>).

3786.b: A place where the Israelites quarreled with Moses
3786.s: Meribah, a place where the Israelites quarreled with Moses and tested the Lord, and where water came from the rock (<ref="Exodus 17:7; Deu.33.8; Psalm 95:8">Exodus 17:7; Deu.33.8; Psalm 95:8</ref>).

3787.b: A place where Moses disobeyed God
3787.s: Meribah-kadesh, a place where Moses disobeyed God by striking the rock to bring forth water (<ref="Numbers 20:13">Numbers 20:13, 24; 27:14; Deu.32.51; Psalm 81:7; 106:32; Ezk.47.19; 48:28</ref>).

3788.b: A place where Joshua defeated Jabin's coalition
3788.s: Merom, a place near the waters of Merom where Joshua defeated a coalition of Canaanite kings led by Jabin king of Hazor (<ref="Joshua 11:5, 7">Joshua 11:5, 7</ref>).

3789.b: A term used to describe two individuals in the Bible
3789.s: Meronothite, a term used to describe Jehdeiah, who was in charge of King David's donkeys (<ref="1Ch.27.30">1Ch.27.30</ref>), and Jadon, who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem (<ref="Nehemiah 3:7">Nehemiah 3:7</ref>).

3790.b: A place cursed for not helping against Sisera
3790.s: Meroz, a place cursed by the angel of the Lord for not coming to help fight against Sisera (<ref="Judges 5:23">Judges 5:23</ref>).

3791.b: A place marking the Joktanite territory
3791.s: Mesha, a place mentioned as the limit of the territory settled by the descendants of Joktan (<ref="Genesis 10:30">Genesis 10:30</ref>).

3792.b: A nation, descendant of Japheth; associated with Tubal
3792.s: Meshech, a nation descended from Japheth (<ref="Genesis 10:2">Genesis 10:2</ref>), often mentioned together with Tubal as trading partners of Tyre (<ref="Ezk.27.13">Ezk.27.13</ref>) and allies of Gog (<ref="Ezk.38.2, 3; 39:1">Ezk.38.2, 3; 39:1</ref>).

3793.b: Two nations mentioned together; defeated by Babylon
3793.s: Meshech-Tubal, two nations mentioned together as having been defeated by the Babylonians and lying in the grave with the uncircumcised (<ref="Ezk.32.26">Ezk.32.26</ref>).

3794.b: The region between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers
3794.s: Mesopotamia, the ancient region between the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, where Abraham lived before being called to Canaan (<ref="Genesis 24:10; Act.7.2">Genesis 24:10; Act.7.2</ref>) and where the Israelites were oppressed by Cushan-rishathaim (<ref="Judges 3:8">Judges 3:8, 10</ref>).

3795.b: A town in Benjamin; site of Saul's camp and Jonathan's victory
3795.s: Michmash, a town in Benjamin where Saul camped (<ref="1Sa.13.2">1Sa.13.2, 5, 11, 16, 23</ref>) and near which Jonathan defeated a Philistine garrison (<ref="1Sa.14.5, 31">1Sa.14.5, 31</ref>).

3796.b: A place on the borders of Ephraim and Manasseh
3796.s: Michmethath, a place on the border between the territories of Ephraim and Manasseh (<ref="Joshua 16:6; 17:7">Joshua 16:6; 17:7</ref>).

3797.b: A town in the wilderness of Judah
3797.s: Middin, a town in the wilderness of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:61">Joshua 15:61</ref>).

3798.b: A nation descended from Abraham; oppressed Israel in the time of the judges
3798.s: Midian, a nation descended from Abraham through Keturah (<ref="Genesis 25:2">Genesis 25:2</ref>), which oppressed Israel during the time of the judges (Judges 6-8) and was later defeated by Gideon (Judges 7-8).

3799.s: Migdal-el, a fortified city in the territory of Naphtali (<ref="Joshua 19:38">Joshua 19:38</ref>).

3800.b: A town in the lowlands of Judah
3800.s: Migdal-gad, a town in the lowlands of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:37">Joshua 15:37</ref>).

3801.b: A place near the Red Sea where the Israelites camped
3801.s: Migdol, a place near the Red Sea where the Israelites camped during the Exodus (<ref="Exodus 14:2; Numbers 33:7">Exodus 14:2; Numbers 33:7</ref>), and a city in Egypt mentioned in prophecies (<ref="Jeremiah 44:1; 46:14; Ezk.29.10; 30:6">Jeremiah 44:1; 46:14; Ezk.29.10; 30:6</ref>).

3802.b: A place near Gibeah where Saul camped
3802.s: Migron, a place near Gibeah where Saul camped with his troops (<ref="1Sa.14.2">1Sa.14.2</ref>), and a town mentioned in Isaiah's prophecy about the Assyrian invasion (<ref="Isaiah 10:28">Isaiah 10:28</ref>).

3803.b: A city in Asia Minor visited by Paul
3803.s: Miletus, a city in Asia Minor where Paul met with the elders of the Ephesian church on his way to Jerusalem (<ref="Act.20.15">Act.20.15, 17</ref>) and where Trophimus was left ill (<ref="2Ti.4.20">2Ti.4.20</ref>).

3804.b: A fortification in Jerusalem built by Solomon
3804.s: Millo (Akra), a fortification in Jerusalem built by Solomon (<ref="1Ki.9.15, 24; 11:27">1Ki.9.15, 24; 11:27</ref>) and repaired by Hezekiah (<ref="2Ch.32.5">2Ch.32.5</ref>).

3805.b: A kingdom allied with Ararat and Ashkenaz
3805.s: Minni, a kingdom mentioned alongside Ararat and Ashkenaz, was called to battle against Babylon.

3806.b: An Ammonite town known for its wheat
3806.s: Minnith, an Ammonite town, was known for its wheat and was a place of defeat for the Ammonites by Jephthah.

3807.s: Misgab, meaning "fortress," was a stronghold in Moab that faced judgment according to Jeremiah's prophecy.

3808.s: Mishal (Mashal), a Levitical city in the territory of Asher (<ref="Joshua 19:26; 21:30; 1Ch.6.74">Joshua 19:26; 21:30; 1Ch.6.74</ref>).

3809.b: A place near Sidon where the Canaanites fled
3809.s: Misrephoth-maim, a location near Sidon, was where the Canaanites fled after being defeated by Joshua.

3810.b: An Israelite campsite during the wilderness wanderings
3810.s: Mithkah was a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness journey, between Terah and Hashmonah.

3811.b: A city on the island of Lesbos visited by Paul
3811.s: Mitylene, a city on the island of Lesbos where Paul's ship stopped on his way to Jerusalem (<ref="Act.20.14">Act.20.14</ref>).

3812.b: A mountain mentioned in a psalm of lament
3812.s: Mount Mizar, a mountain mentioned in a psalm of lament, possibly representing a place of remembrance or longing for God's presence (<ref="Psalm 42:6">Psalm 42:6</ref>).

3813.b: A city in Benjamin; a place of gathering and judgment
3813.s: Mizpah (Mizpeh, Ramah, Ramathaim-zophim, Arimathea), a city in Benjamin where the Israelites gathered for judgment and prayer (<ref="Judges 20:1, 3; 21:1, 5, 8; 1Sa.7.5-7, 11-12, 16; 10:17">Judges 20:1, 3; 21:1, 5, 8; 1Sa.7.5-7, 11-12, 16; 10:17</ref>), and the hometown of Samuel (<ref="1Sa.1.19; 2:11; 7:17; 8:4; 15:34; 16:13; 19:18-23; 20:1; 25:1; 28:3">1Sa.1.19; 2:11; 7:17; 8:4; 15:34; 16:13; 19:18-23; 20:1; 25:1; 28:3</ref>) and Joseph of Arimathea (<ref="Matthew 27:57; Mrk.15.43; Luke 23:50-51; Jhn.19.38">Matthew 27:57; Mrk.15.43; Luke 23:50-51; Jhn.19.38</ref>).

3814.b: A town in the lowlands of Judah
3814.s: Mizpeh, a town in the lowlands (Shephelah) of Judah (<ref="Joshua 15:38">Joshua 15:38</ref>).

3815.s: The Valley of Mizpeh (Mizpah), a region near Mount Hermon where Joshua defeated the kings of the northern Canaanite coalition (<ref="Joshua 11:3, 8">Joshua 11:3, 8</ref>).

3816.b: Ancient kingdom east of the Dead Sea in Jordan
3816.s: Moab was an ancient kingdom located east of the Dead Sea in present-day Jordan, often in conflict with Israel.

3817.b: Region east of the Jordan River, opposite Jericho
3817.s: The plains of Moab, located east of the Jordan River and opposite Jericho, were where the Israelites camped before entering the Promised Land (<ref="Num.22.1; 26:3, 63; 31:12; 33:48-50; 35:1; 36:13; Deut 34:1, 8; Josh 13:32">Num.22.1; 26:3, 63; 31:12; 33:48-50; 35:1; 36:13; Deut 34:1, 8; Josh 13:32</ref>).

3818.b: Town in the Negev, allotted to Judah and Simeon
3818.s: Moladah was a town in the Negev region, allotted to the tribes of Judah and Simeon, and later inhabited by the people of Judah after the Babylonian exile (<ref="Josh 15:26; 19:2; 1Ch.4.28; Neh.11.26">Josh 15:26; 19:2; 1Ch.4.28; Neh.11.26</ref>).

3819.b: Place near Shechem; also a hill near Gilgal
3819.s: Moreh refers to two locations: a place near Shechem where Abraham built an altar (<ref="Gen.12.6">Gen.12.6</ref>) and a hill near Gilgal, associated with the blessing and cursing ceremony (<ref="Deut 11:30">Deut 11:30</ref>).

3820.b: Place near Shechem; hill where Gideon camped
3820.s: Moreh refers to a place near Shechem associated with Abraham (<ref="Gen.12.6">Gen.12.6</ref>) and a hill where Gideon camped before attacking the Midianites (<ref="Judg 7:1">Judg 7:1</ref>).

3821.b: Hometown of the prophet Micah in Judah
3821.s: Moresheth was the hometown of the prophet Micah, located in Judah.

3822.b: Site of Solomon's temple in Jerusalem
3822.s: Mount Moriah was the site where Solomon built the temple in Jerusalem.

3823.b: A district or valley in or near Jerusalem
3823.s: The Mortar was a district or valley in or near Jerusalem, mentioned in Zephaniah's prophecy.

3824.b: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings
3824.s: Moserah was a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings, and where Aaron died and was buried.

3825.b: A place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings
3825.s: Moseroth was a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings after leaving Egypt.

3826.b: The innermost room of the tabernacle and temple
3826.s: The Most Holy Place was the innermost room of the tabernacle and temple, where the Ark of the Covenant was kept.

3827.b: A town in the territory of Benjamin
3827.s: Mozah was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.

3828.b: A gate in Jerusalem mentioned in Nehemiah's time
3828.s: The Muster Gate, also known as the Miphkad Gate, was one of the gates of Jerusalem mentioned in Nehemiah's time.

3829.b: A city in Lycia where Paul's ship stopped
3829.s: Myra was a city in Lycia, Asia Minor, where Paul's ship stopped on his journey to Rome as a prisoner.

3830.b: A region in northwest Asia Minor visited by Paul
3830.s: Mysia was a region in northwest Asia Minor (modern Turkey) that Paul and his companions passed through on his second missionary journey.

3831.b: A town in the Judean lowlands
3831.s: Naamah was a town in the Judean lowlands, mentioned in the tribal allotment of Judah.

3832.b: A border town between Ephraim and Benjamin
3832.s: Naaran, also called Naarah, was a border town between the tribes of Ephraim and Benjamin.

3833.s: Nahalol, also called Nahalal, was a Levitical city in the territory of Zebulun.

3834.b: A town in Galilee where Jesus raised a widow's son
3834.s: Nain was a town in Galilee where Jesus raised a widow's son from the dead.

3835.b: A place near Ramah where David fled from Saul
3835.s: Naioth was a place near Ramah where David fled to escape King Saul, and where Samuel and a group of prophets lived.

3836.b: A region in Issachar with Manassite towns
3836.s: Naphath was a region in Issachar that contained towns belonging to the tribe of Manasseh.

3837.b: The hometown of Jesus in Galilee
3837.s: Nazareth was a village in Galilee where Jesus grew up, giving rise to His title "Jesus of Nazareth."

3838.b: A border town of Zebulun and Asher
3838.s: Neah, also called Neiel, was a border town between the territories of Zebulun and Asher.

3839.b: A port city in Macedonia visited by Paul
3839.s: Neapolis was a port city in Macedonia where Paul landed on his first journey to Europe.

3840.b: A town in Benjamin inhabited by Benjamites after the exile
3840.s: Neballat was a town in the territory of Benjamin where some Benjamites settled after returning from the Babylonian exile.

3841.b: A town in Judah, possibly named after a person
3841.s: Nebo was a town in Judah, possibly named after a person, whose inhabitants returned from the Babylonian exile.

3842.b: A city and mountain in Moab
3842.s: Nebo was a city and mountain in Moab, mentioned in the Old Testament.

3843.b: The mountain where Moses viewed the Promised Land
3843.s: Mount Nebo, also called Abarim, was the mountain from which Moses viewed the Promised Land before his death.

3844.b: The southern region of Israel, a semi-arid area
3844.s: The Negeb, meaning "south," refers to the semi-arid region in the southern part of Israel.

3845.b: A spring on the border of Judah and Benjamin
3845.s: Nephtoah was a spring that served as a boundary marker between the territories of Judah and Benjamin.

3846.b: A place associated with potters in Judah
3846.s: Netaim was a place in Judah where potters lived and worked.

3847.b: A town in Judah, home to several notable individuals
3847.s: Netophah was a town in Judah, known as the hometown of several notable individuals in the Bible.

3848.b: A gate in Jerusalem during Jeremiah's time
3848.s: The New Gate was a gate in Jerusalem during the time of the prophet Jeremiah.

3849.b: A town in the Judean lowlands
3849.s: Nezib was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the lowland region.

3850.b: A town in the Judean wilderness
3850.s: Nibshan was a town in the wilderness of Judah, mentioned in the list of towns allotted to the tribe of Judah.

3851.b: A city in Epirus where Paul planned to winter
3851.s: Nicopolis was a city in Epirus where Paul intended to spend the winter, as mentioned in his letter to Titus.

3852.b: The major river of Egypt, mentioned in various contexts
3852.s: The Nile, the major river of Egypt, is mentioned in various contexts throughout the Bible, often in relation to the history of Israel and God's judgment on Egypt.

3853.b: A place in Moab known for its waters
3853.s: Nimrim was a place in Moab known for its waters, which are mentioned in the context of God's judgment on Moab.

3854.b: The capital of Assyria, known for its wickedness and repentance
3854.s: Nineveh, the capital of Assyria, is known in the Bible for its wickedness and its remarkable repentance following Jonah's preaching.

3855.b: A city of priests near Jerusalem
3855.s: Nob was a city of priests near Jerusalem, known for a massacre ordered by King Saul and as a temporary location of the Ark of the Covenant.

3856.b: The land where Cain settled after killing Abel
3856.s: Nod was the land east of Eden where Cain settled after he was banished for killing his brother Abel.

3857.b: A place where the Israelites camped during the Exodus
3857.s: Oboth was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their journey through the wilderness after the Exodus from Egypt.

3858.b: A mountain ridge east of Jerusalem
3858.s: The Mount of Olives is a mountain ridge east of Jerusalem, known as the site of many significant events in the Bible, particularly in the life of Jesus.

3859.b: An ancient Egyptian city, mentioned in relation to Joseph
3859.s: On, also known as Heliopolis, was an ancient Egyptian city mentioned in the Bible in connection with Joseph's life and prophetic references to Egypt.

3860.b: A town in Benjamin, near Lod
3860.s: Ono was a town in the territory of Benjamin, often mentioned together with Lod, and was the site of a proposed meeting between Nehemiah and his enemies.

3861.s: Ophel was a fortified area in Jerusalem, located near the temple, and was inhabited by temple servants during the time of Nehemiah.

3862.b: A region known for its gold
3862.s: Ophir was a region famous for its high-quality gold, which was imported to Israel during the reigns of David and Solomon.

3863.s: Ophni was a town allotted to the tribe of Benjamin during the division of the Promised Land.

3864.b: A town in Benjamin and a place in Manasseh
3864.s: Ophrah was a town in Benjamin and a place in Manasseh, associated with Gideon and mentioned in a prophecy of Micah.

3865.b: Gideon's hometown in Manasseh; a town in Issachar
3865.s: Ophrah, also known as Hapharaim, was Gideon's hometown in Manasseh and the site of important events during his time as a judge, as well as a town allotted to the tribe of Issachar.

3866.b: A place mentioned in some manuscripts of 1 Timothy
3866.s: Pacatiana is a place mentioned in some manuscripts of <ref="1Ti.6.21">1Ti.6.21</ref>, but its exact location and significance are unknown.

3867.b: The homeland of the patriarchs in Mesopotamia
3867.s: Paddan, also known as Paddan-aram or Aram, was the homeland of the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, located in Mesopotamia.

3868.b: A Roman province in Asia Minor
3868.s: Pamphylia was a Roman province on the southern coast of Asia Minor, visited by Paul and Barnabas during their missionary journeys.

3869.b: A city on the island of Cyprus
3869.s: Paphos was a city on the island of Cyprus, where Paul and Barnabas encountered a sorcerer and converted the proconsul to Christianity.

3870.s: Parah was a city allotted to the tribe of Benjamin, located between Avvim and Ophrah.

3871.b: A desert region in the Sinai Peninsula
3871.s: Paran was a desert region in the Sinai Peninsula, associated with the Israelites' wanderings and the early life of Ishmael.

3872.b: A mountain associated with God's appearance
3872.s: Mount Paran is mentioned in poetic passages as a place from which God comes or shines forth.

3873.b: A colonnade or structure in the temple complex
3873.s: Parbar was a colonnade or structure located on the west side of the temple complex in Jerusalem.

3874.b: A place from which Solomon obtained gold
3874.s: Parvaim was a place or region from which Solomon obtained gold for decorating the temple in Jerusalem.

3875.b: A city in Lycia visited by Paul
3875.s: Patara was a coastal city in Lycia (modern-day Turkey) where Paul changed ships during his journey to Jerusalem.

3876.s: Pathros was a region in Upper Egypt (southern Egypt) where some Judeans settled after the Babylonian exile.

3877.b: An island where John received the Revelation
3877.s: Patmos is a Greek island in the Aegean Sea where the apostle John was exiled and received the visions recorded in the Book of Revelation.

3878.s: Pau, also known as Pai, was a city in Edom mentioned in the genealogy of Edomite kings.

3879.b: An Egyptian city, also known as Sin
3879.s: Pelusium, also known as Sin, was an important Egyptian city mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy against Egypt.

3880.b: A place where Jacob wrestled with God
3880.s: Peniel, also called Penuel, was the place where Jacob wrestled with God and had his name changed to Israel.

3881.b: A gate in Jerusalem mentioned by Jeremiah
3881.s: The People's Gate was one of the gates of Jerusalem, where the prophet Jeremiah was instructed to proclaim God's message.

3882.b: A mountain in Moab associated with idolatry
3882.s: Peor was a mountain in Moab where Balak brought Balaam to curse Israel, and where the Israelites later engaged in idolatry and immorality with the Moabites.

3883.b: A place where David defeated the Philistines
3883.s: Mount Perazim was the location where David, with God's help, defeated the Philistines, and it is used by Isaiah as an example of God's judgment.

3884.b: A place named after Uzzah's death
3884.s: Perez-uzza was the name given to the place where Uzzah died after touching the Ark of the Covenant during its transport to Jerusalem.

3885.b: A city in Pamphylia visited by Paul
3885.s: Perga was a city in Pamphylia (modern-day Turkey) where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel during their first missionary journey.

3886.b: A city in Asia Minor with a church
3886.s: Pergamum was one of the seven churches of Asia addressed in the Book of Revelation, known for its faithfulness despite living in a city associated with Satan's throne.

3887.b: An empire that ruled over the exiled Jews
3887.s: Persia was the empire that conquered Babylon and allowed the exiled Jews to return to Jerusalem and rebuild the temple.

3888.b: The hometown of Balaam in Mesopotamia
3888.s: Pethor was the hometown of Balaam, the prophet hired by Balak to curse Israel, located near the Euphrates River in Mesopotamia.

3889.s: Pharpar was one of the rivers of Damascus, mentioned by Naaman the leper when comparing them to the Jordan River in Israel.

3890.b: One of the seven churches in Asia Minor
3890.s: Philadelphia was one of the seven churches in Asia Minor addressed in the Book of Revelation, known for its faithfulness and endurance.

3891.b: A city in Macedonia visited by Paul
3891.s: Philippi was a city in Macedonia where Paul founded a church and experienced persecution, imprisonment, and a miraculous deliverance.

3892.b: An ancient people and region in Canaan
3892.s: The Philistines were a powerful people who inhabited the coastal plain of Canaan and were often in conflict with the Israelites during the period of the judges and early monarchy.

3893.b: A region and people on the Mediterranean coast
3893.s: Phoenicia was a region along the Mediterranean coast, north of Israel, known for its maritime trade and mentioned in the New Testament in connection with the spread of the gospel.

3894.b: A harbor on the island of Crete
3894.s: Phoenix was a harbor on the island of Crete where the ship carrying Paul and other prisoners attempted to winter during their journey to Rome.

3895.b: A region in Asia Minor with early Christians
3895.s: Phrygia was a region in Asia Minor where Paul traveled and preached the gospel, and some of its inhabitants were present in Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.

3896.b: An Egyptian city mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
3896.s: Pi-beseth was an Egyptian city that Ezekiel prophesied would experience God's judgment along with other cities in Egypt.

3897.b: A place near the Red Sea crossing
3897.s: Pi-hahiroth was a location near the Red Sea where the Israelites camped before crossing the sea during the Exodus from Egypt.

3898.b: A town in Ephraim, home of several notable Israelites
3898.s: Pirathon was a town in the hill country of Ephraim, associated with the judge Abdon and two of David's mighty men, Benaiah and Hiddai.

3899.b: A mountain range in Moab, east of the Jordan
3899.s: Pisgah, or the slopes of Pisgah, was a mountain range in Moab where Moses viewed the Promised Land before his death.

3900.b: A river flowing from Eden, encircling Havilah
3900.s: Pishon was one of the four rivers that flowed from the river in the Garden of Eden, encircling the land of Havilah, which was known for its gold, bdellium, and onyx.

3901.b: A region in Asia Minor visited by Paul
3901.s: Pisidia was a mountainous region in Asia Minor where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel during their first missionary journey.

3902.b: A store city built by the Israelites in Egypt
3902.s: Pithom was one of the store cities built by the Israelites during their enslavement in Egypt, along with Rameses.

3903.b: A region in Asia Minor with Jewish inhabitants
3903.s: Pontus was a region in Asia Minor along the Black Sea coast, home to Jewish inhabitants and early Christian converts.

3904.b: A gate in Jerusalem mentioned by Jeremiah
3904.s: The Potsherd Gate was a gate in Jerusalem near the Valley of Ben Hinnom, where Jeremiah was instructed to proclaim a message of judgment against Judah.

3905.b: A stopping place for the Israelites in the wilderness
3905.s: Punon was one of the places where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings, located between Zalmonah and Oboth.

3906.b: A port city in Italy visited by Paul
3906.s: Puteoli was a major port city in Italy where Paul stayed for seven days on his journey to Rome as a prisoner.

3907.b: A trading partner of Tyre, possibly in Arabia
3907.s: Raamah was a place, possibly located in Arabia, that traded with the city of Tyre, offering spices, precious stones, and gold.

3908.b: A store city built by the Israelites in Egypt
3908.s: Raamses was one of the store cities built by the Israelites during their enslavement in Egypt, along with Pithom.

3909.b: A town allotted to the tribe of Issachar
3909.s: Rabbith was a town in the territory of Issachar, mentioned in the list of cities and towns allocated to the tribe during the division of the Promised Land.

3910.b: City on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee
3910.s: Tiberias (Rakkath), a city on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, near where Jesus fed the five thousand (<ref="Josh. 19:35; Jhn.6.23">Josh. 19:35; Jhn.6.23</ref>).

3911.b: A town allotted to the tribe of Dan
3911.s: Rakkon was a town mentioned in the description of the territory allocated to the tribe of Dan in the Promised Land.

3912.b: A town in Benjamin, near Gibeah and Jerusalem
3912.s: Ramah was a town in the territory of Benjamin, often associated with significant events in Israel's history, such as the mourning of Rachel and the imprisonment of Jeremiah.

3913.b: A town on the border of Asher and Tyre
3913.s: Ramah was a town located on the border between the territory of Asher and the city-state of Tyre.

3914.b: A fortified city in the territory of Naphtali
3914.s: Ramah was a fortified city located in the territory of Naphtali, mentioned in the list of cities allocated to the tribe during the division of the Promised Land.

3915.b: The place where Samson killed a thousand Philistines
3915.s: Ramath-lehi, meaning "hill of the jawbone," was the place where Samson killed a thousand Philistines with the jawbone of a donkey.

3916.b: Egyptian city where Israelites lived before the Exodus
3916.s: Rameses was a city in Egypt where the Israelites lived during their enslavement before the Exodus (<ref="Gen. 47:11; Exo. 12:37">Gen. 47:11; Exo. 12:37</ref>).

3917.b: City of refuge east of the Jordan
3917.s: Ramoth, also called Ramoth-gilead, was a city of refuge in Gad and a Levitical city (<ref="Deu. 4:43; Jos. 20:8; 21:38">Deu. 4:43; Jos. 20:8; 21:38</ref>).

3918.s: Recah was a descendant of Judah through Caleb (<ref="1Ch. 4:12">1Ch. 4:12</ref>).

3919.b: Sea crossed by Israelites in the Exodus
3919.s: The Red Sea was the body of water miraculously crossed by the Israelites in their escape from Egypt (<ref="Exo. 13:18; 15:4">Exo. 13:18; 15:4</ref>).

3920.b: City on the border of Asher
3920.s: Rehob was a city on the northern border of the territory allotted to the tribe of Asher (<ref="Jos. 19:28">Jos. 19:28</ref>).

3921.s: Rehob was a Levitical city within the territory of Asher (<ref="Jos. 19:30; 21:31; 1Ch. 6:75">Jos. 19:30; 21:31; 1Ch. 6:75</ref>).

3922.s: Rehoboth was the name of a well dug by Isaac where he found room and water (<ref="Gen. 26:22">Gen. 26:22</ref>).

3923.b: City associated with an Edomite king
3923.s: Rehoboth was a city associated with Shaul, an Edomite king (<ref="Gen. 36:37; 1Ch. 1:48">Gen. 36:37; 1Ch. 1:48</ref>).

3924.s: Rekem was a city allotted to the tribe of Benjamin (<ref="Jos. 18:27">Jos. 18:27</ref>).

3925.s: Remeth, also called Ramoth, was a Levitical city allotted to the tribe of Issachar (<ref="Jos. 19:21; 1Ch. 6:73">Jos. 19:21; 1Ch. 6:73</ref>).

3926.b: Valley near Jerusalem, site of battles
3926.s: The Valley of Rephaim was a valley near Jerusalem where David fought the Philistines (<ref="2Sa. 5:18, 22; 23:13; 1Ch. 11:15; 14:9">2Sa. 5:18, 22; 23:13; 1Ch. 11:15; 14:9</ref>).

3927.s: Rephidim was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Sinai (<ref="Exo. 17:1, 8; 19:2; Num. 33:14, 15">Exo. 17:1, 8; 19:2; Num. 33:14, 15</ref>).

3928.b: Ancient Assyrian city built by Nimrod
3928.s: Resen was an ancient Assyrian city built by Nimrod between Nineveh and Calah (<ref="Gen. 10:12">Gen. 10:12</ref>).

3929.s: Rezeph was a city conquered by the Assyrians, mentioned in a letter from the Assyrian king to Hezekiah (<ref="2Ki. 19:12; Isa. 37:12">2Ki. 19:12; Isa. 37:12</ref>).

3930.s: Rhegium was a city in Italy where Paul's ship stopped on his journey to Rome (<ref="Act. 28:13">Act. 28:13</ref>).

3931.b: Island visited by Paul on his journey
3931.s: Rhodes was an island where Paul stopped during his journey to Jerusalem (<ref="Act. 21:1">Act. 21:1</ref>).

3932.b: Babylonian headquarters during the conquest of Judah
3932.s: Riblah was a city in Hamath where the Babylonians set up their headquarters during their campaigns against Judah (<ref="2Ki. 23:33; 25:6, 20-21; Jer. 39:5-6; 52:9-10, 26-27">2Ki. 23:33; 25:6, 20-21; Jer. 39:5-6; 52:9-10, 26-27</ref>).

3933.b: Place on the eastern border of the Promised Land
3933.s: Riblah was a place mentioned in the description of the eastern border of the Promised Land (<ref="Num. 34:11">Num. 34:11</ref>).

3934.b: Rock where Benjamites fled after battle
3934.s: Rimmon was a rock where 600 Benjamite survivors fled after a battle with the other Israelite tribes (<ref="Jdg. 20:45, 47; 21:13">Jdg. 20:45, 47; 21:13</ref>).

3935.b: A town in Judah and Simeon
3935.s: Rimmon, a town allotted to Judah and later given to Simeon, was located in the Negev region.

3936.s: Rimmon-perez was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Canaan (<ref="Num. 33:19-20">Num. 33:19-20</ref>).

3937.s: Rissah was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Canaan (<ref="Num. 33:21-22">Num. 33:21-22</ref>).

3938.s: Rithmah was a place where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to Canaan (<ref="Num. 33:18-19">Num. 33:18-19</ref>).

3939.b: Place where Saul stopped pursuing David
3939.s: The Rock of Escape was a place where Saul stopped pursuing David after being called away to fight the Philistines (<ref="1Sa. 23:28">1Sa. 23:28</ref>).

3940.s: Rogelim was the hometown of Barzillai the Gileadite, who provided supplies for David during Absalom's rebellion (<ref="2Sa. 17:27; 19:31">2Sa. 17:27; 19:31</ref>).

3941.b: Capital city of the Roman Empire
3941.s: Rome was the capital of the Roman Empire, where Paul was imprisoned and wrote several epistles (<ref="Act.28.16; Rom. 1:7">Act.28.16; Rom. 1:7</ref>).

3942.b: Unknown location mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
3942.s: Sahar is a place mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy, but its exact location is unknown (<ref="Ezk. 27:18">Ezk. 27:18</ref>).

3943.b: City on Cyprus visited by Paul and Barnabas
3943.s: Salamis was a city on the island of Cyprus where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel in the Jewish synagogues (<ref="Act.13.5">Act.13.5</ref>).

3944.b: City in Bashan, east of the Jordan River
3944.s: Salecah was a city in the region of Bashan, east of the Jordan River, associated with the kingdoms of Og and Sihon (<ref="Deut. 3:10; Josh. 12:5; 13:11; 1Chr. 5:11">Deut. 3:10; Josh. 12:5; 13:11; 1Chr. 5:11</ref>).

3945.b: Place near Aenon where John the Baptist baptized
3945.s: Salim was a place near Aenon where John the Baptist was baptizing, because there was plenty of water there (<ref="Jhn.3.23">Jhn.3.23</ref>).

3946.b: Promontory on the island of Crete
3946.s: Salmone was a promontory on the island of Crete that Paul's ship passed on his voyage to Rome (<ref="Act.27.7">Act.27.7</ref>).

3947.b: Another name for the Dead Sea
3947.s: The Salt Sea, also known as the Sea of Arabah, is another name for the Dead Sea, located at the lowest point on Earth (<ref="Gen. 14:3; Num. 34:3, 12; Deut. 3:17; Josh. 3:16; 12:3; 15:2, 5; 18:19; Deut. 4:49; 2Ki. 14:25">Gen. 14:3; Num. 34:3, 12; Deut. 3:17; Josh. 3:16; 12:3; 15:2, 5; 18:19; Deut. 4:49; 2Ki. 14:25</ref>).

3948.b: Valley where David and his commanders defeated enemies
3948.s: The Salt Valley was a location where David and his commanders defeated the Edomites and Arameans (<ref="2Sa. 8:13; 2Ki. 14:7; 1Chr. 18:12; 2Chr. 25:11; Psa. 60:1">2Sa. 8:13; 2Ki. 14:7; 1Chr. 18:12; 2Chr. 25:11; Psa. 60:1</ref>).

3949.b: Capital city of the northern kingdom of Israel; Samaritan inhabitants
3949.s: Samaria was the capital city of the northern kingdom of Israel, and its inhabitants were known as Samaritans (<ref="1Ki. 16:24; 2Ki. 17:24; Jhn. 4:9; Act.8.5">1Ki. 16:24; 2Ki. 17:24; Jhn. 4:9; Act.8.5</ref>).

3950.b: Island visited by Paul during his travels
3950.s: Samos is an island in the Aegean Sea where Paul stopped during his third missionary journey (<ref="Act.20.15">Act.20.15</ref>).

3951.b: Island visited by Paul during his second missionary journey
3951.s: Samothrace is an island in the Aegean Sea where Paul and his companions landed during his second missionary journey (<ref="Act.16.11">Act.16.11</ref>).

3952.b: Town in the Negev region of Judah
3952.s: Sansannah was a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the Negev region (<ref="Josh. 15:31">Josh. 15:31</ref>).

3953.s: Sarid was a border town in the territory allotted to the tribe of Zebulun (<ref="Josh. 19:10, 12">Josh. 19:10, 12</ref>).

3954.b: Kingdom mentioned in prophetic and poetic texts
3954.s: Seba was a kingdom mentioned in prophetic and poetic texts, often in the context of bringing gifts to God (<ref="Psa. 72:10; Isa. 43:3">Psa. 72:10; Isa. 43:3</ref>).

3955.b: Town in the territory of Reuben
3955.s: Sebam was one of the towns in the territory of Reuben, east of the Jordan River (<ref="Num. 32:3">Num. 32:3</ref>).

3956.b: Town in the wilderness of Judah
3956.s: Secacah was a town located in the wilderness region of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:61">Josh. 15:61</ref>).

3957.b: District in Jerusalem mentioned by Huldah and Zephaniah
3957.s: The Second Quarter was a district in Jerusalem mentioned in connection with the prophetess Huldah (<ref="2Ki. 22:14; 2Chr. 34:22">2Ki. 22:14; 2Chr. 34:22</ref>) and in Zephaniah's prophecy (<ref="Zeph. 1:10">Zeph. 1:10</ref>).

3958.b: Place near Ramah visited by Saul
3958.s: Secu was a place near Ramah where Saul went in search of David (<ref="1Sam. 19:22">1Sam. 19:22</ref>).

3959.b: Region inhabited by Edomites, descendants of Esau
3959.s: Seir was a mountainous region inhabited by the Edomites, the descendants of Esau (<ref="Gen. 32:3; 36:8; Num. 24:18; Deut. 2:4; Josh. 24:4">Gen. 32:3; 36:8; Num. 24:18; Deut. 2:4; Josh. 24:4</ref>).

3960.b: Mountainous region in Seir, associated with Edom
3960.s: Mount Seir refers to the mountainous region within Seir, often associated with the Edomites (<ref="Deut. 1:2; 2:1, 5; 1Chr. 4:42; Ezek. 35:2, 3, 7, 15">Deut. 1:2; 2:1, 5; 1Chr. 4:42; Ezek. 35:2, 3, 7, 15</ref>).

3961.b: Landmark on the boundary of Judah
3961.s: Mount Seir was a landmark on the boundary of Judah, near Kiriath-jearim and Chesalon (<ref="Josh. 15:10">Josh. 15:10</ref>).

3962.b: Place where Ehud escaped after killing Eglon
3962.s: Seirah was the place to which Ehud escaped after killing Eglon, the king of Moab (<ref="Judg. 3:26">Judg. 3:26</ref>).

3963.b: Edomite stronghold captured by King Amaziah of Judah
3963.s: Sela, also known as rock or Joktheel, was an Edomite stronghold captured by King Amaziah of Judah (<ref="2Ki. 14:7; 2Chr. 25:12; Isa. 16:1; 42:11; Judg. 1:36">2Ki. 14:7; 2Chr. 25:12; Isa. 16:1; 42:11; Judg. 1:36</ref>).

3964.b: Port city from which Paul and Barnabas sailed
3964.s: Seleucia was the port city from which Paul and Barnabas sailed to Cyprus on their first missionary journey (<ref="Act.13.4">Act.13.4</ref>).

3965.b: Town whose people returned from Babylonian exile
3965.s: Senaah was a town whose people are listed among those who returned to Judah from the Babylonian exile (<ref="Ezr. 2:35; Neh. 7:38">Ezr. 2:35; Neh. 7:38</ref>).

3966.s: Seneh was one of two rocky crags between which Jonathan and his armor-bearer passed to attack the Philistine garrison at Michmash (<ref="1Sam. 14:4">1Sam. 14:4</ref>).

3967.b: Boundary of the territory settled by Joktan's descendants
3967.s: Sephar was a mountain in the east that marked the boundary of the territory settled by the descendants of Joktan (<ref="Gen. 10:30">Gen. 10:30</ref>).

3968.b: City in Asia Minor; destination of exiled Jews
3968.s: Sepharad, possibly referring to Sardis, was a destination of exiled Jews (<ref="Obad. 1:20">Obad. 1:20</ref>) and one of the seven churches mentioned in Revelation (<ref="Rev. 1:11; 3:1, 4">Rev. 1:11; 3:1, 4</ref>).

3969.b: City of origin for people resettled in Samaria
3969.s: Sepharvaim was one of the cities from which the Assyrians brought people to resettle in Samaria after the deportation of the Israelites (<ref="2Ki. 17:24, 31; 18:34; 19:13; Isa. 36:19; 37:13">2Ki. 17:24, 31; 18:34; 19:13; Isa. 36:19; 37:13</ref>).

3970.b: Town in Dan, home of David's mighty men
3970.s: Shaalbim, also called Shaalabbin, was a town allotted to the tribe of Dan (<ref="Josh. 19:42; Judg. 1:35">Josh. 19:42; Judg. 1:35</ref>) and the hometown of some of David's mighty men (<ref="2Sam. 23:32; 1Chr. 11:33">2Sam. 23:32; 1Chr. 11:33</ref>). It was also a town under Solomon's administration (<ref="1Ki. 4:9">1Ki. 4:9</ref>).

3971.b: Region traversed by Saul in search of donkeys
3971.s: Shaalim was a region through which Saul passed while searching for his father's lost donkeys (<ref="1Sam. 9:4">1Sam. 9:4</ref>).

3972.b: Town in Judah; site of Philistine retreat
3972.s: Shaaraim was a town in the Shephelah of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:36">Josh. 15:36</ref>) and a place the Philistines passed in their retreat from Socoh (<ref="1Sam. 17:52">1Sam. 17:52</ref>).

3973.s: Shahazumah was a town on the border of Issachar's territory (<ref="Josh. 19:22">Josh. 19:22</ref>).

3974.b: Region Saul passed through seeking donkeys
3974.s: Shalishah was a region Saul and his servant passed through while searching for his father's lost donkeys (<ref="1Sam. 9:4">1Sam. 9:4</ref>).

3975.b: Gate in Jerusalem assigned to Shuppim and Hosah
3975.s: Shallecheth was a gate in Jerusalem assigned to the Levites Shuppim and Hosah for guard duty (<ref="1Chr. 26:16">1Chr. 26:16</ref>).

3976.b: Issacharite judge who led Israel for 23 years
3976.s: Shamir, from the hill country of Ephraim, was an Issacharite who judged Israel for 23 years (<ref="Judg. 10:1-2">Judg. 10:1-2</ref>).

3977.b: Town in the hill country of Judah
3977.s: Shamir was a town in the hill country of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:48">Josh. 15:48</ref>).

3978.s: Shaphir was a town mentioned in Micah's prophecy, urged to pass on in nakedness and shame (<ref="Mic. 1:11">Mic. 1:11</ref>).

3979.b: Coastal plain known for its beauty and fertility
3979.s: Sharon was a coastal plain known for its beauty, fertility, and pastureland (<ref="1Chr. 27:29; Sng.2.1; Isa. 33:9; 35:2; 65:10; Act.9.35">1Chr. 27:29; Sng.2.1; Isa. 33:9; 35:2; 65:10; Act.9.35</ref>).

3980.b: Region where Gadites pastured their flocks
3980.s: Sharon was a region east of the Jordan where the Gadites pastured their flocks (<ref="1Chr. 5:16">1Chr. 5:16</ref>).

3981.b: Town allotted to Simeon within Judah's territory
3981.s: Sharuhen, also called Shaaraim or Shilhim, was a town allotted to the tribe of Simeon within Judah's territory (<ref="Josh. 19:6; 1Chr. 4:31; Josh. 15:32">Josh. 19:6; 1Chr. 4:31; Josh. 15:32</ref>).

3982.b: Valley where Chedorlaomer defeated the Emites
3982.s: Shaveh Kiriathaim was a valley where Chedorlaomer and his allies defeated the Emites before battling the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah (<ref="Gen. 14:5, 17">Gen. 14:5, 17</ref>).

3983.b: Kingdom known for wealth, trade, and the Queen of Sheba
3983.s: Sheba, also referred to as the South, was a kingdom known for its wealth, trade, and the visit of its queen to King Solomon (<ref="1Ki. 10:1-13; 2Chr. 9:1-12; Ps. 72:10, 15; Isa. 60:6; Jer. 6:20; Ezek. 27:22-23; 38:13; Luke 11:31">1Ki. 10:1-13; 2Chr. 9:1-12; Ps. 72:10, 15; Isa. 60:6; Jer. 6:20; Ezek. 27:22-23; 38:13; Luke 11:31</ref>).

3984.b: Place near Ai where Israelites fled
3984.s: Shebarim was a place near Ai where the Israelites fled after being defeated due to Achan's sin (<ref="Josh. 7:5">Josh. 7:5</ref>).

3985.b: City in Canaan, later allotted to Ephraim
3985.s: Shechem was a prominent city in Canaan, later allotted to the tribe of Ephraim, and the site of important events in Israel's history (<ref="Gen. 12:6; 33:18-20; Josh. 20:7; 24:1, 25-26; Judg. 9; 1Ki. 12:1, 25; Ps. 60:6; 108:7; Act.7.16">Gen. 12:6; 33:18-20; Josh. 20:7; 24:1, 25-26; Judg. 9; 1Ki. 12:1, 25; Ps. 60:6; 108:7; Act.7.16</ref>).

3986.b: Gate in Jerusalem near the sheep market
3986.s: The Sheep Gate was a gate in Jerusalem's wall, likely near the sheep market, that was rebuilt during Nehemiah's time (<ref="Neh. 3:1, 32; 12:39; Jhn.5.2">Neh. 3:1, 32; 12:39; Jhn.5.2</ref>).

3987.s: Shelah, also called Shiloah, the King's Pool, or Siloam, was a pool in Jerusalem fed by the Gihon Spring via Hezekiah's Tunnel (<ref="Neh. 3:15; Isa. 8:6; Neh. 2:14; Luke 13:4; Jhn.9.7, 11">Neh. 3:15; Isa. 8:6; Neh. 2:14; Luke 13:4; Jhn.9.7, 11</ref>).

3988.b: Town in the Negev region of Judah
3988.s: Shema was a town in the Negev region of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:26">Josh. 15:26</ref>).

3989.b: Place where Samuel set up the Ebenezer stone
3989.s: Shen was the place where Samuel set up the Ebenezer stone to commemorate the Israelites' victory over the Philistines (<ref="1Sam. 7:12">1Sam. 7:12</ref>).

3990.b: Landmark on the northeastern border of the Promised Land
3990.s: Shepham was a landmark on the northeastern border of the Promised Land, between Hazar-enan and Riblah (<ref="Num. 34:10-11">Num. 34:10-11</ref>).

3991.b: Lowland region between Judean hills and coastal plain
3991.s: The Shephelah was the lowland region between the Judean hills and the coastal plain, known for its fertile valleys and strategic importance (<ref="Josh. 9:1; 10:40; 2Chr. 28:18; Jer. 17:26; 32:44; 33:13">Josh. 9:1; 10:40; 2Chr. 28:18; Jer. 17:26; 32:44; 33:13</ref>).

3992.s: Mount Shepher was a place where the Israelites camped during their wilderness wanderings between Kehelathah and Haradah (<ref="Num. 33:23-24">Num. 33:23-24</ref>).

3993.s: Shihor-libnath was a place that marked the boundary of the territory allotted to the tribe of Asher (<ref="Josh. 19:26">Josh. 19:26</ref>).

3994.b: Town on the border of Judah
3994.s: Shikkeron was a town on the northern border of Judah's territory, near Mount Baalah (<ref="Josh. 15:11">Josh. 15:11</ref>).

3995.b: Israelite sanctuary and assembly point during the judges' period
3995.s: Shiloh was an important Israelite sanctuary and assembly point during the period of the judges, where the tabernacle was set up and the land was allotted to the tribes (<ref="Josh. 18:1, 8-10; 1Sam. 1:3, 9, 24; 2:14; 3:21; Jer. 7:12, 14">Josh. 18:1, 8-10; 1Sam. 1:3, 9, 24; 2:14; 3:21; Jer. 7:12, 14</ref>).

3996.b: Canaanite city conquered by Joshua, allotted to Zebulun
3996.s: Shimron, also called Shimron-meron, was a Canaanite city conquered by Joshua (<ref="Josh. 11:1; 12:20">Josh. 11:1; 12:20</ref>) and later allotted to the tribe of Zebulun (<ref="Josh. 19:15">Josh. 19:15</ref>).

3997.b: Ancient region in Mesopotamia, associated with Babylon
3997.s: Shinar was an ancient region in Mesopotamia, associated with the cities of Babylon and Uruk, and the site of the Tower of Babel (<ref="Gen. 10:10; 11:2; 14:1, 9; Josh. 7:21; Isa. 11:11; Dan. 1:2; Zech. 5:11">Gen. 10:10; 11:2; 14:1, 9; Josh. 7:21; Isa. 11:11; Dan. 1:2; Zech. 5:11</ref>).

3998.b: Town in the territory of Issachar
3998.s: Shion was a town allotted to the tribe of Issachar, mentioned along with Shunem, Hapharaim, and Anaharath (<ref="Josh. 19:19">Josh. 19:19</ref>).

3999.b: The last Israelite campsite before crossing the Jordan.
3999.s: Shittim, also called Abel-shittim, the final Israelite encampment before entering Canaan.

4000.s: The Shittim Valley is mentioned in Joel's prophecy as a place where water will flow when God restores Judah's fortunes (<ref="Jol.3.18">Jol.3.18</ref>).

4001.b: People group mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
4001.s: Shoa was a people group mentioned along with the Babylonians, Chaldeans, and Assyrians in Ezekiel's prophecy against Jerusalem (<ref="Ezek. 23:23">Ezek. 23:23</ref>).

4002.b: Region raided by Philistines during Saul's reign
4002.s: Shual was a region raided by Philistine raiders during Saul's reign, along with Ophrah and the land of Shaalim (<ref="1Sam. 13:17">1Sam. 13:17</ref>).

4003.b: Town in Issachar; home of the Shunammite woman
4003.s: Shunem was a town allotted to the tribe of Issachar (<ref="Josh. 19:18">Josh. 19:18</ref>), known for being the home of the Shunammite woman who hosted Elisha (<ref="2Ki. 4:8">2Ki. 4:8</ref>) and where the Philistines camped before battling Saul (<ref="1Sam. 28:4">1Sam. 28:4</ref>).

4004.b: Wilderness area between Canaan and Egypt
4004.s: Shur was a wilderness area between Canaan and Egypt, mentioned in connection with Hagar (<ref="Gen. 16:7">Gen. 16:7</ref>), Abraham (<ref="Gen. 20:1; 25:18">Gen. 20:1; 25:18</ref>), the Israelites' wanderings (<ref="Exod. 15:22">Exod. 15:22</ref>), and Saul's battles (<ref="1Sam. 15:7; 27:8">1Sam. 15:7; 27:8</ref>).

4005.b: Moabite town known for its vineyards
4005.s: Sibmah was a Moabite town known for its vineyards, allotted to the tribe of Reuben (<ref="Num. 32:38; Josh. 13:19">Num. 32:38; Josh. 13:19</ref>) and later mentioned in prophecies concerning Moab (<ref="Isa. 16:8-9; Jer. 48:32">Isa. 16:8-9; Jer. 48:32</ref>).

4006.b: Landmark on the northeastern border of the Promised Land
4006.s: Sibraim was a place mentioned by Ezekiel as a landmark on the northeastern border of the Promised Land, between the territory of Damascus and that of Hamath (<ref="Ezek. 47:16">Ezek. 47:16</ref>).

4007.b: Valley near the Dead Sea; site of battle
4007.s: The Valley of Siddim, located near the Dead Sea, was the site of a battle between the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah and the kings of Elam and their allies (<ref="Gen. 14:3, 8, 10">Gen. 14:3, 8, 10</ref>).

4008.s: Sidon, also called Great Sidon, was a prominent Phoenician city known for its trade and culture, and was the hometown of Jezebel, wife of King Ahab (<ref="1Ki. 16:31">1Ki. 16:31</ref>). It is mentioned in various contexts throughout the Bible, including the Old Testament (<ref="Gen. 10:19; Josh. 11:8; Judg. 10:6; Isa. 23:2-4; Jer. 27:3; Ezek. 28:21-22">Gen. 10:19; Josh. 11:8; Judg. 10:6; Isa. 23:2-4; Jer. 27:3; Ezek. 28:21-22</ref>) and the New Testament (<ref="Matt. 11:21-22; Luke 4:26; Act.27.3">Matt. 11:21-22; Luke 4:26; Act.27.3</ref>).

4009.b: Place where King Joash was assassinated
4009.s: Silla was the place where King Joash of Judah was assassinated by his servants (<ref="2Ki. 12:20">2Ki. 12:20</ref>).

4010.b: Wilderness area between Elim and Sinai
4010.s: Sin was a wilderness area between Elim and Sinai where the Israelites camped during their journey from Egypt to the Promised Land (<ref="Exod. 16:1; 17:1; Num. 33:11-12">Exod. 16:1; 17:1; Num. 33:11-12</ref>).

4011.b: Mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments
4011.s: Sinai, also called Mount Sinai, Horeb, or Mount Horeb, was the mountain where God gave Moses the Ten Commandments and other laws (<ref="Exod. 19-40; Lev. 7:38; 25:1; 26:46; 27:34; Num. 3:1; 28:6; Deut. 33:2; Judg. 5:5; Ps. 68:8, 17; Neh. 9:13; Mal. 4:4; Act.7.30, 38; Gal. 4:24-25">Exod. 19-40; Lev. 7:38; 25:1; 26:46; 27:34; Num. 3:1; 28:6; Deut. 33:2; Judg. 5:5; Ps. 68:8, 17; Neh. 9:13; Mal. 4:4; Act.7.30, 38; Gal. 4:24-25</ref>).

4012.b: Wilderness where Israel camped after leaving Egypt
4012.s: The Sinai Wilderness was the region where the Israelites camped after the Exodus and received the Law.

4013.b: Town in southern Judah that received spoils from David
4013.s: Siphmoth was one of the towns in southern Judah that received a share of the spoils from David after he defeated the Amalekites (<ref="1Sam. 30:28">1Sam. 30:28</ref>).

4014.b: Place near Hebron where Abner was killed by Joab
4014.s: Sirah, also called the Cistern of Sirah, was a place near Hebron where Joab killed Abner in revenge for the death of his brother Asahel (<ref="2Sam. 3:26">2Sam. 3:26</ref>).

4015.b: Well dug by Isaac, disputed by Philistines
4015.s: Sitnah was a well dug by Isaac in the Valley of Gerar, but the Philistines disputed its ownership (<ref="Gen. 26:21">Gen. 26:21</ref>).

4016.b: One of the seven churches of Asia Minor
4016.s: Smyrna was one of the seven churches of Asia Minor addressed in the Book of Revelation, known for its persecution and poverty, yet faithful to Christ (<ref="Rev. 1:11; 2:8-11">Rev. 1:11; 2:8-11</ref>).

4017.b: Town in Judah; site of David's battle with Goliath
4017.s: Socoh was a town in the Shephelah region of Judah (<ref="Josh. 15:35">Josh. 15:35</ref>), known for being near the site of David's battle with Goliath (<ref="1Sam. 17:1">1Sam. 17:1</ref>) and later fortified by Rehoboam (<ref="2Chr. 11:7">2Chr. 11:7</ref>).

4018.b: A town in the hill country of Judah
4018.s: Socoh, a town allotted to the tribe of Judah in the hill country (<ref="Jos. 15:48">Jos. 15:48</ref>).

4019.b: Wicked city destroyed by God for its sins
4019.s: Sodom, a notoriously wicked city destroyed by God along with Gomorrah for their grave sins (<ref="Gen. 19:24-25">Gen. 19:24-25</ref>).

4020.b: Colonnade in Jerusalem's temple where apostles taught
4020.s: Solomon's Portico, a colonnade in the Jerusalem temple where the apostles gathered to teach (<ref="Act.3.11; 5:12">Act.3.11; 5:12</ref>).

4021.b: Valley where Delilah lived, Samson's downfall occurred
4021.s: Sorek Valley, the place where Delilah lived and where Samson's downfall began (<ref="Judg. 16:4">Judg. 16:4</ref>).

4022.b: Country Paul intended to visit to preach gospel
4022.s: Spain, a country Paul planned to visit to preach the gospel (<ref="Rom. 15:24, 28">Rom. 15:24, 28</ref>).

4023.b: Street in Damascus where Saul stayed after conversion
4023.s: Straight, a street in Damascus where Saul stayed in the house of Judas after his conversion (<ref="Act.9.11">Act.9.11</ref>).

4024.b: First Israelite campsite after leaving Egypt during Exodus
4024.s: Succoth, the first place the Israelites camped after leaving Egypt during the Exodus (<ref="Exod. 12:37; Num. 33:5">Exod. 12:37; Num. 33:5</ref>).

4025.b: City in Canaan, location of Solomon's bronze works
4025.s: Succoth, a city in Canaan allocated to the tribe of Gad, later the site of Solomon's bronze works (<ref="Gen. 33:17; Josh. 13:27; 1Kgs. 7:46">Gen. 33:17; Josh. 13:27; 1Kgs. 7:46</ref>).

4026.b: Place near where Moses spoke to Israel
4026.s: Suph, a place near the wilderness where Moses spoke to the Israelites (<ref="Deut. 1:1">Deut. 1:1</ref>).

4027.b: Place mentioned in the Book of the Wars of the Lord
4027.s: Suphah, a place mentioned in the Book of the Wars of the Lord (<ref="Num. 21:14">Num. 21:14</ref>).

4028.b: Gate of the temple in Jerusalem
4028.s: Sur, a gate of the temple in Jerusalem, possibly referring to the Foundation Gate (<ref="2Kgs. 11:6">2Kgs. 11:6</ref>).

4029.b: Capital city of the Persian Empire
4029.s: Susa, the capital city of the Persian Empire, where Esther lived and the events of her book took place (<ref="Esth. 1:2; Dan. 8:2">Esth. 1:2; Dan. 8:2</ref>).

4030.s: Sychar, a Samaritan city near Jacob's well, where Jesus spoke with a Samaritan woman (<ref="Jhn.4.5">Jhn.4.5</ref>).

4031.b: Southern border of Egypt, modern-day Aswan
4031.s: Syene, the southern border of Egypt, mentioned in prophecies about Egypt's destruction (<ref="Ezek. 29:10; 30:6">Ezek. 29:10; 30:6</ref>).

4032.b: City in Sicily where Paul's ship stopped
4032.s: Syracuse, a city on the island of Sicily where Paul's ship stopped for three days on his journey to Rome (<ref="Act.28.12">Act.28.12</ref>).

4033.b: Ancient region north of Israel, often in conflict
4033.s: Syria, an ancient region north of Israel, often engaged in conflicts with Israel and Judah (<ref="1Kgs. 20:1; 2Kgs. 13:3">1Kgs. 20:1; 2Kgs. 13:3</ref>).

4034.b: Dangerous shallow waters off the coast of Libya
4034.s: Syrtis, a dangerous area of shallow waters off the coast of Libya, feared by sailors (<ref="Act.27.17">Act.27.17</ref>).

4035.b: Canaanite city allotted to Manasseh, later a Levitical city
